strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_16: Hm. Yes, Bella, it would be most unfortunate if Digus, who has grown so wise, suddenly died...
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_17: Ha! You must invent a ritual for us, apple eater.
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_18: A ritual that will kill all our enemies at once!
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_19: Write the Necronomicon. Then we will heal you.
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_2: The village is destroyed. Half of us were taken prisoner. The rest were killed.
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_3: We already know, my friend. Go now. Rest, and feed your family.
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_4: What?! Go grab your swords and fight! We must take revenge, Bella!
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_5: My dear Clotho, what's the point of that... Look!
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_6: Dad's been badly wounded! Someone, help him!
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_7: Horadric! Ha! What a pleasant surprise!
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_8: But before I tear out your eyes and tongue, tell me: why did you do it?!
strings.dlc_scene_12_rep_9: Because of Chain. I love her, but the Ancient God forbids...
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_1: I take it you killed the guards on the upper floors, Horadric? Impressive.
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_10: Oh hi birdie! Honey, what did they do to you?!
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_12: It's over, my love! You're free. Here, take my hand.
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_13: Remember my promise? We're together at last. We can be happy!
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_15: Yeah, yeah, I know everything went to hell, and it's all my fault, but...
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_16: In the end, our love is what's really important!
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_18: The whole world is ruined! Tell me, is it right for such love to exist?
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_19: Forgive me, my dear... But I... I can't...
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_2: Guys, go get some beer. For the four of us.
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_3: You'll have to cut off my legs, Krezvold. Or I will march on.
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_4: You don't understand. You think Jove and Lucius don't know who saved Digus?
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_5: If you rescue Chain, they'll declare you a traitor and a heretic!
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_6: Brother, let's sit together, have a beer, and talk it over... Just like old times!
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_7: It will never be like old times, Krezvold.
strings.dlc_scene_13_rep_8: Brother... my brother would have helped me rescue Chain.
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_1: My subjects! We've fought for many long years. And... and...
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_10: I... Hm... It's... too complicated! I'll describe it in a special Holy Book!
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_11: So let's destroy the bridge! Who among us is courageous enough?
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_12: I repeat — who? Whose faith is strong enough?
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_14: Then look upon me, the New God!
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_15: I sacrifice this final symbol of the Old Faith!
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_2: Citizens, nobody's seen a piece of paper with some writing? No?
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_3: So there you have it. The pagans and their Ancient God are no more!
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_4: Let their remnants lurk among the swamps...
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_5: The war is over! I, king Jove, thank you all. You're free!
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_6: Wait! There's one last thing: we must destroy the Ancient Bridge!
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_7: Er... Pontiff Lucius, but then how will we be able to go to the Land of Dead?
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_8: We don't need to! Our way now leads to the sky realm of the New God!
strings.dlc_scene_14_rep_9: Okay. Could you describe that process... er... technically?
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_10: Thank God... I'll warm up at least... This apartment... it's a little cold down here, Lucius...
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_11: Cool! In any case, I have my offer for you.
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_12: Rather than throwing you in the fire, I'll let you be Bishop, and give you anything you could want!
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_13: Just answer one question: where's their swamp camp?!
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_14: I'd rather become... barbecue... than be your bishop, Lucius.
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_15: So I see. We'll see if your sense of humor helps you tomorrow, Horadric.
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_16: I'm so sorry I didn't come earlier. They wouldn't let me.
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_17: I heard you came to them and gave yourself up. But why?!
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_18: A good soldier follows orders, so don't let it trouble you. What's new, Krezvold?
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_19: Repression, trials, executions... It's the same thing every day.
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_20: The people are scared. Some have even left the Town.
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_21: And... hmm... the walking dead have appeared around our cemeteries.
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_22: Ha, ha... what a glorious new world... that we helped to build!
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_23: Horadric, I... What the hell, I don't want to see you burning on the bonfire!
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_24: Then you'll just have to close your eyes, Krezvold.
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_6: Ouch! That hurts! Do it again.
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_8: Today is your final torture session.
strings.dlc_scene_15_rep_9: King Jove ordered you burned as a heretic.
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_1: ...And finally, concerning the invasion of the walking dead!
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_10: Heresy! The Master came down to us from the sky, in answer to our prayers!
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_11: I grow tired. Burn him and let's go home.
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_12: Wait, Horadric's right! The Master appeared from the Portal. I saw it myself!
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_14: Also, the Master rejected all religion. How could he become a God?
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_16: Lucius, your face looks so funny when you yell...
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_2: I, king Jove, hereby forbid everyone from speaking or thinking that it could be because we destroyed the Ancient Bridge!
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_20: Horadric, stop twitching! I'll cut off your arm instead of the rope!
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_22: Ha, as usual. I rescue him from the fire, and still he's not satisfied.
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_24: So, are we gonna run, or wait around for them to get sight back?
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_3: I decree that you believe: it's the New God's wrath, because the pagans still live!
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_6: Traitor, be a good fellow and repent before you die.
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_7: Well... Yes, I do deserve death! I'm a traitor indeed!
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_8: I couldn't be with my beloved because of the Ancient God...
strings.dlc_scene_16_rep_9: And then I helped summon the Master from the Portal!
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_1: Clotho, sister, let's go home. We'll talk, and then we'll get you a sedative...
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_10: She's right, Ancient God. I switched the ritual so I might speak to you!
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_11: Listen to me. You’re our last hope.
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_12: The Ancient Bridge is destroyed. Our dead remain here as zombies.
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_13: They're killing people. And nobody can stop the madness.
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_14: This no longer concerns me, mortal.
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_15: Really? Soon there won't be anybody left to pray to you. And then you'll vanish!
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_16: You already grow weak. Otherwise you could have resisted my ritual.
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_2: We've betrayed our God, Bella, and must be punished! All of us!
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_3: Clotho, killing a thousand people at once is a bad idea!
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_4: It sure is! That's why I'll read the spell three times, so we'll kill three thousand at once!
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_5: Everything is ready. Time for the Necronomicon.
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_6: What?! My Lord?! Did I misread the page?!
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_7: My former priestess, how dare you trouble me?!
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_8: I... no... it wasn't me... I'd never...
strings.dlc_scene_17_rep_9: Arr! Digus tricked me! This ritual was to supposed to kill our foes!
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_1: The Contract is ready. When you sign it, this world will be bound by it.
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_10: And the Ships of the Dead, not Walking dead.
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_11: The guarantor of the Contract is the Graveyard Keeper.
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_12: All signers are immortal as long as the Contract is valid.
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_13: And the last one! The truly guilty men will be punished.
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_14: Their lost souls will be bound to their dying flesh forever!
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_15: Oh, I don't envy those "truly guilty men"...
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_16: And you'll have to rebuild the village again. But remember about fire safety!
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_17: Father, you make it sound like you're leaving...
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_18: Religious conflicts, bloodthirsty priestesses, and red-eyed gods are too much at my age...
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_19: Plus... there's still so many sweets I must try!
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_2: If the Contract is violated, the Ancient Curse will return.
strings.dlc_scene_18_rep_7: Oops, sorry, he's mute. Freedom, not Prisons.
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_1: The first Keeper is about to arrive, but we're running out of marble, the beams are wobbly...
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_11: The stone Krezvold used to blind guards during the execution...
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_12: It was your magic stone! You rescued me.
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_13: Sorry, Horadric, I really need to go.
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_15: We've done too many terrible things...
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_17: Maybe we can try to fix what can be fixed... together?
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_2: ... half of the brigade is off drinking, and Krezvold hasn't delivered the nails. Not a good start...
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_4: Er... I’m sorry to trouble you, Horadric, but...
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_5: Bella and I... could we settle beside the Village?
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_7: Clotho is... she's ill. Mentally ill. She'd better stay away in the swamp.
strings.dlc_scene_19_rep_9: Chain, wait a minute! Please. I haven't thanked you.
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_1: Are you playing hide-and-seek, my red-haired birdie?
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_10: And he chose me to serve Him.
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_11: So it's all for nothing. We can never be together...
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_12: Ah, but my dear Chain, I entirely disagree with...
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_16: My sisters and I...we can see future. And... I saw no future for us.
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_17: Well... that just means you're not looking closely enough. We'll be together! I swear it!
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_19: Even the Ancient God won't stop me!
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_2: I am here. But I grow tired of birds, and rabbits, and frogs...
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_3: Oh, I get it, you want to be my kitty! Grr!
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_4: Kitty! Horrie dear, you know what I mean.
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_5: Well, yes. Just tell me which animal you prefer, and I'll...
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_6: Oh, my God... Do you not know that I'm a priestess of the Ancient God?
strings.dlc_scene_1_rep_8: And he chooses a destiny for each of us.
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_12: On the count of "three", you'll forget everything.
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_15: Calm down. You've merely turned a page in your life.
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_16: A whole new chapter awaits you ahead.
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_17: But I need to go home! Can I go home?
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_18: There is always a way to get home...
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_19: Hm... Let me see. Your new home is a graveyard.
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_2: Calm down. You've merely turned a page in your life.
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_21: It means you're a <Graveyard Keeper> now!
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_3: A whole new chapter awaits you ahead.
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_4: Two chapters, actually. Let's sort the wheat from the chaff.
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_6: Merely a safeguard against possible failure.
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_7: What the hell? Tell me right now — who are you?! And what's going on here?!
strings.dlc_scene_20_rep_8: Well... See if you can figure it out, my overly aggressive friend.
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_1: What a lovely day it is today!
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_10: Anyway, we've quite run out of food.
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_11: You are a decent man, my friend. The Ancient God blesses... Ah!
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_12: She fainted dead away! Chain, help me! Clotho! Clotho!
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_13: I'm okay, Bella. The Ancient God has sent me a vision!
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_15: Excuse me, but what about me?
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_16: Go home, and you'll get some bread, salt, and black caviar... Next!
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_17: Excuse me, I just need to ask one teeny-tiny question...
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_2: How long have you been here?
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_20: The Ancient God forbids cutting in line!
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_5: Great priestess Clotho, I bear a humble request for the Ancient God. I...
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_6: Be quick, man. There's a line!
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_7: Our God teaches that through prayer, you can achieve everything you could want.
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_8: So we did nothing for three months straight, and just prayed. And...
strings.dlc_scene_2_rep_9: Argh! Oh Ancient God, I beg you! Why must they be so chatty?!
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_1: Rest in peace, our deceased friend!
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_10: Sorry, the Ancient God forbids me from giving them to anyone. Perhaps a sweet cupcake would suffice?
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_11: I had a vision, Digus! He wants us to use the Portal!
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_12: Don't shout, Clotho. It's not healthy for people who are a thousand years old.
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_13: Listen, aren't you afraid for Horadric, your adopted son?
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_14: I'm afraid that's why I can't give you the keys. The Portal is unpredictable and dangerous.
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_15: You have a cupcake instead of a brain, you old fool!
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_2: Your road now leads over the Ancient Bridge and into the Land of the Dead!
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_3: Let's go divide up the inheritance!
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_4: It's so annoying when they die on the weekend!
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_5: Clotho, what a surprise! Tea? Coffee? A little mead with pepper?
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_6: No, no, once was enough. Digus, our God has sent me a vision.
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_7: I saw fire, blood-stained blades, and corpses. Oh, and the Ancient Portal!
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_8: A vision? Oh, oh, oh! I warned you, your experiments with mushrooms could be...
strings.dlc_scene_3_rep_9: I need the keys to the Portal, funny man. Right now.
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_10: We don't need him, Horadric! We can provide food and water for ourselves! Am I right, Lucius?
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_11: Sure. And I want to pick my own woman! Have you seen the cow He chose for me?!
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_12: We'd never manage it anyway. Digus will never give us the keys to the Portal.
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_13: True. You'll just have to steal them.
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_14: Rob my father? Krezvold, how can we...
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_15: Well... Hm... He's only your adopted father, so...
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_16: Okay, we'll do everything without you. Pfft, you promised Chain that you would be together, and...
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_17: I... but... ok, Jove, you win. I'm in.
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_2: Cool, Krezvold. Horadric, what about you?
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_3: I'm not sure, Jove. This case — it smells bad.
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_4: The chamber pots we empty for the priests smell bad, man!
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_5: Aren't you ashamed of yourself? You're a tough warrior!
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_6: But you just stand like a statue and drive away the priestesses' drunken fans!
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_7: That's it! I've already forgotten where to put a helmet on!
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_8: But it's the Ancient God's will, Jove...
strings.dlc_scene_4_rep_9: Then let our strong-willed Ancient God empty his priests' chamber pots himself!
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_1: Chin up, buddy! We didn't even have to twist his arms!
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_10: We want to get rid of the Ancient God, his laws, and prayers and all the other stuff.
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_11: Besides, we want to learn how to build houses, sew clothes, grow food.
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_12: And... also give us the power to make others to do it for us!
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_15: What? Who the hell are you?
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_16: I'm the one who possesses the knowledge to awaken and transform your minds.
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_17: I will grant you the skills to make your hands strong and productive.
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_19: Well, guys, that's an epic fail.
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_4: Correct. Lucius, you have the keys? All six of them?
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_5: Oh yes! Horadric came through like a professional!
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_6: He tied up his father, and tossed the whole house! Am I right, bro?
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_7: Jove is waiting for us. Let's get on with it.
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_8: Where have you been, Lucius? Two legionnaires couldn't handle a feeble old man?
strings.dlc_scene_6_rep_9: Let's begin! Listen to our words, Portal!
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_1: And, finally, why doesn't the sky fall down onto the earth?!
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_10: I decided to serve the Master, Horadric. That's enough.
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_13: You're too late! They're not yours anymore!
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_14: Certainly, Digus. And they're not yours either. They belong to themselves.
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_15: People, the Ancient God gave us the sun and moon!
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_16: That's just molecules. The same molecules make each of us — and even the Ancient God.
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_17: The Ancient God forgives us of our sins!
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_18: Religion itself is the origin of sin.
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_19: Our God lets you not work on weekends!
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_2: It's thanks to the Ancient God!
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_20: Good. But why work at all? We could approve...
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_27: Forgive them, Ancient God. They know not what they do...
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_3: And your Master cannot even bring the mildest rain!
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_5: The Master doesn't even heal blind men!
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_7: Comb your hair, put on guilty faces, and follow me!
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_8: What do you think about that, Krezvold?
strings.dlc_scene_7_rep_9: A good soldier doesn't think. A good soldier does his duty.
strings.dlc_scene_8_rep_1: Rest in peace, our deceased friend!
strings.dlc_scene_8_rep_10: Digus, why are you going on about that stuff!? We're talking about ideas!
strings.dlc_scene_8_rep_11: The Master taught us everything! And now we will build a brave new world!
strings.dlc_scene_8_rep_12: Oh, dear... A new world... Krezvold, try to get the water back on at least!
strings.dlc_scene_8_rep_13: I know you're all just mocking me! Chain refuses to talk to me. You too, Dad...
strings.dlc_scene_8_rep_14: I am your father no longer, Horadric.
strings.dlc_scene_8_rep_2: Your road now leads over the Ancient Bridge and into the Land of the Dead!
strings.dlc_scene_8_rep_5: Dad, I know you're mad at me, but..... how about we take a closer look at the situation?
strings.dlc_scene_8_rep_7: Let's take a closer look for example at the aqueduct. The water! Where's the water?
strings.dlc_scene_8_rep_9: Our God has abandoned us. No water, no food... Nothing...
strings.dlc_scene_9_rep_1: Jove, are you sure it's... the right time?
strings.dlc_scene_9_rep_10: The time is now. Do you know what awaits?
strings.dlc_scene_9_rep_11: I know everything that has happened and will happen.
strings.dlc_scene_9_rep_2: Yes, Lucius. The whole Town is his domain. His work is done. We don't need him more.
strings.dlc_scene_9_rep_3: Hm, our poor Master is running late...
strings.dlc_scene_9_rep_4: He must have found out. And he'll come here with guards!
strings.dlc_scene_9_rep_5: Our merciful Master will come to arrest us? Meh, what nonsense!
strings.dlc_scene_9_rep_6: What if he doesn't come at all?!
strings.dlc_scene_9_rep_7: Oh, he'll come. He must do everything that we asked the Portal for.
strings.dlc_scene_9_rep_8: Have you forgotten? We asked it for the power to rule the people!
strings.donkey_1_1: Got a fresh corpse from <The Town>!
strings.donkey_1_10: This situation is deeply humiliating. You know where I'm coming from, right comrade?
strings.donkey_1_11: The bastard pretends that he doesn't understand anything I'm saying!
strings.donkey_1_12: Anyway I need go back to <The Town>. You get rid of this one, and I'll bring you a new one.
strings.donkey_1_13: What a strange land this is...
strings.donkey_1_8: I'm cheap labor. This cart isn't mine. So I have to work for the capitalist bastard who owns it!
strings.donkey_1_9: And I only earn 5 carrots a day!
strings.donkey_lock_wool_d: Smells of sweat, carrots, and communism.
strings.donkey_oil_1: Great. Finally I'll get a little peace and quiet. And I'll be able to think about my theories! And ways to fight for what's right!
strings.donkey_oil_2: I already have all the wharf rats on my side!
strings.donkey_plague_2: Nobody pays me extra to carry these plague corpses!
strings.donkey_plague_3: Can you imagine? There are dead corpses in the river that goes through <The Town>!
strings.donkey_plague_4: Who can be dumb enough to throw dead bodies into the river...
strings.donkey_plague_5: They have no respect for their dead in <The Town>...
strings.donkey_plague_6: They're afraid to visit their graves...
strings.donkey_reach_1: Good news — I work for myself now! I bought this cart.
strings.donkey_reach_2: As soon as I got a little money, everyone started to understand me! It's a miracle...
strings.donkey_reach_4: So you're a capitalist now too.
strings.donkey_reach_5: No I'm not. I am still just a modest proletarian.
strings.donkey_reach_6: I don't get how that works.
strings.donkey_reach_7: You'll never understand the working class. Adios.
strings.donkey_starving_2: My 5 <carrots> would be worth a fortune there!
strings.donkey_starving_3: It's against my principles to get involved in speculating on the markets.
strings.donkey_starving_4: But somebody needs to help the proletariat!
strings.donkey_strike_10: Second, I need a day off. — So no more corpses on (d6)!
strings.donkey_strike_11: And last but not least! I need better pay. From you!
strings.donkey_strike_13: These corpses aren't your property. They're like a natural resource. And I want my cut!
strings.donkey_strike_14: Each new corpse will cost you 5 <carrots>! In advance!
strings.donkey_strike_15: You can place them in a special box here. I'll take the <carrots> from it.
strings.donkey_strike_16: If you refuse, then you can find yourself another donkey... Oh, and there isn't another donkey! Ha ha!
strings.donkey_strike_7: It means I'm tired of being oppressed! And I'm not bringing you any more corpses!
strings.donkey_strike_8: At least — not for free! I have a list of demands.
strings.donkey_strike_9: First, I demand better working conditions! Grease the wheels for a change. I can't keep listening to the squeak!
strings.donkey_strike_done_1: Good! Now just put my carrots in the box.
strings.donkey_strike_done_2: See? That wasn't so hard! Ha ha! But this is only the beginning!
strings.donkey_strike_done_3: Do you really need to do that here?
strings.donkey_strike_done_4: Yes I do! And what right do you have to complain? This isn't your road, anyway! Enjoy my manifest!
strings.donkey_strike_done_5: I used to think you were a nice donkey...
strings.donkey_strike_done_6: I am! But not for you!
strings.donkey_talk_1: It looks like you're doing all right here.
strings.donkey_talk_2: Yes, I just opened the Church.
strings.donkey_talk_3: So now you own everything here?
strings.donkey_talk_5: Congratulations! You're a lucky man. You've acquired all this capital... Your work for yourself...
strings.donkey_talk_6: You're a true capitalist now! But this world has no such reward for a hard working donkey like me!
strings.donkey_talk_7: Even you are benefitting from my cheap labor... I fear I cannot call you comrade any longer.
strings.donkey_talk_8: But I won't just lie down and take it! Here's a little present, just for you!
strings.donkey_war_1: I hate having to work overtime!
strings.donkey_war_2: They used to eat until they burst, and buy everything they wanted.
strings.donkey_war_3: But food has become so expensive. — So now they feel my pain!
strings.donkey_war_4: Recently they decided to have a riot over the food shortage...
strings.donkey_war_5: And of course it's up to the donkey to clean up all the mess...
strings.dungeon_kill_all: Need to kill all enemies first.
strings.embalm_50_d: This embalming fluid reduces body's decay by 50%.
strings.embalm_already_applied: You can't embalm a body with the same liquid twice.
strings.embalm_not_enough: You can't apply this liquid because the body doesn't have enough %1.
strings.embalm_stop_d: This embalming fluid halts the body's decay.
strings.engineer_tp_1: The door is closed until I have (happy)80 with <Engineer>.
strings.exhume_confirmation: To exhume a body you need to have:
strings.exhume_confirmation_bot: Are you sure you want to exhume the body?
strings.exit_menu_confirm_txt: All unsaved progress will be lost.
strings.farmer_1_1: Whatever you're selling, I'm not buying. Even if it's drugs, or magic elixirs!
strings.farmer_1_2: I'm just looking around. I don't know what's happening, but everyone is telling me that I'm a graveyard keeper.
strings.farmer_1_3: Oh. Then you're even worse than those shifty travelling merchants.
strings.farmer_1_4: I must say, your whole profession is a fraud. And I don't like you!
strings.farmer_1_5: Now that I've made my position clear, we can do business.
strings.farmer_alisa_1: I'm here to ask your permission to let your daughter go to <The Town> with Ms Charm.
strings.farmer_alisa_2: It's a great opportunity for her!
strings.farmer_alisa_3: I need her here! We have a lot of work to do on the farm. Besides that, I don't trust this actress.
strings.farmer_alisa_4: She already spent too much time helping out at the tavern! I don't like it!
strings.farmer_alisa_done: I hear the <Mill> is fixed. That's good for business.
strings.farmer_alisa_done_1: And <Alisa> really does want to go. I love my daughter!
strings.farmer_alisa_done_2: I want what's best for her!
strings.farmer_farm_2: Is there anything special I need know to be a good farmer?
strings.farmer_farm_3: You need to know how to fertilize the soil. And be ready to work hard!
strings.farmer_farm_4: Honestly you don't look much like a farmer.
strings.farmer_farm_5: You're better off buying from a professional like me!
strings.farmer_farm_6: Even somebody like you could cook something nice with my vegetables!
strings.farmer_son_1: I need to finish my chores or father will be terrifyingly angry.
strings.farmer_tp_1: The door is closed until I have (happy)40 with the <Farmer>.
strings.farmerson_alisa_4: Mmm... I like when she plays.
strings.farmerson_alisa_6: If you help my uncle to fix the <Mill>...
strings.farmerson_alisa_7: Then father will be so happy! I'll ask about <Alisa>, and I bet he'll let her go.
strings.farmerson_alisa_8: Thank you! I'll talk to your uncle.
strings.first_death_2: It seems like I'm alive and back home.
strings.first_death_3: Under the circumstances I'm not sure that's good news...
strings.fishing_something_wrong: I'm not going to catch anything like this
strings.fishing_spot_info:
This is a fishing spot like others you can find in the 
<Village>, <River>, <Swamp> and <Sea>.
strings.frog_1: Pardon me. Would you be so kind as to bring me back to Aunt Clotho?
strings.frog_2: A talking frog... Ok. I'm not even surprised...
strings.frog_3: Sure, I'll bring you to Clotho.
strings.game_of_crone_popup_window:
Thank you for purchasing the “Game of Crone" DLC!
We hope you enjoy the new story — and your refugee camp!
The additional content will become available when you wake up and meet an unexpected guest in your house.
strings.garden_broken:
<The Garden.>
Property in forfeiture!
For commercial use contact the tavern owner <Horadric>.
strings.garlic_bunch_d: Effective against vampires... and friends alike.
strings.gerry_about_machine_2: I figured it out! Just buy some land and build a <tavern>!
strings.gerry_about_machine_3: A <Tavern>? Hmm. Why not a ten-story palace?
strings.gerry_about_machine_4: The <tavern> will be a cover, dummy!
strings.gerry_about_machine_5: We'll dig out the cellar and use the <machine>!
strings.gerry_about_machine_6: Plus, you even stand a chance of making some money!
strings.gerry_about_machine_7: Knowledge from the <machine>, and money from the <tavern>!
strings.gerry_about_machine_8: And what's in it for you? Nothing? I don't believe it.
strings.gerry_about_machine_9: Well... maybe this machine will tell us something... about <my past>?
strings.gerry_after_10cs_2: You were right: I was a man!
strings.gerry_after_10cs_3: I was the <Master>! The Master who has returned to avenge himself upon those pagans!
strings.gerry_after_10cs_4: I doubt it. They said he became the <New God>.
strings.gerry_after_10cs_5: And the <Master> was kind... wise... and he didn't drink a lot.
strings.gerry_after_10cs_6: Yes, but... Okay, you're right again.
strings.gerry_after_11cs_1: Listen, that <Portal>... To activate it, we'll need to assemble seven people with six keys, right?
strings.gerry_after_11cs_2: I knew about that! I even told it to my <friend> the <Keeper>!
strings.gerry_after_11cs_3: That's strange. How could you have known about it?
strings.gerry_after_11cs_4: Good question! I wanted to help him get home, and...
strings.gerry_after_11cs_5: I can't remember anything after that.
strings.gerry_after_12cs_1: An interesting twist... By the way, you never finished your story.
strings.gerry_after_12cs_3: Well, we looked for <keys and their bearers> for 5 years.
strings.gerry_after_12cs_5: I think so. But then... I don't remember.
strings.gerry_after_13cs_1: Sad but it makes sense... Did you remember anything new?
strings.gerry_after_13cs_2: Oh yes! The <Keeper> asked the <Portal> to return him home...
strings.gerry_after_13cs_4: Holy sard! The Keeper is dead! The others! They're all dead!
strings.gerry_after_13cs_5: Maybe the Keeper didn't formulate his wish correctly. Or maybe it was something else...
strings.gerry_after_13cs_6: After all, the <man with the red eye> found me and took me away.
strings.gerry_after_14cs_1: Ha ha, that was a mistake. A bi-i-ig mistake!
strings.gerry_after_14cs_3: Oh sard... Let's watch some more.
strings.gerry_after_14cs_4: But anyway, those guys <Jove> and <Lucius> are cool!
strings.gerry_after_14cs_5: From nothing they rose up to become King and pontiff!
strings.gerry_after_15cs_1: Oh my! The <red-eyed man> held me here after the <Great Blast>!
strings.gerry_after_15cs_2: Because I told the <Keeper> something that I was forbidden to tell...
strings.gerry_after_15cs_3: And what is forbidden to tell the <Keepers>?
strings.gerry_after_15cs_4: Err... I forgot. But it doesn't matter.
strings.gerry_after_15cs_5: So... after that, he buried me. And you dug me up. The end!
strings.gerry_after_16cs_1: By the way, have you heard the story about <king Jove>... <Joe the First>?
strings.gerry_after_16cs_3: Listen! He ruled a long time. Incredibly long.
strings.gerry_after_16cs_4: So his <impatient heir> had to cut off Dad's head.
strings.gerry_after_16cs_5: But! He was greatly afraid of his Dad's resurrection.
strings.gerry_after_16cs_6: So he ordered Dad's head to be buried separately from his body! Ha ha!
strings.gerry_after_17cs_1: Do you want to keep watching?
strings.gerry_after_17cs_2: I feel like this thing is mocking me! Where am I, in these images of the past?!
strings.gerry_after_17cs_4: Maybe. Or maybe I have no past. And that grave somehow... hmm... gave birth to me!
strings.gerry_after_17cs_6: There's still hope. The list isn't complete yet.
strings.gerry_after_17cs_7: Pfff... I'm running out of patience.
strings.gerry_after_18cs_1: Damned that <red-eyed bastard>! I knew it! I knew!
strings.gerry_after_18cs_2: But I don't understand: why? WHY?
strings.gerry_after_18cs_3: Gerry, calm down! What are you...
strings.gerry_after_18cs_4: <Jove>! He became like a walking corpse because of these scum!
strings.gerry_after_18cs_5: Eternally rotting flesh... The hellish pain... It was their punishment!
strings.gerry_after_18cs_6: <Jove> couldn't even kill himself. He could only drink...
strings.gerry_after_18cs_8: Ha ha ha! What a perfect joke!
strings.gerry_after_18cs_9: <Jove's son> actually helped him when he cut off his head!
strings.gerry_after_19cs_1: Enough. Now find a big club and smash this <machine>.
strings.gerry_after_19cs_10: There aren't any more artifacts on the <list>.
strings.gerry_after_19cs_12: Well, there's one more ancient thing we could use.
strings.gerry_after_19cs_15: Hmm, I didn't know you had a...
strings.gerry_after_19cs_17: You've got to be kidding! No way! No way!
strings.gerry_after_19cs_19: There's no other way to learn the <truth>.
strings.gerry_after_19cs_2: Er... Gerry, could you at least explain one thing?
strings.gerry_after_19cs_5: But I helped people! I gave them a future! I avenged the <Master>!
strings.gerry_after_19cs_6: The <Bridge> — it was Lucius' idea! Why did they punish me?!
strings.gerry_after_19cs_8: Maybe, the <machine> will give us an answer?
strings.gerry_after_1cs_2: Look at the date! That was 210 years ago!
strings.gerry_after_1cs_3: How could we have seen <Horadric> and <Chain> there?
strings.gerry_after_1cs_4: Yeah, they must be a little older than they look!
strings.gerry_after_1cs_5: Maybe they use cosmetics and live a healthy lifestyle?
strings.gerry_after_1cs_6: By the way, you can watch scenes more than once.
strings.gerry_after_2cs_1: <Clotho>?! But Clotho is our crazy witch from the swamps!
strings.gerry_after_2cs_2: The past 200 years have been rough on the old sard!
strings.gerry_after_2cs_3: Hmm... but where are <you> in all this?
strings.gerry_after_3cs_1: Umm... I remember that place. That's where the <Keeper> dug me up!
strings.gerry_after_3cs_2: He was looking for spare bones for his <zombies>.
strings.gerry_after_3cs_3: I woke up, and I couldn't remember anything... but I wanted beer!
strings.gerry_after_4cs_1: Listen, that <Jove> — he's a cool guy!
strings.gerry_after_4cs_2: He knows what he wants. Not like these other wusses.
strings.gerry_after_4cs_4: By the way, I didn't see <you> there this time either.
strings.gerry_after_4cs_6: Do we think we can get a wig and some glue?
strings.gerry_after_4cs_7: I prefer you bald. Let's continue.
strings.gerry_after_6cs_1: That Keeper constructed his <machine> on this <Hill>.
strings.gerry_after_6cs_2: It seems like he was really smart.
strings.gerry_after_6cs_3: He was a genius! You know I even feel a little sorry for him.
strings.gerry_after_6cs_4: Just imagine, he used the machine on his <final day of service>...
strings.gerry_after_6cs_6: And the results are right in front of you!
strings.gerry_after_6cs_7: Very sad... Time to move on?
strings.gerry_after_7cs_1: I'm starting to worry. Where am <I> in the past?
strings.gerry_after_7cs_2: Listen. Maybe you... weren't always a skull?
strings.gerry_after_7cs_3: Ok, then what was I? A rib? A femur?
strings.gerry_after_7cs_4: You were probably a man or a woman.
strings.gerry_after_7cs_5: A woman? Mmm, in that case, I hope I had a titillating figure!
strings.gerry_after_8cs_1: Boy do I need a drink. Wait... Where's my <cognac>?
strings.gerry_after_8cs_3: Pff! The <last Keeper> was my <real friend>. He always had something to drink!
strings.gerry_after_8cs_4: What drinking parties we used to have!
strings.gerry_after_8cs_5: And he often spoke of his family?
strings.gerry_after_8cs_6: Well... to tell you the truth. — He longed for them every day.
strings.gerry_after_9cs_10: Don't you think that's a strange question to be asking a skull?
strings.gerry_after_9cs_11: By the way, I remembered something interesting.
strings.gerry_after_9cs_12: After the war, Lucius and I stole part of royal treasure and buried it somewhere nearby.
strings.gerry_after_9cs_14: Well... then we definitely need to check it out!
strings.gerry_after_9cs_2: Holy sard! Not remembering was such a great gift!
strings.gerry_after_chest_1: Oh my... look at all this gold. And... And...
strings.gerry_after_chest_10: See you in the old cellar. Oh, life is so wonderful!
strings.gerry_after_chest_4: Thanks to all the gods — Ancient and New!
strings.gerry_after_chest_5: All my sufferings have been rewarded!
strings.gerry_after_chest_6: 200 years old?! Huh... can I taste it?
strings.gerry_after_chest_7: Of course no! It belongs to King Jove! And that's me — so it belongs to me!
strings.gerry_after_chest_8: But I'll graciously allow you to take the gold.
strings.gerry_before_10cs_2: That <Logger> is an eccentric guy, wouldn't you say?
strings.gerry_before_10cs_3: Well, he's much more normal than <Beekeeper>.
strings.gerry_before_11cs_2: They're just <shards of clay>. They must have been easy to get, right?
strings.gerry_before_11cs_3: You know what? I don't care to discuss it.
strings.gerry_before_12cs_2: I heard you organized a <rat race>. That's great!
strings.gerry_before_12cs_3: Maybe it'll inspire the <cultists> to drown more <inquisitors>... Hmm.
strings.gerry_before_13cs_2: Hm, it'll be interesting to see who these <shackles> belonged to...
strings.gerry_before_13cs_3: To one of the numberless victims of the <New Faith>?
strings.gerry_before_14cs_2: Do you have any idea what I had to do to get this <pickaxe>?
strings.gerry_before_14cs_4: I'm so tired. So very tired.
strings.gerry_before_15cs_2: Hm, you smell like <honey>! You having a nice rest?
strings.gerry_before_15cs_3: Very nearly. I almost ate Dig's <poisoned cake>.
strings.gerry_before_15cs_4: Oh, he's crazy. Don't pay any attention to him!
strings.gerry_before_16cs_1after_wrong: Nope, that doesn't work. You dig up anything else?
strings.gerry_before_18cs_2: Rat races... The whole <Village> has gone crazy over them!
strings.gerry_before_18cs_3: It's too bad nobody takes bets from talking skulls...
strings.gerry_before_1cs_2: I got the <statuette>. Strange, it looks familiar...
strings.gerry_before_1cs_3: Ha, it's that <man with the red eye>!
strings.gerry_before_1cs_5: Put it right there, under the screen with the buttons.
strings.gerry_before_1cs_6: Gently... Gently... Ready! Ok! Push the lever!
strings.gerry_before_2cs_2: Oh, there's still some wine in it... Mmm, it's semi-sweet!
strings.gerry_before_2cs_3: Tasty, but there's not enough. Now we just shove it in there...
strings.gerry_before_3cs_2: Sorry, the hinge is damp and dirty...
strings.gerry_before_3cs_3: Ha, living skulls aren't afraid of a little dirt!
strings.gerry_before_4cs_3: I think you're the first person that <Farmer> ever let in.
strings.gerry_before_6cs_2: So our <Miller> is a thief? Really?
strings.gerry_before_6cs_3: Of course not. It's a... long story.
strings.gerry_before_7cs_2: Here's the <medallion>. Dig traded it for <booze>.
strings.gerry_before_7cs_3: Booze!? You should have brought it to me!
strings.gerry_before_8cs_2: Let's use this <dagger>. And let's forget how expensive it was to obtain!
strings.gerry_burn: How can I burn a body?
strings.gerry_burn_1: You know what? You're one of those guys who looks a lot smarter than they actually are.
strings.gerry_burn_5: You need fire and some wood. Ha ha...
strings.gerry_burn_6: It's a bit tricky to make the whole thing burn to ash.
strings.gerry_burn_8: Hm... you'd need a nice, quiet place. Like the place I use for my meditation.
strings.gerry_burn_9: Across the road from the mortuary entrance, near the cliff.
strings.gerry_for_10_11cs_1: Down to business... The next artifact is... er...
strings.gerry_for_10_11cs_3: And another thing... The machines reads <clay shards>! What's that about?
strings.gerry_for_10_11cs_4: <Of an ancient vase>. And <Adam> has them.
strings.gerry_for_12_13cs_1: Well, okay. Tell me about the next artifact.
strings.gerry_for_12_13cs_2: The first one is an <Amulet of the Ancient God>.
strings.gerry_for_12_13cs_3: You should ask the <Lighthouse Keeper> about it.
strings.gerry_for_12_13cs_4: Or you can go and dig up some <ancient shackles>.
strings.gerry_for_12_13cs_5: They're somewhere between the graveyard and the swamp.
strings.gerry_for_14_16cs_2: Amazing. Okay, let's get to the next artifact.
strings.gerry_for_14_16cs_3: An <ancient pickaxe>. And... it belongs to <Koukol>.
strings.gerry_for_14_16cs_4: I also see here that we need the <ancient keys> to the prison cell.
strings.gerry_for_14_16cs_5: And... they are in <Adam's home>. That right?
strings.gerry_for_14_16cs_7: Let me look. Damn! The ink ran...
strings.gerry_for_14_16cs_8: The machine says <Witch Hill>. Try to dig around there.
strings.gerry_for_17_18cs_1: An amazing story. What does the machine say?
strings.gerry_for_17_18cs_3: It belongs to the <Farmer's wife>. But she's dead, right?
strings.gerry_for_17_18cs_4: I'll try to talk to the <Farmer>. Anything else?
strings.gerry_for_17_18cs_5: Ah, yes. The <Priest's signet>. Old Dig has it.
strings.gerry_for_19cs_3: It's too hard. Let's try one last time.
strings.gerry_for_19cs_5: Yes! "<A brick from the Church>". Go, please...
strings.gerry_for_2tq_2: So... The next one is ... an <ancient wine flask>. And...
strings.gerry_for_2tq_3: <Adam> owns it. Er... Or the <Farmer's son>... or the <Miller>...
strings.gerry_for_2tq_4: Now it's just static. You'll need to check all the people I mentioned.
strings.gerry_for_2tq_5: But what should I do with the statuette? Keep it under my pillow?
strings.gerry_for_2tq_6: Why not? Or build a special case in your tavern and put it there.
strings.gerry_for_2tq_7: Lots of people go crazy for ancient junk. Some might even pay to view it!
strings.gerry_for_2tq_8: Graveyard Keeper, Garden Keeper, Tavern Keeper... And now Museum Keeper!
strings.gerry_for_3_4tq_1: Time to press onwards. The next thing is <ancient door hinge>...
strings.gerry_for_3_4tq_2: Hmm, it's in the <ground>. Somewhere between the Village and Dig's home.
strings.gerry_for_3_4tq_3: So go find it and dig it out.
strings.gerry_for_3_4tq_4: Maybe, I can search for more than one artifact at a time?
strings.gerry_for_3_4tq_5: Why not! The <Legionary Helm> is located in...
strings.gerry_for_3_4tq_8: But remember: using the artifacts in the correct order is critically important!
strings.gerry_for_6_8tq_2: Wow! It belongs to the <Miller>! What a twist!
strings.gerry_for_6_8tq_3: Well, it is a little unexpected...
strings.gerry_for_6_8tq_5: And old <Dig> can help us with it. Dig? Hmm...
strings.gerry_in_ravern_2: Where's the music maker, the gossip, the drinks?! Where's the cool <bartender>?
strings.gerry_in_ravern_3: I'm considering various candidates right now, and...
strings.gerry_in_ravern_4: Okay, you're helpless. I'll manage it instead of you.
strings.gerry_in_ravern_6: Your task is to construct a <wooden doll of a bartender> and set it here.
strings.gerry_in_ravern_6_1: Just go to your <workbench> and do it!
strings.gerry_in_ravern_7: Go, go! Save your questions for later!
strings.gerry_launch_machine_1: There must be a <button>. Push it.
strings.gerry_launch_machine_10: An artifact? This is getting complicated...
strings.gerry_launch_machine_11: There must be an itemized list of artifacts in the instructions...
strings.gerry_launch_machine_12: By the way, the wrong order of artifacts could cause an <apocalypse>.
strings.gerry_launch_machine_13: And here, he included a complete list. The old Keeper already handled most of the research.
strings.gerry_launch_machine_14: It says right here: "The first is the <Statuette of the Ancient God>".
strings.gerry_launch_machine_15: And the machine says... let's look... "The statuette's owner: <Horadric>".
strings.gerry_launch_machine_17: I'll put it more simply: take the <statuette> from Horadric and bring it here.
strings.gerry_launch_machine_18: And take care of the <corpse>. Who's the Keeper here — me or you?
strings.gerry_launch_machine_3: Don't pay any attention. It's that <inventor Keeper>.
strings.gerry_launch_machine_4: Do you know how to use this device?
strings.gerry_launch_machine_5: The old Keeper even didn't ever let me get close.
strings.gerry_launch_machine_6: There must be <instructions>... There, I see them!
strings.gerry_launch_machine_8: It works! We only need to put an <artifact> into this hole...
strings.gerry_launch_machine_9: And we'll witness a <scene from the far past>!
strings.gerry_lightning_0: Sard. What the heck was that?
strings.gerry_lightning_1: I think I was struck by lightning on my way to <The Town>.
strings.gerry_lightning_11: I talk with him all the time. I hide in a pile of... dead skulls... and we talk.
strings.gerry_lightning_12: He thinks that I'm his inner voice... So he's very open with me...
strings.gerry_lightning_13: Did he tell you anything interesting?
strings.gerry_lightning_14: As his inner voice, I find that that question most unethical.
strings.gerry_lightning_15: Ok. I'll talk with <Snake>. Maybe he'll be able to help.
strings.gerry_lightning_2: Hm. I felt it. An ancient and powerful rage... Bounce on over here immediately.
strings.gerry_lightning_3: It would seem that someone or something of great power doesn't want you in <The Town>.
strings.gerry_lightning_5: Actually I'm pretty sure that if you keep trying, things will end badly for you. Like "I'm a talking skull now too" bad.
strings.gerry_lightning_6: But I need to go there! There's some magic items I need to track down. I need to go home...
strings.gerry_lightning_7: I am a little offended that you're trying to leave me...
strings.gerry_lightning_8: But as your friend I suggest you to talk with <Snake> in the church cellar.
strings.gerry_lightning_9: I think he'll be able to find these items for you. He's quite a nimble rogue.
strings.gerry_river_0: Do you know where that river leads?
strings.gerry_river_1: The river... Somewhere down... to <The Town>, I think.
strings.gerry_river_body_0: What do you think you're doing here?
strings.gerry_river_body_1: A ghost ask me to get rid of this body.
strings.gerry_river_body_2: So what — now you're just going to do everything he asks?
strings.gerry_river_body_3: It's not like he can do anything to you. Ha ha! He's disembodied...
strings.gerry_river_body_4: Whereas I can bite you to death... while you're sleeping...
strings.gerry_river_body_5: Of course, I'd never do anything like that. Because we're friends... But you get my point, right?
strings.gerry_river_body_6: Anyway, if you ask me, the best way to get rid of a body is to burn it!
strings.gerry_tavern_ready_2: Sard it! I'd already lost hope!
strings.gerry_tavern_ready_3: I'll wait for you in the <tavern>!
strings.gerry_tavern_ready_5: My past and beer for me!
strings.gerry_tooth_d: Apparently it was once a part of Gerry's smile
strings.gerry_wrong_trigger_item: The wrong order of artifacts can cause the <apocalypse>.
strings.gerry_yorick_tavern_1: Clumsy work, but it's good enough. <Yorick>, it's your turn!
strings.gerry_yorick_tavern_2: Yorick? Are you sure it's a good idea?
strings.gerry_yorick_tavern_3: More complaints! Just think: he can work around the clock.
strings.gerry_yorick_tavern_4: He knows all the gossip and rumors.
strings.gerry_yorick_tavern_5: And he has 30 years of bartending experience.
strings.gerry_yorick_tavern_6: Before he poisoned himself with an expired cocktail.
strings.gerry_yorick_tavern_7: And most of all: he doesn't claim a salary! Who's the genius here?
strings.gerry_yorick_tavern_9: Talk to him. I'll be waiting for you in the <local cellar>.
strings.ghost_0: This is not good... Not good at all!
strings.ghost_1: Who do you think you are?!
strings.ghost_10: He can only dream of what a peaceful rest we're having...
strings.ghost_11: Who am I kidding... It's terrible here. Especially that guy down in the lower-right corner grave. He's so mean!
strings.ghost_12: Could you just get rid of him? Just dig him up and throw him in the river!
strings.ghost_13: I can even give you this license that I stole back when I was alive!
strings.ghost_15: You're such a dummy! To dig up a corpse, you need a license. The <Old Keeper> used to buy them through the <Mailbox> near the <Church>.
strings.ghost_3: Hooray! A kipper! Wow, I've been here for... Hm... how long... I'm Yorick!
strings.ghost_4: I'm so lonely... Poor, poor me... It's too bad you're here...
strings.ghost_5: Wait... No, on the contrary, I'm very glad to see you!
strings.ghost_6: But we do have a rather unpleasant fellow buried here. We'd really like to have a new neighbor instead!
strings.ghost_7: That sound like something you can help us with?
strings.ghost_8: I'm not exactly sure why I'm here, actually. Gerry only told me about burying bodies. You're Yorick and he's Gerry, funny.
strings.ghost_9: Ahhh. The half-dead skull. That jealous bastard! Ha ha!
strings.ghost_after_0: Good. It's much nicer without him at the graveyard...
strings.ghost_after_1: I'm still so sad, though. I'm so lonely. I was bad when I was alive... I should have been a better person...
strings.ghost_after_3: We're dead, but we still deserve some respect!
strings.ghost_after_4: Oh, fine, I'll tell you. Each corpse is a soul's vessel. It bears the mark of his life. Sins are (rskull) and good deeds are (skull).
strings.ghost_after_5: Even the best decorations (wr) can't make graveyard a peaceful place (wskull)... When it is full of (rskull)...\t
strings.ghost_after_6: I'm not sure, that I understand what you're talking about.
strings.ghost_after_7: I'm sure you don't! Ha ha! You better take a good care of the graveyard ! I'll be watching you...
strings.ghost_after_8: I can't do anything... I'm so sad... Boooooooo....
strings.ghost_psyco_1: Oh how nice to meet you here.
strings.ghost_psyco_2: These days I'm not often a guest in the material world.
strings.ghost_psyco_4: Are you really interested? Well then — I'll tell you.
strings.ghost_psyco_5: I was elected as superintendent of the graveyard.
strings.ghost_psyco_6: It's a tough job. Not all the new arrivals are pleasant...
strings.ghost_psyco_9: Thank you for your kind words. Now I need to return to my duties.
strings.ghost_ruin_1: I can't handle this job any more...
strings.ghost_ruin_12: Again, sorry about that. Ah, but now I feel so relieved! All the bad energy has whished away!
strings.ghost_ruin_2: This is all your fault. New guys, they are terrible...
strings.ghost_ruin_3: Hey, sorry! I really am trying my best to get rid of the (rskull).
strings.ghost_ruin_7: Oh what have I done. I so sorry...
strings.ghost_ruin_8: Just try to hang in there. I'll try to fix everything.
strings.give_blod_nails_1: Good. These nails can break the seal!
strings.graveyard2_broken:
This area is closed due to <Cultist activity>.

Please address any concerns to <The Inquisitor>.
strings.graveyard2_broken_unlocked: Finally! Now I can use the western half of the graveyard.
strings.graveyard_zone_lvlup2_d: Raise your graveyard to the next level
strings.grille_closed_think: This gate is closed. Looks like I'll need a key to open it.
strings.guard_6_1: This path leads to the <Mountain Fort>. No entry is permitted.
strings.guard_6_letin_1: I need to talk with Koukol.
strings.guard_6_letin_2: I can't let you in. But you can meet him outside the fort.
strings.guard_6_letin_3: He goes into the forest every night. To the west, not far from here.
strings.guard_6_letin_4: Nobody needs the <Mountain Fort> anymore. We all have to make a living somehow...
strings.guard_at_north_1: This gate is closed! Please, go away.
strings.guard_at_north_2: I used to be an adventurer like you, until I took an arrow in the knee...
strings.guard_burn_1: Even I'm afraid of our mighty Inquisitor. God bless that he's on our side!
strings.guard_burn_2: We'll burn all of them! Their Cult is an abomination!
strings.guard_hill_1: Hey stop sneaking around. You've been warned!
strings.guard_hill_10: Mmm... Bad cultists. They're definitely connected with witches.
strings.guard_hill_12: They're witch-cultist bastards! They want to kill our beloved King!
strings.guard_hill_13: If they win. Mmmm.... They'll put an end to the <Great Inquisition>!
strings.guard_hill_14: Yeah! And we'll lose our jobs!
strings.guard_hill_16: No, no. I'm the <Graveyard Keeper> and I'm leaving.
strings.guard_hill_17: I can't check the <Pedestal> while they're here...
strings.guard_hill_4: Then what are you doing here?
strings.guard_hill_6: Mmmm... I'm not an expert but it doesn't look like an ambush to me.
strings.guard_hill_7: Inquisitor had a bad dream about this portal and the cultists.
strings.guard_hill_8: So now we're waiting here for the cultists!
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_1: Can you tell me about your sister, Esmeralda? Where is she now?
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_2: Why are you asking? Who are you?
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_4: Hmm... You're Inquisitor's friend... You know, I'll tell you about my sister — but on one condition.
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_5: <The Inquisitor's> guards grabbed one of our friends. She's still waiting for her trial, so she might still be released.
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_6: Ask your friend, <Lord Inquisitor>, to release her. And I'll tell you everything I know.
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_7: He's not my friend... But I'll try to help.
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_again_10: We haven't spoken her real name for many years!
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_again_2: Probably she's far, far away. They put her on a <Ship of the Dead> many years ago.
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_again_3: But she had a child. Didn't she?
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_again_4: Yes. A daughter. Once she was a blessing to me, but now she is my shame.
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_again_6: Yes she's alive, But she betrayed her own people! She even betrayed the memory of her mother!
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_again_8: She sold her mother's last gift. Disowned our legacy. And for what...
strings.gypsy_esmeralda_again_9: For lust! For impertinence! In <The Town>, she's known as <Ms Charm>!
strings.gypsy_inquisitor_1: I talked to <Lord Inquisitor>. Your friend is free.
strings.gypsy_inquisitor_2: I was right! He is your friend... So you're an important man around here...
strings.gypsy_intro: If you looking for someone to read your palm, you should go to <The Town>.
strings.gypsy_intro_1: Everybody there is scrambling to earn enough to buy a scrap of bread.
strings.gypsy_recipe_3: It's great, isn't it? That's my kebab.
strings.gypsy_recipe_4: It's an old family recipe. Bring me some good fish fillets and I'll teach you.
strings.gypsy_recipe_done_2: The trick is to use a bonfire — not a stove! Fresh air is the key!
strings.gypsy_recipe_done_3: And of course, a good fish. Actually, you can use any fish. But we're talking about good kebabs! Ha ha!
strings.gypsy_recipe_done_4: Eat these kebabs and you'll be strong like me. Ha ha!
strings.gypsy_smell: Hmm. I smell something tasty and smoky...
strings.hatch_closed: The hatch is closed for now.
strings.hint_embalm: This liquid can be applied to a body on the embalming table to modify its characteristics.
strings.hint_science_decompose: Can be decomposed on the Study Table to get (sci)%1.
strings.homes_at_night_npc: It's wrong to break into other people's homes at night.
strings.horadric_1_1: Welcome to the <Dead Horse Tavern>. I am <Horadric>. How can I help you?
strings.horadric_1_2: I came from the graveyard. I woke up here today and things have been crazy since then.
strings.horadric_1_3: Oh sorry, how could I not have recognized you! Good, this is good!
strings.horadric_1_4: Things are looking bright for our small village!
strings.horadric_1_5: When are you planning on opening the <Church>?
strings.horadric_1_6a_1: There's no need to be rude. We all live here together in harmony. Just take your time and you'll see.
strings.horadric_1_6b: I need to fix the graveyard first.
strings.horadric_1_6b_1: Sure, sure. It's been a while since anybody took care of it.
strings.horadric_1_7: So let's get down to business, shall we? How can I help you?
strings.horadric_2_1a_1: The <Bishop> told me that you would buy my <Burial Certificates>.
strings.horadric_2_1a_2: Yes he's right. As the head of the village, according to the <Ancient Contract>, I have to trade it for <Money>.
strings.horadric_2_1a_3: Of course. Only if I have any <Money>.
strings.horadric_2_1a_5: <The Village> is going through hard times. We're short on <Money>.
strings.horadric_2_1a_6: But as soon as you open the church, pilgrims will bring lots of shiny coins to <the Village>!
strings.horadric_2_1c_1: Oh, Keeper. Could you kindly take this <Letter> to our local <Blacksmith Krezvold>?
strings.horadric_2_1c_2: Sure. Where can I find him?
strings.horadric_2_1c_3: The south-eastern corner of the village.
strings.horadric_2_1d_1: I found an abandoned <Garden> near the <Graveyard>. Can you tell me anything about it?
strings.horadric_2_1d_2: Oh, the <Garden>. It was seized by the <Merchant> to cover someone's debts. I can't find anybody who will make any use of it.
strings.horadric_2_1d_3: Hm... I can give you <Permission> to use the garden! Who else would agree to grow crops near the graveyard?
strings.horadric_2_1d_4b_1: You should find someone who will use it. You said that the <Garden> belonged to the <Merchant>.
strings.horadric_2_1d_4b_2: It's a bit tricky. He has the right to rent it, but everything north of the path to <The Town> is village property.
strings.horadric_2_1d_4b_3: We have a democratic community here. And I'm head of it.
strings.horadric_2_1d_5: Good. But you still need to talk to the <Merchant>. It's his property.
strings.horadric_2_1d_6: It's not exactly proper to give you permission without his approval. But it'll be fine if you just promise to settle the details with him later.
strings.horadric_2_1d_8: He comes to trade with the locals every (d4). He owns the barn just south of the tavern.
strings.horadric_2_1e_1: Could you remind me one more time what I should do with the letter?
strings.horadric_2_1e_2: Just take the latter to our local <Blacksmith Krezvold>. He lives at the south-eastern corner of the village.
strings.horadric_2_1f: Do you know how I can get back home?
strings.horadric_2_1f_1: Can you tell me where I am, because I really need to get home. My darling will be so worried.
strings.horadric_2_1f_10: And what is the name of our beloved kingdom?
strings.horadric_2_1f_11: <The Kingdom>. And it is definitely not beloved here in <The Village>...
strings.horadric_2_1f_12: Do you have any other questions?
strings.horadric_2_1f_3: Ok. It looks... medieval. Maybe I traveled through time!
strings.horadric_2_1f_4: And what year is it now?
strings.horadric_2_1f_6: The time it takes for the Earth to make one revolution around the Sun...
strings.horadric_2_1f_7: Oh you've been listening to the <Astrologer's> nonsense.
strings.horadric_2_1f_8: Everybody know that the Earth is flat.
strings.horadric_2_1f_9: But I get you. It's 200 after the <Ancient Contract> and 210 after... hmm... never mind.
strings.horadric_2_1g_2: The <Inquisitor> can grant a <Town Pass>. Or you can just purchase citizenship.
strings.horadric_2_1g_3: Let me think. Hmm — you know. There is one villager who could help you.
strings.horadric_2_1g_4: <Ms Charm>. Maybe she can help you.
strings.horadric_2_1h_1: Meat is a delicacy in our village. I'd be glad to buy it. I just need to see the <Royal Meat Stamp> on it.
strings.horadric_2_1h_10: There's this guy called <Snake>. I think he has a fake <Royal Stamp>.
strings.horadric_2_1h_11: But to be honest I haven't seen him for a while.
strings.horadric_2_1h_12: You can ask <Ms Charm>. She comes here every (d5). I bet she can help you to find <Snake>.
strings.horadric_2_1h_2: Many years ago there was an accident with an... inappropriate meat. Ever since, all meat must be approved by royal authority.
strings.horadric_2_1h_3: And I don't need any trouble with <The Town>. Does your meat have a <Stamp>?
strings.horadric_2_1h_4b_1: Good. Then this meat just needs a little preparation on your <Kitchen Table>.
strings.horadric_2_1h_4b_2: Wrap it in paper, put a stamp on it, and I'll gladly buy it!
strings.horadric_2_1h_5: I don't even want to know where you can get unauthorized meat. But wow, it really looks good!
strings.horadric_2_1h_6: But without a stamp my hands are tied.
strings.horadric_2_1h_8: Oh, you can send a form to the royal court through the <Mail Box> near your <Church>. But it'll cost you a bundle.
strings.horadric_2_1h_9: But there's another way... I'll tell you just because we're neighbors... Come closer...
strings.horadric_about_old_keeper_2: Horadric, I'd like to know more about the previous Graveyard Keepers.
strings.horadric_about_old_keeper_3: Well... the first Keeper appeared more than 200 years ago.
strings.horadric_after_slime_1: It's good you know how to use a sword. <Krezvold> told me about how you helped him.
strings.horadric_after_slime_2: Here, have a beer! It's on the house.
strings.horadric_beer_2: You are a fine brewer indeed. You know what... Go upstairs and take the scroll from my table.
strings.horadric_beer_3: It's my secret project! Honey beer! I think you just might be able to do it!
strings.horadric_land_buy_10: Don't worry, it's just a hypothetical question!
strings.horadric_land_buy_11: <Cory> and his brother <Tress>. They're the best specialists.
strings.horadric_land_buy_2: Of course! Tell me, he's in good health and high spirits?
strings.horadric_land_buy_4: Poor, poor old Dig! If only you knew...
strings.horadric_land_buy_5: No matter. The cost of the land is (slv)30.
strings.horadric_land_buy_8: By the way...  who could help me build a <tavern>?
strings.horadric_land_buy_9: What?! You intend to compete with me?! I never...
strings.horadric_land_deal_2: Of course! Let's see... taxes... fees... facilitators' services...
strings.horadric_land_deal_5: It's the law. But I can give you some free advice...
strings.horadric_land_deal_6: Buy the land in the name of a very poor and old villager.
strings.horadric_land_deal_7: You'll get plenty of benefits and discounts!
strings.horadric_recipe_1: Hm... I smell onions. They're my favorite vegetables!
strings.horadric_recipe_4: I serve onion rings and onion toast. It keeps people thirsty, so I keep selling beer.
strings.horadric_recipe_5: I think they were made for each other!
strings.horadric_recipe_6: If you like onions, I can teach how to cook a couple dishes. But remember — always eat them with a beer, ha ha!
strings.horadric_side2_1: I heard about the last witch burning. Sounds like it was quite an event!
strings.horadric_side2_2: I think it's absolutely barbaric. — But who am I to judge...
strings.horadric_side2_3: In old days, our people arranged fights to death, just for entertainment...
strings.horadric_side2_4: I don't support the burning. For me, it's just a way to sell beer.
strings.horadric_side2_5: People even told me that you serve better beer than I do here. But I don't believe them.
strings.horadric_side2_6: It's actually pretty good. I can bring you some.
strings.horadric_side_1: Congratulations! The new church is a big deal for our <The Village>!
strings.horadric_side_2: Soon enough, I'll to add more rooms and tables!
strings.ice_axe_d: This pickaxe is a quality tool, but you feel something's wrong with it. Maybe it's that little spot of dried blood that's on your mind?
strings.illustration_1_1: He was young, romantic, a dreamer. And an incredible idler!
strings.illustration_1_2: He'd spend whole days writing poems, painting landscapes, and playing his mouth organ...
strings.illustration_1_3: Sometimes the villagers had to bury their deceased instead of him!
strings.illustration_1_4: That's all I know... er... all I've read about him.
strings.illustration_2_1: I still remember his ugly face, his whooshy whisper, and his vile laugh!
strings.illustration_2_2: Someone even saw him cooking and eating flesh cut right from his corpses!
strings.illustration_2_3: We were all scared of him. We hated him. And he hated us.
strings.illustration_2_4: And when his service finally ended 100 years ago, I was so...
strings.illustration_2_5: Oh... Ha ha ha! Sorry, I'm not that old, of course! It's just what I've been told.
strings.illustration_3_1: He was so cute, so gallant... and so smart! And those glasses... Oh my!
strings.illustration_3_2: He gave me the most delightful cures for my sciatica and hypertension!
strings.illustration_3_3: And in return, I taught him how to revive the dead!
strings.illustration_4_1: The last Keeper was a very decent man. Quite unlike you.
strings.illustration_4_2: I used to buy alcohol in the Town and we'd drink it together.
strings.illustration_4_3: When he used to get drunk, it drove him crazy. It was wildly amusing!
strings.illustration_4_4: He'd always start telling old fables about talking skulls and other worlds! Ha ha!
strings.in_cellar_3: I'll come here every night if I have to, but I'll get through eventually!
strings.in_cellar_4: Looks like I can remove this blockage and fortify the arch.
strings.in_cellar_5: This blockage can be removed only from the other side.
strings.in_the_dark_10: Then you need to be a good <Graveyard Keeper>!
strings.in_the_dark_11: You should dig up <Gerry>. He'll help you sort everything out.
strings.in_the_dark_13: What a strange vision. What is this nightmare? Ok. Let's find <Gerry>.
strings.in_the_dark_2: Calm down. You've merely turned a page in your life.
strings.in_the_dark_3: A whole new chapter awaits you ahead.
strings.in_the_dark_4: But I need to go home! Can I go home?
strings.in_the_dark_5: There is always a way to get home...
strings.in_the_dark_6: Hm... Let me see. Your new home is a graveyard.
strings.in_the_dark_8: It means you're a <Graveyard Keeper> now!
strings.in_the_dark_9: But I need to go <home> to my love!
strings.ingot_metal_d: A raw piece of iron, forged in the shape of an ingot.
strings.inquisitor_1_10: So how did you find yourself in such an interesting position?
strings.inquisitor_1_11a: Tell him about the real world.
strings.inquisitor_1_11a_1: Actually I'm from another world. I'm not entirely sure how I got here.
strings.inquisitor_1_11a_2: I need to get back home to my love.
strings.inquisitor_1_11ab_3: I don't think it's an appropriate time for jokes! And I don't appreciate your... general demeanor!
strings.inquisitor_1_11b_1: You know, I've wanted to be a graveyard keeper ever since I was a kid.
strings.inquisitor_1_11b_2: I strongly suggest you avoid bothering people with such silly stories.
strings.inquisitor_1_11c_1: Well... It just happened. There's nothing special to say...
strings.inquisitor_1_11c_2: You're definitely hiding something. And I'll find out what!
strings.inquisitor_1_12: Here I am — the <Great Inquisitor>. I protect the one true faith and humankind itself!
strings.inquisitor_1_13: We're having a tough time in <The Town>! The <Ship of the Dead> is already overloaded. And there's a new one stuck in the shipyard.
strings.inquisitor_1_14: Your graveyard is opening again at a suspiciously auspicious time.
strings.inquisitor_1_15: The dark cult is rising. I can feel it. Righteous anger rises with it in my soul!
strings.inquisitor_1_16: We've burned thousands of witches and heretics for 30 years.
strings.inquisitor_1_3: No, monsignor. — Except there was this strange fella snooping around.
strings.inquisitor_1_5: Guys, calm down. I live here at the graveyard.
strings.inquisitor_1_6: He calls us "guys"? Why, he's a cultist for certain, Monsignor!
strings.inquisitor_1_7a_1: I work as the keeper of the local graveyard. You can ask any of the villagers about me.
strings.inquisitor_1_7a_2: Then you're definitely a new one. I feel that you're telling the truth.
strings.inquisitor_1_7b_1: You know, <The Bishop> is a good friend of mine. He... he appointed me as keeper of the local graveyard.
strings.inquisitor_1_7b_2: Interesting. But I can believe you're a friend of his — though it's not a terribly impressive feat. Just pay him a compliment and he's your friend.
strings.inquisitor_1_7b_3: But appointing someone to the graveyard is certainly outside his area of responsibility.
strings.inquisitor_1_7b_4: I'll have to visit him and remind him again of the limits of his authority.
strings.inquisitor_1_8: Would you join me at the witch burning ceremony?
strings.inquisitor_1_9b_1: I have rather a weak stomach. So..
strings.inquisitor_2_1: So. You work with a lot of dead bodies, hunh?
strings.inquisitor_2_2: Yes. I think it's part of my job.
strings.inquisitor_2_3: And you live right beside this hill, near the graveyard. That right?
strings.inquisitor_2_5: Interesting, interesting... You know. I need someone to be my friend here at <The Village>.
strings.inquisitor_2_6: A friend of mine is a friend of the <Holy Inquisition>.
strings.inquisitor_2_7: I don't trust the villagers. They don't go to Church, and even refuse to lay in their graves after death!
strings.inquisitor_2_8: But you're new here. You might notice something unusual.
strings.inquisitor_2_9a_1: Sure, it'll be a pleasure to be your friend.
strings.inquisitor_2_9a_2: A wise choice. Friendship is based on trust and good will.
strings.inquisitor_2_9a_3: To earn my trust and to be a friend of the Inquisition, you will first have to show your good will.
strings.inquisitor_2_9a_4: So. I have a couple of minor tasks for you.
strings.inquisitor_2_9a_6: Everything in due time. Today is a day of wrath! Not a day of sweating the minor details.
strings.inquisitor_2_9a_7: We can talk next (d2). Or any other (d2). I like to come here. There is no other place where I can feel my holy wrath so deeply.
strings.inquisitor_2_9a_8: Now, return to your duties. Your job is very important in these dark times.
strings.inquisitor_2_9b_1: I am not interested in that kind of friendship.
strings.inquisitor_2_9b_2: I see. Well, it's up to you. I just hope that you don't become my enemy!
strings.inquisitor_2_9b_3: You may live now. Return to your duties.
strings.inquisitor_after_burning_1: <The Town> will be talking for a month about today's burning!
strings.inquisitor_after_burning_2: Whenever you're ready, we should put on a repeat performance. Just get your tent ready and we'll be in business!
strings.inquisitor_after_dark_1: Terrible... These dark organs mean nothing to him... He said it didn't prove anything...
strings.inquisitor_after_dark_2: What fools they are! While we do nothing, the curse continues to grow in power!
strings.inquisitor_after_dark_3: Soon enough it'll be too late to do anything about it...
strings.inquisitor_after_dark_4: I know you and I have had some hard times...
strings.inquisitor_after_dark_5: But you know, for the first time, I am humbly asking for your help.
strings.inquisitor_after_dark_6: In the name of the family I've lost!
strings.inquisitor_after_dark_7: Please tell me if you know of anything that can be used as evidence of witchcraft. Or the undead. Or any other cult stuff.
strings.inquisitor_black_1: I have two pieces of news for you. One bad, and one good.
strings.inquisitor_black_10: Sounds like witchcraft to me! But we decide to ask someone from the <University> about this ancient curse.
strings.inquisitor_black_11: We had one of them in the next cell over, in fact. He told us that once, a terrible curse was laid upon <The Town>. And it was quieted by an Ancient Contract.
strings.inquisitor_black_12: The first sign of the curse's return should be dark magic organs inside corpses. We'll need to gather them...
strings.inquisitor_black_13: A <Dark Heart>, <Dark Brain> and a <Dark Intestine>.
strings.inquisitor_black_14: Find them in corpses, and bring them to me as a evidence of witchcraft for the King!
strings.inquisitor_black_15: Here are some old notes. Maybe they'll help you.
strings.inquisitor_black_2: First the bad news. I'm sorry to say it, but there's a chance our king is possessed.
strings.inquisitor_black_3: He's been talking too much recently about humanity and human rights...
strings.inquisitor_black_4: I had a audience with him, and he told that it's not ok to just grab people without any evidence and burn them alive.
strings.inquisitor_black_5: So we need to put our little burning on pause. Until we bring him some evidence.
strings.inquisitor_black_6: But here's the good news. — I know where we can get this evidence.
strings.inquisitor_black_7: Not long ago we were torturing — I mean, 'interrogating' a witch.
strings.inquisitor_black_8: She swore up and down that she was innocent. But just after her death, a big ghost that looked like a chicken with red eyes appeared above her.
strings.inquisitor_black_9: And the ghost with the creepy voice said that the reckoning is at hand. The Ancient Curse returns, and soon the dead will wage war upon the living.
strings.inquisitor_burn_1: Ah, <Keeper>. I enjoy the air here. There is something righteous in it!
strings.inquisitor_burn_2: It is good to know that we'll soon be burning another witch here. We're still torturing her.
strings.inquisitor_burn_3: But forgiveness is worth it! This time the burning should go perfect!
strings.inquisitor_burn_3a_1: And we need a man like you on our side! Will you join with your fellow guardians of the faith?
strings.inquisitor_burn_3a_1a_1: I am displeased with your choice. But you are a free man... for now.
strings.inquisitor_burn_3a_1b_1: Good. You've joined at the perfect time.
strings.inquisitor_burn_4: We need to prove that no witch can escape our righteousness.
strings.inquisitor_burn_5: We need to make some preparations here. You can aid the <Holy Inquisition>.
strings.inquisitor_burn_6: We need some <Firewood> for a nice warm fire, and as many advertising <Flyers> as you can get.
strings.inquisitor_burn_7: I'll wait for you. The witch isn't going anywhere. As soon as we have everything ready, we'll burn her.
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_1: Seems your burning isn't so popular.
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_10: Besides, it will be very profitable for you!
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_12: I'll grant you rights to use the eastern slope of <Witch Hill> to grow grapes!
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_13: But I think the land there belongs to <The Village>, not to <The Inquisition>.
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_14: No, that vineyard has been in my family for decades.
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_15: I used to live there with my wife and son...
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_17: They are dead. Died in the <Great Blast>.
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_2: Rrrr.... Five years ago this place was packed.
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_20: This is no time for sentimentality! Grow some grape! Make wine!
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_21: Bring it to me. The guard will then be more motivated, and will work with extra zeal!
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_22: Believe me! When they're drunk, they find a new witch every day!
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_23: And once we get enough of them... Then we'll need to figure out how to make the burnings more entertaining.
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_24: I have some thoughts I'd like to run by you.
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_4: Seems everybody just got tired of it... Only my holy anger keeps <The Inquisition> alive!
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_5: Even our blessed Inquisition Guards haven't been able to find a new witch for a month.
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_6: Maybe it's because of the water shortage. But I think it's just a lack of motivation!
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_7: Hmm... Speaking of motivation... Do you know how to grow grapes?
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_8: It seems I'm a man of many talents...
strings.inquisitor_burn_task_9: Good. I have a very important task for you! And this time you just can't say no!
strings.inquisitor_buy_1: I appreciate your help, even if I have to pay for it!
strings.inquisitor_buy_2: Here's your money. At least you're working for us, not our enemies.
strings.inquisitor_ceremony_1: Monsignor, can I ask you for a favor?
strings.inquisitor_ceremony_3: Could you attend a big ceremony at my new <Cathedral>?
strings.inquisitor_ceremony_4: Together with <Bishop>, we'll pray for water to return to <The Town>.
strings.inquisitor_ceremony_5: Meh... I have no time for such nonsense.
strings.inquisitor_ceremony_6: But we need someone important to attend...
strings.inquisitor_ceremony_7: Try to find someone from the <Royal Court>.
strings.inquisitor_ceremony_8: Some <Keeper of the King's Kitchen> or <Keeper of the King's Chamber Pot> will be happy to show himself in public for a change.
strings.inquisitor_cultists: There's a dark cult shrine, in the cellar under the regular one.
strings.inquisitor_cultists_2: They planning to hold a dark ritual soon.
strings.inquisitor_cultists_3: Great. We'll catch them after the ritual!
strings.inquisitor_dark_all: Good we've gathered enough evidence. I will show these cursed organs to <The King>.
strings.inquisitor_dark_all_1: We'll tear <The Town> to pieces looking for heretics!
strings.inquisitor_dark_body_1: Monsignor, it's true. The dead have awakened...
strings.inquisitor_dark_body_2: I know... But we need evidence. The King must grant us extra authority!
strings.inquisitor_gerry: I could bring you a talking skull. His name is Gerry.
strings.inquisitor_gerry_1: So.. a talking skull. Interesting. — And he looks like common skull?
strings.inquisitor_gerry_2: He's an alcoholic but besides that he's just a normal skull.
strings.inquisitor_gerry_3: So what if he doesn't talk? Nobody will know that he's so special.
strings.inquisitor_gerry_4: I guess that's true... He might just pretend to be a dead skull. He does have a bad temper.
strings.inquisitor_gerry_5: Then it's no good. I'm not sure there's any way to compel the dead to talk...
strings.inquisitor_grave_1_2: A couple of years ago, it was desecrated by cultists. They had a picnic there. And I'm not sure that the evil has entirely left the place.
strings.inquisitor_grave_1_3: So I need to be sure that you're on our side in this fight before I give you <Permission> to use this part of the <Graveyard> again.
strings.inquisitor_grave_1a_1: For a friend of the inquisition it would be free, but for you we'll need to charge a fee of (slv)10.
strings.inquisitor_grave_2_2: I'm not sure... But obviously you are more trusted than most of my guards. So here's your <Permission>.
strings.inquisitor_grave_2_3: If you see anything suspicious, tell me immediately!
strings.inquisitor_grave_2a_1: I think you can be trusted as long as we have common business interests.
strings.inquisitor_gypsy_1: It is not in my rules to release someone.
strings.inquisitor_gypsy_2: But this time I'll make an exception. Her friends have been making too much of a ruckus outside my headquarters.
strings.inquisitor_help_1: I'm glad to see you're with us in our righteous battle!
strings.inquisitor_help_2: Everybody will hear about inevitability of the true faith!
strings.inquisitor_magic_item_1: I heard from one of your guardsman that you might have an <Eternal Burning Coal>.
strings.inquisitor_magic_item_2: I need it to reunite with my family.
strings.inquisitor_magic_item_3: Family... I had a family. But they were all burned... My wife and my son. Burned alive in my house.
