strings.inquisitor_magic_item_4: My house was lit on fire by the <Great Blast>. And my son was so young... I even couldn't find his remains...
strings.inquisitor_magic_item_5: But I found this coal among the ashes!
strings.inquisitor_magic_item_6: And it's been burning ever since, fuelling my anger!
strings.inquisitor_magic_item_7: I'm sure the explosion was caused by a witch coven or cultists. I founded the Inquisition to avenge all evil!
strings.inquisitor_magic_item_8: I can't give it to you until I've burned them all!
strings.inquisitor_magic_item_9: Maybe one day, with you help... But not before!
strings.inquisitor_nothing: I wouldn't know anything about that sort of thing.
strings.inquisitor_portal_done_1: I'm sure I can show you that I can be trusted well enough to look after <Witch Hill>.
strings.inquisitor_portal_done_2: Indeed... Perhaps one day I will embrace you as an Inquisitor apprentice.
strings.inquisitor_portal_guard_1: Monsignor, do you think the guards here on <Witch Hill> are really necessary?
strings.inquisitor_portal_guard_2: I'm not sure. But <The Town> is full of rumors. Someone has been seeking forbidden knowledge...
strings.inquisitor_portal_guard_3: Damn heretics! Last time, their dark rituals here on the mountain ended with a <Great Blast>!
strings.inquisitor_portal_guard_4: We can't be too careful about such things.
strings.inquisitor_portal_guard_5: I can look after the hill. I'll let you know if I see anyone come by.
strings.inquisitor_portal_guard_6: You guard ambush is obvious from a mile away.
strings.inquisitor_portal_guard_7: Hmm... You're right. But are you worthy of this sacred trust?
strings.inquisitor_second_burn_1: Anyway. I was planning a burning for today.
strings.inquisitor_second_burn_2: The witch became too weak. And burning a dead one is too boring.
strings.inquisitor_tent_1: So what's on your mind? Thinking about how you can get more people to come here?
strings.inquisitor_tent_10: Beer for sure. Beer is good for patriotism and burning stuff.
strings.inquisitor_tent_11: And something with meat. That's a very expensive delicacy in <The Town>.
strings.inquisitor_tent_12: I heard you have a source of a cheap meat...
strings.inquisitor_tent_14: But who cares about the little details when we're talking about fighting heretics!
strings.inquisitor_tent_15: Ok. I guess I can make some burgers...
strings.inquisitor_tent_16: Excellent! Build the tent! Fill it with beer and bu.. burje...
strings.inquisitor_tent_18: Yes burgers. I'll spread the news. As soon as your tent is ready and we've got a witch, we'll give them the burning of a lifetime!
strings.inquisitor_tent_2: One time we were burning old scrolls. Full of useless junk... like geometry...
strings.inquisitor_tent_3: But one of them was pretty interesting. It said that everything you need to be happy can be provided by two things: bread and circuses.
strings.inquisitor_tent_4: Of course that's only true for pagans. I can't imagine anyone living a happy life without the Church and prayer.
strings.inquisitor_tent_5: Still, what could be more entertaining than watching those evil witches burn?
strings.inquisitor_tent_7: Right! So I realized, we need to add bread! Not actual bread, of course — but snacks and drinks!
strings.inquisitor_tent_8: You're a man of business. I imagine you can open a stand or something. All the profits would be yours!
strings.inquisitor_tent_ready_1: Good! The people are going to love this!
strings.inquisitor_tent_ready_10: The audience is gathering. Do your part well. And I will do mine!
strings.inquisitor_tent_ready_2: And you'll probably earn a lot of money.
strings.inquisitor_tent_ready_4: You know at first I thought you were kind of shady. Like you might be a problem...
strings.inquisitor_tent_ready_5: I had this strange feeling that you didn't belong here...
strings.inquisitor_tent_ready_6: But now it seems like you've blended in just fine. You do what you've been asked to do.
strings.inquisitor_tent_ready_7: And profit means everything to you. I believe there's a place for a person like you in our future world.
strings.inquisitor_tent_ready_8: In the world we're going to build in <The Town>! The world of pure faith!
strings.inquisitor_wine_ready_1: Not bad! This will definitely be the best wine they've ever drunk.
strings.inquisitor_wine_ready_2: Soon our cells will be full of witches!
strings.intro_txt_1: It is an ordinary day. And our hero is hurrying home, where someone very important is waiting for him.
strings.intro_txt_2: Even in everyday routine, there's a place for loving and feeling loved.
strings.intro_txt_3: Especially when you know that someone misses you.
strings.jelly_splinter_d: A biologically active additive. No responsibility for the consequences.
strings.koukol_intro: What do you need? I have all sorts of armor and weapons.
strings.koukol_naclase_1: I heard that your master, the <Lord Commander>, recently bought a <Necklace>. I'll pay you well if you bring it to me.
strings.koukol_naclase_2: My master wouldn't buy something as useless as a <Necklace>. But the young master — the son of the <Lord Commander>. He might.
strings.koukol_naclase_3: But he left a couple years ago.
strings.koukol_naclase_4: Seems that I'll never find this <Necklace>.
strings.krezvold_about_old_keeper_2: Krezvold, do you have the time to tell me something about the other Keepers?
strings.krezvold_about_old_keeper_3: Of course not. But if it's the only way to get rid of you...
strings.light_keeper_book_1: Hi. Do you still have that book the <Astrologer> gave you?
strings.light_keeper_book_2: Yes. It's a big, fat book. The pictures are ugly! I'm using it as a leg for my wardrobe.
strings.light_keeper_book_3: Can you give it to me?
strings.light_keeper_book_4: I've already made a new leg, so why not. But it's a big, fat book, and judging from the pictures it must be very interesting.
strings.light_keeper_book_5: But I'll trade it for a bunch of <Maggots>.
strings.light_keeper_intro_2: You look like someone who desires to be a part of the magic world of...
strings.light_keeper_intro_4: I don't know much about fishing.
strings.light_keeper_intro_5: Lucky you! I know a whole lot about fishing!
strings.light_keeper_intro_6: It's so relaxing... And it can be profitable! Plus, fish are really tasty!
strings.light_keeper_intro_8: Smart choice, my boy! I'll provide you with everything you need, and teach you how to cook fish!
strings.light_keeper_recipe_2: Can you show me how you do it?
strings.light_keeper_recipe_3: You can always just grill it. But personally I like to slice it and fry the slices in oil.
strings.light_keeper_recipe_4: Then just pop fish sticks in your mouth.
strings.light_keeper_recipe_5: And you know what else? When you eat fish, you start to think like a fish! All good fisherman always eat a lot of fish!
strings.light_keeper_rode_2: Do you have one you can give me?
strings.light_keeper_rode_3: That I do, my boy. I have an old one. But I'm not just handing it over as a gift! I'll ask you to bring me some <Moths>.
strings.light_keeper_rode_4: They're good as bait. But you can only catch them at night. And I can't hardly make out anything when it's dark.
strings.light_keeper_rode_done_2: Ha! Looks like now you're officially one of us!
strings.light_keeper_rode_done_3: I'll be glad to buy any fish you catch. And as you prove yourself, I'll even sell you a nicer rod.
strings.line_replaced_1: The second part of the book's text is covered with something sticky. I'll need to clean it off first.
strings.line_replaced_2: I think I'll need some <Acid> to clean it. I gave up alchemy many years ago. It's really a dead end occupation. But I know where you can get some <Acid>.
strings.lock_tp_1: I need to cut off some flesh first.
strings.logger_intro_1: Hey. Don't even think about chopping the trees here!
strings.logger_intro_2: No, I'm just exploring the area.
strings.logger_intro_3: Good. I've paid a lot to <The Village> for the right to chop the trees around here!
strings.logger_intro_4: And I gotta tell you — it's a hard work!
strings.logger_intro_5: If only I had a better axe.
strings.logger_intro_6: What if I brought you one?
strings.logger_intro_7: I haven't made much money yet. I don't even have a house!
strings.logger_intro_8: But I can teach you my old family recipe! It's a nice pasta — it'll help you keep up your stamina while you're working.
strings.logger_recipe_2: I'll give you two recipes: pasta and lasagna. That will be all you need to keep cutting trees all day long.
strings.logger_recipe_4: Meat is expensive! The trick is in slow-releasing carbs. Lentils have even better protein!
strings.magic_pumpkin_d: Well aren't you the fairy godmother! Well, fairy godfather.
strings.mailbox_intro_1:
From: Head of  Royal Treasury Department
We are happy to congratulate you on the reopening of the <Church> and the <Graveyard>.
strings.mailbox_intro_2:
Also we are pleased to inform you that by using these lands you have become a subject of Royal law. 
All on-ground structures remain property of the Holy Church.
strings.mailbox_intro_3:
However all surface land and buildings that sit no deeper than 1 Royal leap 4 Royal spit, 
as dictated by the ancient contract, belong to the Royal family and The Town!
strings.mailbox_intro_4:
Through this mailbox, you may now access a vast array of services provided by the Royal Treasury Department. 
Your taxes may also be paid by mail. Have a nice day, and remember — King Joe VII loves you!
strings.marble_gold_plate_2: A polished brick of Spirit stone
strings.memory_potion_d: Unstable, unreliable, unbearable. Spray it in both eyes.
strings.memory_potion_receipt_d: Now you can brew up a Memory tincture. 1% alcohol, 99% bubbles.
strings.merchant_1_10: But I'm not so lucky to be highborn. So I have to earn hic... my coins here, in this onion-potato hell.
strings.merchant_1_2: If you have any spare silv hic... ver, I can offer you amazing things, tasty and rare!
strings.merchant_1_3: I humbly apologize, but I'm not buying any of your shi hic... stuff. Unless it's something invaluable.
strings.merchant_1_4: And I doubt you can find some hic... thing like that here.
strings.merchant_1_5: Actually I'm new here. Everybody thinks I'm the keeper at the local graveyard.
strings.merchant_1_6: But I'm from another world, and I need to go back.
strings.merchant_1_7: I understand you all too well. This world is not mine hic... either.
strings.merchant_1_9: Mine is a world of grandeur hic... the palaces of <The Town>.
strings.merchant_2a: Scare him to cure his hiccups.
strings.merchant_2a_2: Are you mad?! What are you doing?
strings.merchant_2a_3: I was only trying to help you with your hiccups.
strings.merchant_2a_4: That was a fool thing to do! I just need a little time.
strings.merchant_2a_5: That shark fin steak I ate this morning was so delicious. But I have to admit that the golden fried butterfly wings stole the show.
strings.merchant_2a_6: It seems like you're ok now, after my little surprise attack.
strings.merchant_2b_1: Horadric gave me permission to use the garden near the church. I need to discuss the terms of use with you.
strings.merchant_2b_2: Oh. I had totally forgot about that dead weight. It cost me so little.
strings.merchant_2b_3: But of course that was so many years ago, and due to inflation — and the good soil... why, now it's quite a valuable commodity!
strings.merchant_2b_4: Let me see. Hmm. How about (gld)10?
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2a_1: Still too much but. It's ok.
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_0: I'm short on money. Maybe we can discuss some kind of barter?
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_1: I see. You're a poor man, who wants to earn a little money by growing crops.
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_2: We can discuss the terms of your rent. But first let's see how good a farmer you are.
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_3: Let's make a deal. You deliver a batch of carrots, cabbages, and beets...
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_4: Then I'll see you as a serious business partner, and we'll make a long-term deal that's profitable for both parties. What do you say?
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_4a_0: As soon as I have my first harvest, I'll bring it to you.
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_4a_1: One more thing. If you have the time, I'd like to ask you for a small favor.
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_4b_0: You know what? I'm gonna use this garden, and I won't pay you a penny!
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_4b_2: Now this garden will cost you a fortune. I can't prevent you for using it.
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_4b_3: But I have a feeling we'll have another talk about this garden in the future...
strings.merchant_2b_5b_2b_4b_4: Right now I'm not interested in doing business with you.
strings.merchant_2e_1abc_1: Now just repay your loan and we can move on to our cooperation!
strings.merchant_2e_1d_1: Where can I buy some seeds?
strings.merchant_2e_1d_2: I don't trade in that cheap stuff. I expect you can buy some low quality seeds at a local farm.
strings.merchant_2e_1d_3: If you need some money, I can lend you some. (slv)5 now, and you'll pay me back (slv)10.
strings.merchant_2e_1d_4a_1: A loan with no return date. I'll take one of those!
strings.merchant_2e_1d_4b_1: Thanks, but this loan seems unfair.
strings.merchant_70_1: So does anything else stand between you and the job?
strings.merchant_70_10: And there it is. A simple yet elegant plan!
strings.merchant_70_12: Not really. I've always chosen a good dinner over the company of a woman. Ha ha...
strings.merchant_70_13: Just tell me when you've gotten her on our side.
strings.merchant_70_2: I think we've done everything you wanted.
strings.merchant_70_3: Almost! The head of the <Royal Council> isn't a member of the gourmet's club.
strings.merchant_70_6: Ms Charm's... charms... If you know what I mean.
strings.merchant_70_7b_1: Sometimes she gives him... private concerts...
strings.merchant_70_7b_2b_1: Well... he's rather fond of her little melody... so to speak... you know...
strings.merchant_70_8: So Ms Charm is the only person who can talk him into supporting me.
strings.merchant_70_9: And you're the kind of guy who could possibly get along with her.
strings.merchant_actress_1: I've talked to Ms Charm. She'll take care of the head of the <Royal Council>.
strings.merchant_afterall: Hi. How's life with your new title?
strings.merchant_afterall_1: It's miserable. The King is used to eating rubbish...and he seems to be ok with it.
strings.merchant_afterall_2: I'll try to improve his tastes, but it's going to be a lot of work...
strings.merchant_afterall_3: So if you have all that work to do, why are you still coming here?
strings.merchant_afterall_4: Heh... My new job is honorable but not very profitable. And apparently, my glorious brother is deep in debt.
strings.merchant_afterall_5: It's my family responsibility to help him. So the fun never stops for me. Let's do some business. Ha ha!
strings.merchant_ceremony_1: Could you attend the big ceremony at my new <Cathedral>?
strings.merchant_ceremony_2: Together with <Bishop>, we'll pray for water to return to <The Town>.
strings.merchant_ceremony_4: I guess so, yes. The cheeky one.
strings.merchant_ceremony_5: Heh. This ceremony will be a great way to show everyone my new position.
strings.merchant_ceremony_7: I don't know. The <Bishop> is my brother... We haven't spoken in many years.
strings.merchant_ceremony_8: He thinks I've been wasting my time traveling, instead of making career here in <The Town>.
strings.merchant_ceremony_9: Maybe it's time for you to make peace...
strings.merchant_common_part_1: You seem like a reasonable guy I could trust.
strings.merchant_common_part_12: To achieve my goal, we'll need to win the battle on two fronts.
strings.merchant_common_part_13: First we need to corner the high-end food market in <The Town>.
strings.merchant_common_part_14: Second we need to bribe the members of the <Royal Council>!
strings.merchant_common_part_4: And I happy to know you're on my side.
strings.merchant_common_part_5: It's time you and I achieved the justice we deserve!
strings.merchant_common_part_6: I mean what we really, really deserve!
strings.merchant_common_part_7: And to that end, I must become the <Keeper of the King's Kitchen> — and first tester, of course!
strings.merchant_common_part_8: This will grant me incredible power! Plus I'll get to try all that delicious food, which only the king can afford.
strings.merchant_common_part_9: And what's all this have to do with me?
strings.merchant_crate_2: The most obvious way is to move them along the road.
strings.merchant_crate_3: But maybe there's another way. I think the storage room is connected to the church cellar.
strings.merchant_crate_4: But I'm a little too portly to climb down there and check it myself.
strings.merchant_crate_5: Hm... Maybe I can move these crates through the tunnel.
strings.merchant_crate_6: But I'll need to build an elevator for the crates.
strings.merchant_dinner_1: It wasn't easy, but I made them.
strings.merchant_dinner_2: Looks great. You're a real chef.
strings.merchant_dinner_3: Tomorrow the court will flood with rumors about tonight's dinner.
strings.merchant_dinner_4: Come see me next week and I'll tell you how it went.
strings.merchant_favore_1: My friend. I like delicious food. But lately I've been having stomach problems.
strings.merchant_favore_2: After a good dinner I get the hiccups. It's driving me mad.
strings.merchant_favore_3: A friend of mine from the wine club told me that <Hiccup-Grass> can help.
strings.merchant_favore_4: I believe there's plenty of it in the swamp. I'd be very grateful if you could bring me some!
strings.merchant_favore_5: Sure, I'll look around for some.
strings.merchant_favore_done_1: Oh, thank you. I'll eat it right now.
strings.merchant_favore_done_11: Wait a minute. Do you know any witches?
strings.merchant_favore_done_12a_1: There's an old lady living in the swamp. I'm not sure if she's a real witch. But she called herself a witch.
strings.merchant_favore_done_12a_2: Clotho. She's still alive. She must be a real witch then!
strings.merchant_favore_done_12b_1: Hmm... The Inquisitor probably burned them all.
strings.merchant_favore_done_12b_2: If old <Clotho> is still alive... She was pretty old when I was young. If she's still alive, she must be a real wit...
strings.merchant_favore_done_12b_3: You should find her in the center of the <Western Swamp>.
strings.merchant_favore_done_13: Tell her that the merchant and priest who used to buy the <Love Potions> from her need help. I am sure she'll remember us.
strings.merchant_favore_done_15: No my brother was the priest... I don't want to talk about it... So I'm counting on you, my friend! Bring me a cure for this curse!
strings.merchant_favore_done_16: I'll see what I can do.
strings.merchant_favore_done_2: What a strange taste. Hm... Now I taste nothing.
strings.merchant_favore_done_3: Wait a second. Let me take a bite of the spicy cookie I have in my pocket.
strings.merchant_favore_done_4: Why, it's tasteless! I sense nothing at all. What did you give me?!
strings.merchant_favore_done_6: Oh my god, it's happened! It's the curse! Once, when I was young, I was told that I'd lose the most important thing in my life!
strings.merchant_favore_done_8: An old fortune teller. I was traveling with my caravan in the desert, across the northern mountains.
strings.merchant_favore_done_9: We stopped at an oasis. And there was this old woman. Everything she said came true. And now this.
strings.merchant_forgive_1: I think I was wrong about all that stuff with the garden. So I want to apologize.
strings.merchant_forgive_2: Sure. We're business people. Apology accepted!
strings.merchant_forgive_4: Now you just need to pay me (gld)1 for the garden.
strings.merchant_forgive_5: And do a small favor for me.
strings.merchant_magic_item_1: I've heard rumored that you have a <Salty Fork>.
strings.merchant_magic_item_2: I've reached the point in my life that a <Salty Fork> is something I desperately need.
strings.merchant_magic_item_3: Oh... Well, this <Salty Fork> means a lot to me. It was one of two things that I found with my brother.
strings.merchant_magic_item_4: We were looking for food at <The Town> dump. And I found this fork. I think it came from the <Great Blast>.
strings.merchant_magic_item_5: I'm from a very poor family, and this fork made me who I am. I looked at it for hours, imagining what is it for.
strings.merchant_magic_item_6: I decided to travel, and find some answers. So I left <The Town>... I discovered that forks are for eating... Also I learned a lot of other wonderful things.
strings.merchant_magic_item_7: You know, sometimes I think this fork actually make things tastier...Ha ha...
strings.merchant_magic_item_8: Now I'm on the brink of a new phase of my life. I could give it to you. But first I want to be sure that you're worthy of the gift.
strings.merchant_marketing_1: We'll use an ancient technique that never fails.
strings.merchant_marketing_2: Make a bunch of advertising <Flyers> and leave them on a office desk.
strings.merchant_marketing_3: Hmm... In my world we use celebrities to boost sales...
strings.merchant_marketing_4: Brilliant idea! You can ask Ms Charm to represent our company. That'll definitely work!
strings.merchant_marketing_5: I could also advertise our company during my (d6) ceremony at church.
strings.merchant_marketing_6: That's a great idea! Now I know for sure that I've chosen a right person to be my partner!
strings.merchant_marketing_done_1: Great. Now I see why the baker gave me a free pie this morning.
strings.merchant_marketing_done_2: People are starting to talk about our product's high quality!
strings.merchant_marketing_done_3: Too bad we can't sell more than 10 <Crates> per week. Darn license restrictions...
strings.merchant_marketing_done_4: But the better (marketing) we have, the better price I can get!
strings.merchant_on_cure_1: Here, I brought this cure for you. <Clotho> told me it would help.
strings.merchant_on_cure_10: Just make some snacks, a main course and some dessert. — But they should all be of the highest quality!
strings.merchant_on_cure_11: Why me? I'm no good at all this cooking stuff.
strings.merchant_on_cure_12: I can trust no other soul in <The Town>! The stakes are too high!
strings.merchant_on_cure_13: Why don't you cook it yourself?
strings.merchant_on_cure_14: Nonsense! I'm a foodie, not a cook!
strings.merchant_on_cure_15: Don't worry, you can do this. And that <Spice> you made — it'll make this dinner unforgettable!
strings.merchant_on_cure_2: Hmm. Let me try it. I'll just sprinkle it on these fried grasshoppers.
strings.merchant_on_cure_3: Mmmm... Delicious! Even tastier than before...
strings.merchant_on_cure_4: Thank you so much. So where did you get this precious ingredient?
strings.merchant_on_cure_5: I just made it myself. All it took was some alchemy, and a bit of common sense.
strings.merchant_on_cure_6: Interesting... interesting... I see many possibilities here...
strings.merchant_on_cure_7: This flavor could open many gates — even, perhaps, the palace gates...
strings.merchant_on_cure_8: I'll need to arrange a dinner for some of the <Royal Council> members.
strings.merchant_on_cure_9: And that's where I need your help. I need you to cook a great dinner for 5 people.
strings.merchant_on_deal_done: It seems you can manage the garden well enough.
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_1: But to be honest, these vegetables are terrible.
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_2: I could only sell them to the poor townsfolk. — They'll eat anything.
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_3: Especially after two bad harvests in a row.
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_4a_1: I don't see any sign of bad harvests... Seems like everything is growing great!
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_4a_2: This place is truly sacred. But in <The Town> and its suburbs there's a water shortage.
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_4a_3: The <Vimur River> has gone down. Only the <Gjoll>, which runs past you graveyard, still brings some water to <Vimur>.
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_4a_4: Even <The Town's> bay has receded. So the <Ship of the Dead> can't leave.
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_4b_1: Is it possible to sell future harvests?
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_4b_2: We can't corner the market with these vegetables!
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_4b_3: But I see potential. With the a help of some good fertilizer, and the proper selection of crops, I believe you might grow something special!
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_4b_4: But first you need to get a <Trade License> through the <Royal Service Box> near your church.
strings.merchant_on_deal_done_4b_5: Get one, and I'll be glad to have you as my partner!
strings.merchant_plan_done: Ha ha! My friend! Everything went as I predicted.
strings.merchant_plan_done_1: The position is mine. There are still some people who aren't happy with my assignment.
strings.merchant_plan_done_2: Are they going to be a problem for you?
strings.merchant_plan_done_3: Yes. I can't let me guard down. There's no way for me to establish my name. I never get to do anything in public.
strings.merchant_plan_done_4: If only I can attend some public ceremony in my formal capacity as the <Keeper of the King's Kitchen>.
strings.merchant_plan_done_5: I'll need to wait for an opportunity like that. Until then, I just need to keep my head down, and rely on our business.
strings.merchant_strategy_1: The dinner was magnificent. We've gained some support in the <Royal Council>.
strings.merchant_strategy_2a: We'll need to press them more, but first let's settle our little business venture...
strings.merchant_strategy_2b: I think I know a way to gain the <Royal Council's> full support. When you're ready, my friend, I'll be glad to share my plan with you.
strings.merchant_traide_license_1: Great! Now we're in business. Between my connections and your hard work...
strings.merchant_traide_license_10: Let me see. I think for start I can sell one <Crate> per week. That's not too much.
strings.merchant_traide_license_11: But nobody's heard of us. We'll need to invest in marketing! And make our first sale!
strings.merchant_traide_license_12: So our company has two main goals.
strings.merchant_traide_license_13: First, increase our (fame) level to at least 3. That means we'll be able to sell 3 <Crates> per week!
strings.merchant_traide_license_15: I'll be proud for us if we reach these goals!
strings.merchant_traide_license_2: We'll be super rich! But first we need to organize our process.
strings.merchant_traide_license_3: We'll open our first office in this barn...
strings.merchant_traide_license_5: We'll put pallets here. And I'll take <Crates> of goods from here every (d4).
strings.merchant_traide_license_7: That's right, we're in a big business now, so we need to pack our products.
strings.merchant_traide_license_8: You're a handy fellow, and I know you have a workshop near the graveyard. I'm sure you can pack everything in nice wooden <Crates>.
strings.merchant_traide_license_8_1: You know, our trade license allows us to sell practically anything. We can sell any kind of goods.
strings.merchant_traide_license_8_2: You don't need to pack only vegetables. Although the food shortage has driven up prices quite a bit...
strings.merchant_traide_license_8_3: But if you can find some cheap labor, selling other goods can be profitable too.
strings.merchent_expend_1: Soon we'll be able to think about expanding our production line...
strings.merchent_expend_2: You know <The Town> does not live by bread alone.
strings.merchent_expend_done: Now we have a decent share of the market. This is the perfect foothold for our plan.
strings.merchent_expend_done_1: But we still need to secure the support of the <Royal Council>.
strings.merchent_expend_done_2a: And here, my friend, we come to the point where I must trust you once more.
strings.merchent_expend_done_2b: I think I know a way we can gain the <Royal Council's> full support. When you're ready, my friend, I'll share the plan with you.
strings.miller_1_1: Greetings! The mill is broken. Sorry.
strings.miller_1_2: If you need something milled, you'd better go to <The Town>.
strings.miller_1_3: That's too bad. But I have nothing to mill.
strings.miller_1_6: I have some old reserves you may find useful.
strings.miller_2_1: I get so tired without any work to do.
strings.miller_after_fix_1: You can mill your wheat here for free if you want!
strings.miller_after_fix_2: I hope this helps me get <Alisa's Paper>.
strings.miller_fix_mill_1: Do you know what the Mill needs for repairs?
strings.miller_fix_mill_10: I think I'll need <Astrologer's> help to figure this stuff out.
strings.miller_fix_mill_2: You're welcome to give it a shot! I tried to fix it myself, but I only made things only worse.
strings.miller_fix_mill_3: I have this manual for the thing. But it's in Latin.
strings.miller_fix_mill_4: Oh my... And back home we blame IKEA...
strings.miller_fix_mill_5: It says we need stone... And steel parts... Ok, let's see the instructions...
strings.miller_fix_mill_7: Umm. There weren't any pictures on it...I thought it wasn't important...
strings.miller_fix_mill_8: And the paper was so soft...
strings.miller_fix_mill_9: I see... Geometry isn't really my strong suit.
strings.miller_tp_1: The door is closed until I have (happy)80 with the <Miller>.
strings.mine_hint: The mine is full of toxic gasses. If only I could find someone who doesn't need to breathe...
strings.money_income_after_burning: You earned (slv)33 selling beer and burgers.
strings.mrs chain_1: You better talk with my husband. He's in charge here.
strings.need_cancel_craft: You need to halt any other crafts to begin this one.
strings.no_bait_descr: Different baits affect the chance of getting different fish types.
strings.npc_actress_tavern_song_1: I feel it in the air and water...
strings.npc_actress_tavern_song_2: I sense it from below and above...
strings.npc_actress_tavern_song_3: It makes me much stronger, much gentler, much hotter...
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_1_a: I read so much about the dangers of alcohol...
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_1_b: ... that I decided to give up reading altogether.
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_2_a: They say that smoking leads to a slow and torturous death.
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_2_b: So the rest of us will die quickly and cheerfully?
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_3_a: I don't drink beer, it causes the belly to puff up.
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_3_b: I prefer vodka. The liver isn't so visible!
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_4_a: You know, running is great for the spirit!
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_4_b: You run to a pub, run back with a beer — and you feel so good!
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_5_a: Distinguishing high-quality alcohol from low-quality alcohol is very simple.
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_5_b: If you survived — it's high quality.
strings.npc_blacksmith_joke_6_a: I've been having problems with alcohol for a long time. What problems?
strings.npc_cultist_taks_1: Bring a bucket of blood and 5 bloody nails.
strings.npc_guard_2_hill_closed: By order of the <Great Inquisitor>, this path is closed until (d2).
strings.npc_guard_5: Come right ahead, enjoy your visit to <The Town>.
strings.npc_guard_say_2: I'm a guard in the dark.
strings.npc_guard_talk_0: We can talk in the day, not now.
strings.npc_hunchback_joke_1_a: Years ago, I used to divide people into two piles.
strings.npc_hunchback_joke_1_b: And then they put me in jail.
strings.npc_hunchback_joke_2_a: Why pay a vet over and over again...
strings.npc_hunchback_joke_2_b: If you can just pay a taxidermist once?
strings.npc_hunchback_joke_3_b: Because there are skeletons inside them, and skeletons are evil monsters.
strings.npc_hunchback_joke_4_a: How can you be sure which rat will win a rat race?
strings.npc_hunchback_joke_4_b: Just poison all the other rats.
strings.npc_hunchback_joke_5_a: When I was little, I used to spend my holidays with my grandparents.
strings.npc_hunchback_joke_5_b: That should tell you how tired I am of cemeteries!
strings.npc_hunchback_joke_6_b: Until I was 7, I thought my name was "back off".
strings.npc_light_keeper_joke_1_a: Once I caught a three-meter catfish. But I had to let it go.
strings.npc_light_keeper_joke_1_b: No one would have believed it anyway.
strings.npc_light_keeper_joke_2_a: My wife divorced me because I stink of fish. But am I really to blame?
strings.npc_light_keeper_joke_2_b: Fish wash themselves 24 hours a day, and they still stink of fish!
strings.npc_light_keeper_joke_3_a: All my fishing excursions are successful.
strings.npc_light_keeper_joke_4_a: My fisherman friend never has any luck.
strings.npc_light_keeper_joke_4_b: Yesterday his worm celebrated its 10th anniversary...
strings.npc_light_keeper_joke_5_a: My wife wanted to lose weight, and took up horse riding.
strings.npc_light_keeper_joke_6_a: My wife is so caring! I told her that I wanted to be buried under an oak tree.
strings.npc_light_keeper_joke_6_b: And my wife immediately ran out to dig the grave...
strings.npc_miller_joke_1_a: Our Keeper used to affectionately call all his corpses 'puppies'.
strings.npc_miller_joke_2_a: Did you hear about the miller who died while he was falling asleep?
strings.npc_miller_joke_3_a: What's the difference between a graveyard and a tavern?
strings.npc_miller_joke_3_b: In a tavern, you can lie down dead and not be buried.
strings.npc_miller_joke_4_a: It's good to be a graveyard keeper!
strings.npc_miller_joke_4_b: You can always save on flowers for your sweetheart!
strings.npc_miller_joke_5_b: But now no one will find out that I have beetles in my flour!
strings.npc_miller_joke_6_a: Too much flour is bad for your health. But don't be upset.
strings.npc_miller_joke_6_b: After all, it's also bad for your health!
strings.npc_potter_1: Hello, my friend! Sorry, but I'm busy right now.
strings.npc_wood_cutter_1: The weather is so nice today.
strings.obsidian_plate_2: A polished brick of Silence stone
strings.obsidian_plate_3: A carved piece of Silence stone
strings.obstruction_place: There's no way I can remove it.
strings.p_axeman_d: You know how to use an axe. Chopping a small tree can now give you an additional log. Also you can make more firewood and wedges from log chunks.
strings.p_beekeeper2_d: You've been bitten so many times that bees can't even damage you any more. So you have enough time to collect more honey from a beehive.
strings.p_big_guy_d: It appears that if you work with iron a lot, you become big and strong. +1 damage, +1 defense.
strings.p_blacksmith_d: You like to work with red-hot iron. Hammering relaxes you. And when the work is done, you always manage to find time to make extra nails.
strings.p_butcher_d: You know how to work with meat. You have less chance of making a surgical error when extracting Hardspares and Softspares.
strings.p_cardinal_d: The church is not only a triumph of the spirit. It's also a number of buildings and properties. You've learned how to manage them, so ceremonies give you extra money.
strings.p_collector_d: You love nature and nature loves you back. You can gather more resources from small plants.
strings.p_cultist_d: Everything has a meaning. You can see the (skull) and (rskull) of body parts.
strings.p_doctor_d: The dead won't sue you, but still you need to be careful.  You have a reduced chance of making a surgical error when extracting Important parts.
strings.p_eloquence_d: A note in the Church made you more vigilant and careful, and your prayers more sincere. From now on, you'll be gathering more faith.
strings.p_engineer_d: You know how complex mechanisms work. All the details of your work are top quality. Even your carving and jewelry look cleaner.
strings.p_farmer_d: You aren't afraid of getting your hands dirty. You can select good seeds and harvest a better crop.
strings.p_fireman_d: The spurting flame charms you. You know a lot about fire, so you know how to increase your furnace productivity, and you can smelt more ore per load.
strings.p_good_writer_d: You write good books. Actually you find you can just write down anything you remember from modern culture.
strings.p_industriousness_d: Any work develops you, even the work of evil. You've accepted your dark side, and it's enabled you to craft more effectively.
strings.p_jevelery_d: You have a nose for gems, so you'll find them more often. Also you know how to make really nice jewelry.
strings.p_journalist_d: You notice the little things about people. Put these things together and you have a story. Sometimes you can get stories from dialogs.
strings.p_mason_d: Stones are your passion, so your stone carving is really good. Also you're so efficient that you can get an additional piece of stone from a big rock.
strings.p_master_potter_d: A piece of clay, twisting in your hands — and BAM! It's a masterpiece!
strings.p_miner_d: You are a true miner. You can find precious metals and ores more often, but it's still a matter of luck and energy.
strings.p_naturalist_d: You go deeper. Find out the essence of things. Studying an item has a chance of giving you a story.
strings.p_persistence_d: Despite all the danger and risk, you courageously faced down your enemies — and won! Your backbone has gotten firmer, and now restores more energy.
strings.p_preacher_d: Bishop told you that now you can arrange a church service. So there you go!
strings.p_scientist_d: You've inhaled a lot of fumes during your experiments. You've developed an inner voice that help you measure ingredients. You'll produce one extra reagent from any materials.
strings.p_sword_master_d: You know how to use your blade! You inflict additional damage and probably look cool with your sword.
strings.p_tierd_d: Seems that you don't need to sleep so much.
strings.p_wine_master_d: You like to drink good alcohol — especially wine! Your hangover depends of the alcohol you've drank. Moreover, all alcohol you make has a better quality.
strings.p_woodworker_d: You know how to deal with wood! Circular saws are more productive in your hands.
strings.p_writer_d: You know how to put words together. Sometimes you even manage to write a good sentence. Mother would be proud.
strings.pagan_amule_d: One of the most loathsome things ever. Made with love.
strings.pail_water_d: Use this item to get water.
strings.perspective_text_before_1s:
A long time ago...

The Ancient God created the Sky, the Earth, wheat whiskey and three priestess sisters to serve Him.

And He liked it so much that He created priests, and legionaries, and many other people to serve Him.

The people were fools. They knew nothing and could make nothing. But the Ancient God was generous, and He gave the people homes, food, water, clothes...

And after death, their souls would float across the Ancient Bridge and on to the Land of the Dead.

But like all great stories, love spoiled everything...
strings.pick_embalming: Pick an embalming fluid to apply.
strings.player_final: Everything is ready. But what's next?
strings.player_final_1: How do you turn the Portal on?
strings.player_final_11: Well. We've been banned from <The Town>. Two brothers, one in the royal court, the other is a high cleric.
strings.player_final_12: That sort of thing looks suspicious to the <Royal Council>. We went to the tavern, and then Lawrence had a feeling in his stomach that you were here.
strings.player_final_13: But I did manage to excommunicate half <The Town> before we left! Ha ha! Now the only official church is the <Church> beside the graveyard!
strings.player_final_14: You can take the church and garden if you want...
strings.player_final_15: The symbols are starting to shine...
strings.player_final_17: We barely managed to escape <The Town>. The <Lord Commander> used all his influence to slander us.
strings.player_final_18: To be honest it wasn't hard to find something to pin on us. <The Town> is quite a mess these days.
strings.player_final_19: The dead rise. Lord Inquisitor is accused of being the leader of a dark cult. It is a terrible time...
strings.player_final_22: We're going to hide in the lighthouse for a while. Maybe we'll be able to get in touch with Vagner somehow...
strings.player_final_23: I told you he'd be here!
strings.player_final_24: I see you're planning on leaving us, my friend.
strings.player_final_26: This is bad. Very bad. The curse is only gaining the momentum. We can't stop it.
strings.player_final_28: I should feel great about it. But I'm not.
strings.player_final_29: We're going to settle here. And rebuild our old house.
strings.player_final_3: I need to go back to my love.
strings.player_final_30: This place is sacred and protected from the curse.
strings.player_final_31: But still. We'll be facing an <Amazing Time>. Everything will change.
strings.player_final_33: It works! At last! My wish came true!
strings.player_final_4: I'm really sad now. I'll miss you!
strings.player_final_6: Sad... Hmm. This portal isn't just for travelling... It can make your heart's desire come true.
strings.player_final_7: But be careful what you say. We definitely don't need another <Great Blast>.
strings.player_final_9: Hi friend. We've come to say goodbye.
strings.player_found_zombie_need_carveout: I think I need to clear the rocks in the middle of the road.
strings.player_found_zombie_think: This must be the place Gunter was talking about.
strings.player_ready_to_exctract: I should start looking for that zombie...
strings.pot_berserk_d: You deal a lot of damage but also lose (hp) over time.
strings.pray_1: I'd like to say a few words...
strings.pray_3: And now... Let us pray for this blessing!
strings.pray_result_fail: Your preaching was a failure. Try increasing your church quality (cross) to increase your chances of success.
strings.preach_is_locked: Preaching is not available for now
strings.preach_params: %1 needed to guarantee a successful ceremony.
strings.quest_instruction_snake_d: You need to use a <Keeper's Key> with this instruction at a <Study Table>.
strings.red_eye_1_13: Calm down. You just turned one page of your life.
strings.red_eye_1_14: A whole new chapter awaits you ahead.
strings.red_eye_1_15: But I need to go home! How can I go home?
strings.red_eye_1_16: There's always a way to get home...
strings.red_eye_1_17: Hm... let me see. Your new home is a graveyard.
strings.red_eye_1_20: But I need to go <home> to my love!
strings.red_eye_1_21: Then you need to be a good <Graveyard Keeper>!
strings.red_eye_1_22: Go dig up Gerry. He'll help show you the ropes.
strings.red_eye_1_3: Keeper 642. I think I can call you just Keeper.
strings.red_eye_1_4: Your duty is to look after the place. And do as I command.
strings.red_eye_1_7: I hate all these stupid questions.
strings.red_eye_1_8: You know, you should go and dig up Gerry. He used to be quite а chatty fellow.
strings.refguee_s62_1_1: It will be hard to persuade him. I don't have <any evidence>.
strings.refguee_s62_1_10: Listen, I don't have time for stupid jokes. We're getting ready for battle.
strings.refguee_s62_1_11: And I need to care that the boss doesn't notice that half the weaponry has vanished. So buy something or shove off!
strings.refguee_s62_1_12: Wait, there's one piece of evidence! Beatrice owns a <scroll of ghoul raising>!
strings.refguee_s62_1_13: If Koukol sees that scroll, then he'll believe me.
strings.refguee_s62_1_14: I need to talk to him again.
strings.refguee_s62_1_2: Koukol, I have some extremely important information for you and the Lord Commander.
strings.refguee_s62_1_3: Lady Beatrice is planning to inject all the soldiers of Mountain Fort with a Death Emulsion...
strings.refguee_s62_1_4: And after that, she's going to revive them all as ghouls!
strings.refguee_s62_1_6: I'm trying to figure out whether you're drunk or you're off your nut.
strings.refguee_s62_1_7: Dude, she's a nasty bitch. I can't argue with that...
strings.refguee_s62_1_8: But ghouls? Man, couldn't you think of anything more realistic? Ghouls don't exist.
strings.refguee_s62_1_9: Yes, everyone says so, but I'm not lying! You're all in great danger!
strings.refugee_city_1_1_1: This morning I spoke with a former servant of my father. He spoke of the <Inquisitions' repressions>.
strings.refugee_city_1_1_2: The people are falling into panic. Nobody knows who they'll come for next. The atmosphere of fear is growing and growing.
strings.refugee_city_1_1_3: Have they thought about the possibility of leaving <Town>?
strings.refugee_city_1_1_4: They're too frightened. They pay huge bribes in exchange for promises of safety. But the safety only lasts a short while.
strings.refugee_city_1_1_5: But no, generally speaking, there's nowhere to escape around here. Except <our camp>, maybe.
strings.refugee_city_1_1_7: I'd like to help these people. I really would. But our camp is so small...
strings.refugee_city_1_1_8: Well, I could build an <additional tent>.
strings.refugee_city_1_1_9: It would be great. And it also means we'd need a <well>. Otherwise the people will start suffering from thirst.
strings.refugee_city_1_2_1: Excellent work! We appreciate it, my friend.
strings.refugee_city_1_2_10: It looks like there's no problem you can't solve, Graveyard Keeper.
strings.refugee_city_1_2_2: Especially now, when we've almost run out of fresh water.
strings.refugee_city_1_2_4: I asked the old servant to inform <my friends in Town> that we're ready to take them in.
strings.refugee_city_1_2_5: And just the one extra tent is enough, right?
strings.refugee_city_1_2_6: I'm not sure. There are dozens of people on the <inquisitors' lists>.
strings.refugee_city_1_2_7: Then I'll set up <one more tent>.
strings.refugee_city_1_2_8: That will be good, but we're still having trouble with food. And new people will only aggravate the problem.
strings.refugee_city_1_2_9: Obviously, you need a <garden> for growing vegetables.
strings.refugee_city_1_3_1: Now that we have some <empty spaces>, our friends have a chance to escape the fire of the Inquisition!
strings.refugee_city_1_3_2: I sent letters to three of them. Hopefully they'll take advantage of the opportunity.
strings.refugee_city_1_3_3: Well, at least this camp is much friendlier than a jail cell.
strings.refugee_city_1_3_4: There's none of the luxuries here they're accustomed to, of course, but the fresh air and pure well water aren't bad.
strings.refugee_city_1_3_6: I have a great idea! What would you think of an <automatic well>?
strings.refugee_city_1_3_7: That would be more than useful to us. But could you build such a thing?
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_1: I see that I was right to trust you, my friend.
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_10: Then I wish you good luck. And a happy return home very soon.
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_11: That would be perfect. Though I lost my true home long ago.
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_2: You provided us with food, water, and a place to live.
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_3: I know that you're doing it for a <fee>, but that doesn't make your efforts less decent.
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_4: Well, getting paid to do something good is always better than getting paid to do something bad.
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_5: Certainly. And I'd like to award you a part of the promised fee right now. Beginning with this artifact, the <Witcher's Eye>.
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_6: I'm sure it will be useful to you. Beyond that, I don't have new tasks for you for the moment.
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_7: Okay. What are you gonna do now?
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_8: We decided to appeal directly to the <King> — it's our last chance at clemency.
strings.refugee_city_1_fin_9: My cousin will go to him, on the day of the <prince's wedding> — the King will find it hard to refuse, since it's a great holiday.
strings.refugee_city_2_2_1: This camp is beginning to feel more and more like home. Thanks to your efforts, of course.
strings.refugee_city_2_2_2: Thank you, my friend, for the warehouse and the campfire.
strings.refugee_city_2_2_3: No problem, it wasn't too difficult.
strings.refugee_city_2_2_4: As far as I know, many others are already prepared to join us.
strings.refugee_city_2_2_5: Would you be so kind as to raise <one more tent>?
strings.refugee_city_2_2_6: And I'd also ask you to build a <workbench> for me. I've thought up some designs, and I can't wait to see if they work in practice.
strings.refugee_city_2_2_7: Perhaps the results of my research will be useful not only to us but to you as well.
strings.refugee_city_2_2_8: A tent and a workbench? Easy!
strings.refugee_city_2_3_1: Good work! Now we have new vacancies in our camp. Soon <my friends> will join us.
strings.refugee_city_2_3_2: Why can't they come right away? It's dangerous for them to remain in Town.
strings.refugee_city_2_3_3: There are many obstacles... Besides, it's not easy to abandon your home, your relatives, your community...
strings.refugee_city_2_3_4: Not to mention, it's no easy task to leave Town in secret. As a matter of fact, it's <mortally dangerous>.
strings.refugee_city_2_3_5: The town guard have lists of people who are counted by Inquisition as possible heretics.
strings.refugee_city_2_fin_10: And a little something from me personally — <this book>. A close friend wrote it. They cut him down while we were escaping from prison.
strings.refugee_city_2_fin_12: Thanks a lot to you, my friend.
strings.refugee_city_2_fin_2: We were miserable fugitives, frightened, helpless, desperate. Doomed.
strings.refugee_city_2_fin_3: And now we've become <proud settlers>, looking to the future with bravery and hope.
strings.refugee_city_2_fin_4: This would have been impossible without your help, my dear friend.
strings.refugee_city_2_fin_5: Well... yep, it would be silly to deny it. But it's thanks to you too.
strings.refugee_city_2_fin_6: Moreover, we have serious potential for further development.
strings.refugee_city_2_fin_7: I spoke in secret with the head of the local Village, <Horadric>. He wouldn't mind establishing regular trade with us, and so on.
strings.refugee_city_2_fin_8: I'm sincerely happy for you and your people, marquis.
strings.refugee_city_2_fin_9: So it's high time to grant you the final part of <your fee>.
strings.refugee_city_3_1_1: Marquis, I have to warn you: your enemies have learned your whereabouts.
strings.refugee_city_3_1_11: Enough. I've made my decision. We won't run. <We'll fight>.
strings.refugee_city_3_1_12: Only one question remains. — Will you stand ready to help us once more?
strings.refugee_city_3_1_13: As long as you didn't mean fight for you — sure, I'm ready.
strings.refugee_city_3_1_14: No, not actually fighting. Rather, we need <weapons> and <fortifications>. Will you provide them?
strings.refugee_city_3_1_16: I do. Set <stakes> around the camp. And you'll have your reward when it's over.
strings.refugee_city_3_1_2: The <Lord Commander> from Mountain Fort has vowed to eliminate your camp.
strings.refugee_city_3_1_3: I'm so sorry to have to tell you this.
strings.refugee_city_3_1_5: Then we have only one option.
strings.refugee_city_3_1_6: I see. But where will you go?
strings.refugee_city_3_1_7: We're not going anywhere. We'll stay right here — and protect ourselves.
strings.refugee_city_3_1_8: Marquis, that's total madness! You can't stand against trained soldiers from Mountain Fort!
strings.refugee_city_3_1_9: We didn't come all this way, just to become helpless refugees again, Keeper!
strings.refugee_city_3_2_1: Your <stakes> look frightening. It's perfect. Our foes will think twice before attacking us.
strings.refugee_city_3_2_10: I'm feeling too lazy to make them on my own. Maybe I should buy the swords from Koukol...
strings.refugee_city_3_2_2: I spoke to our people: most of them are ready to take up arms to defend each other.
strings.refugee_city_3_2_4: <Alaric> tried to persuade everyone that my plan was meaningless and dangerous.
strings.refugee_city_3_2_5: In his opinion, we either run or die.
strings.refugee_city_3_2_6: The damned coward! I should have banished him long ago! He's spoiling morale, and undermining my credibility...
strings.refugee_city_3_2_7: Anyway, I don't want to discuss it. We need a <rack of swords>. Can you make one?
strings.refugee_city_3_2_9: Then I kindly bid you make haste. Now I must return to my research.
strings.refugee_city_3_3_1: The swords are ready? Perfect! Our people have already mastered their wooden sticks. It's time to practice with swords.
strings.refugee_city_3_3_2: As for me, I've studied some books on the art of siege. We'll soon be entirely ready.
strings.refugee_city_3_3_3: How can I help you any more?
strings.refugee_city_3_3_4: The only chance they have of breaking our defense is to attack unexpectedly. But we can eliminate that threat.
strings.refugee_city_3_3_5: Are you talking about a <viewing tower>?
strings.refugee_city_3_3_6: Exactly. Build it, and Mountain Fort will never be able to touch us. No way.
strings.refugee_city_3_3_8: Go ahead and imagine it's already done.
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_1: Your <viewing tower> is so nice — did you remark its beauty?
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_12: A huge group of soldiers from Town — the <whole army> — just entered Mountain Fort!
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_13: There's no way we can hold off such an attack!
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_14: Master Alaric was right! We have to run before it's too late!
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_16: I hear you. But keep silent for a moment now, please. I don't want everyone to panic.
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_18: I need a little time to think this through. There must be a <solution>! It can't be the end! It can't!
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_19: All this... it can't all be for nothing!
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_2: It's not bad, but I wouldn't call it especially beautiful.
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_20: Keeper, do you have any ideas?
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_23: Both of you, leave me here, please. I must think. I must think. There must be a solution...
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_24: I doubt he needs my compassion. It's better to leave him alone for now.
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_3: It's so much more than a tower. It's a symbol! A symbol of freedom. A symbol of fairness.
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_4: I think your work here is complete, my friend. Lord Commander doesn't have the power to overcome our defenses.
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_5: You've done so much more than we ever expected of you.
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_6: Of course, <this award>, which we pitched in together for you, is so little on balance with your efforts.
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_7: But I hope our eternal gratitude will compensate for the difference.
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_8: Well... gratitude in addition to material things is better than... just gratitude.
strings.refugee_city_3_fin_9: Also, I prepared a speech for such an... wait! Something's wrong!
strings.refugee_cloud_10_1: There're several people around a burned dead woman. They're talking and waiting for someone.
strings.refugee_cloud_10_2: Three vagabonds search the ashes for values.
strings.refugee_cloud_10_3: A woman vagabond finds a strange bundle in the nearby bushes, and runs away with it. Hmm...
strings.refugee_cloud_11_1: A small boy draws smiling faces in soil. Two inquisitors approach him and say something. He runs into his house.
strings.refugee_cloud_11_2: Farmer leaves his home and starts arguing loudly with his visitors. They point to the nearby window from time to time.
strings.refugee_cloud_11_3: In the end, Farmer grabs a pitchfork and confronts them. The inquisitors quickly leave.
strings.refugee_cloud_11_4: A pale and thin woman appears in the door. She looks gravely ill. Farmer embraces her gently, calms her, and leads back inside.
strings.refugee_cloud_12_1: A young Astrologer and a gypsy quickly kiss each other, and then he goes away.
strings.refugee_cloud_12_2: The Gypsy Baron appears. He pushes the woman aside, pulls out a knife, and runs after Astrologer.
strings.refugee_cloud_12_3: The young gypsy yells something and points at her belly.
strings.refugee_cloud_12_4: Then he rips off her necklace and slaps her. She falls down and cries...
strings.refugee_cloud_13_1: The Lord Commander and some Mountain Fort soldiers were here.
strings.refugee_cloud_13_2: The Lord passed sentence. And they hung someone... Yorick! That's how he died!
strings.refugee_cloud_13_3: What the hell... No, they hung two Yoricks!
strings.refugee_cloud_14_1: There was a long line here. Cory, Adam, Miller, Merchant, and five others.
strings.refugee_cloud_14_2: All elegantly dressed, with flowers and gifts. Oh, they're here to woo Rose!
strings.refugee_cloud_14_3: Shepherd appears, pushes everyone to sides, takes Rose in his hands, kisses her lips, and carries her away.
strings.refugee_cloud_15_1: Lots of swords and armor surround Koukol and Snake, who are bargaining violently.
strings.refugee_cloud_15_2: A crowd of gypsies comes up, armed with knives. Koukol runs away.
strings.refugee_cloud_15_3: Snake and the Gypsy Baron shake hands. Snake takes part of the stuff away, and the gypsies take the rest.
strings.refugee_cloud_16_1: Wow, a whole squad of soldiers was here.  Thirty-three guys in black and orange uniforms.
strings.refugee_cloud_16_2: And Inquisitor is with them. He gives them an inspiring speech and sends them to... to capture Clotho?!
strings.refugee_cloud_16_3: The Inquisitor waits for an hour, killing mosquitoes and flies with a huge gilded book.
strings.refugee_cloud_16_4: The Inquisitor departs, accompanied by thirty-three black-and-orange-clad frogs.
strings.refugee_cloud_17_1: Tress was napping beside the fire, surrounded by hundreds of origami paper rabbits. Hmm, this was recent, Tress was already old!
strings.refugee_cloud_17_2: Cory and some man from Town are watching from a distance. The man looks like a doctor.
strings.refugee_cloud_17_3: The doctor leaves. Cory suddenly rushes over to Tress, gathers all the rabbits, and throws them into the fire...
strings.refugee_cloud_17_4: Tress awakens, shouts, and burns his hands trying to save the rabbits from the fire...
strings.refugee_cloud_18_1: An astonishingly fat woman carrying a crowbar is looking for someone. Her face is crimson with fury, and she's breathing heavily.
strings.refugee_cloud_18_2: The Lighthouse Keeper is returning to the Lighthouse, singing a funny song. He's carrying a fishing rod and a bucket full of fish.
strings.refugee_cloud_18_3: He sees the woman, and she sees him. She rushes towards him.
strings.refugee_cloud_18_4: He throws down the rod and bucket, runs towards the cliff, and leaps from it into the sea.
strings.refugee_cloud_19_1: Miss Charm swims in crystal clear water. What a magnificent sight!
strings.refugee_cloud_19_2: Vagner watches Miss Charm from the nearby bushes.
strings.refugee_cloud_19_3: Nearly naked, she returns to the beach. Vagner inhales deeply...
strings.refugee_cloud_19_4: ... and starts writing an inspired poem.
strings.refugee_cloud_20_1: In the center, Beekeeper puts up a mannequin portraying Adam, with targets on his legs and arms.
strings.refugee_cloud_20_2: Beekeeper strikes a gong. Nothing happens.
strings.refugee_cloud_20_3: Beekeeper takes the mannequin away, and brings in Dig. He's happily licking a honey-stick, with targets attached to his body.
strings.refugee_cloud_21_1: Koukol puts several pieces of raw meat on the ground, then whistles.
strings.refugee_cloud_21_2: An old falcon with a broken wing appears from the bushes. He starts swallowing pieces of meat. Koukol smiles kindly.
strings.refugee_cloud_21_3: Koukol pulls out a sandwich and starts chewing. Before he's done, he throws half his cutlet to the falcon.
strings.refugee_cloud_22_1: Bishop knocks on Miller's door. Two quick knocks, a pause, three slow knocks, a pause, and two more quick knocks.
strings.refugee_cloud_22_2: After that, he leaves a small bag of gold in front of the door, then goes to wait around the corner.
strings.refugee_cloud_22_3: Miller comes out, counts the gold, and takes it, leaving a bottle of whiskey in its place.
strings.refugee_cloud_22_4: Bishop examines the bottle, puts it on his head, covers it with his hat, and walks away.
strings.refugee_cloud_23_1: Adam displays several very beautiful vases in front of Merchant.
strings.refugee_cloud_23_2: Merchant examines them thoroughly, frowns, shakes his head, and goes away.
strings.refugee_cloud_23_3: Adam's lower lip shakes. He rushes into his house, and quickly returns with a small rag doll portraying Merchant.
strings.refugee_cloud_23_4: He takes out a pin and starts desperately stabbing the doll with it.
strings.refugee_cloud_24_1: Late at night, Beekeeper is holding a torch, showing Krezvold a parchment with the plans for a Bee Gun, Bee Grenades, and Honeyed Goggles.
strings.refugee_cloud_24_2: Krezvold thinks and nods. Beekeeper shakes his hand, then places on the ground something wrapped in a blanket.
strings.refugee_cloud_24_3: After Beekeeper leaves, Krezvold unwraps the blanket, and gently passes his hand over a gilded cuirass, tarnished by rust.
strings.refugee_cloud_25_1: In the dead of night, three refugees sit around a fire telling scary stories.
strings.refugee_cloud_25_2: They hear a squeal from somewhere nearby! The refugees scramble and run away.
strings.refugee_cloud_25_3: A troubled little hamster passes beside the fire.
strings.refugee_cloud_26_1: It is night. Master Alaric talks to Moneylender, who is peeling an apple.
strings.refugee_cloud_26_2: Moneylender accidentally cuts his finger, and a bead of blood appears on his skin.
strings.refugee_cloud_26_3: Suddenly, master Alaric grabs his arm and holds it tightly. Then he releases it and quickly withdraws.
strings.refugee_cloud_27_1: In the evening, Cook stirs a pot of soup, then she goes to the tents to talk to Teodoro.
strings.refugee_cloud_27_2: The villager Adam appears from the side of the nearby tent. He places a flower with a pink ribbon near the pot, then quietly departs.
strings.refugee_cloud_27_3: Upon her return, Cook is surprised to discover the flower.
strings.refugee_cloud_27_4: Then she smiles, slices the flower into tiny parts, and places them in the pot of soup.
strings.refugee_cook_1_1: Ah, nice man, could you help a defenseless little woman with huge and awful problems?
strings.refugee_cook_1_2: Why not. But only if you tell me every little thing in detail.
strings.refugee_cook_1_3: Oh, dear Keeper, I feel so helpless, so useless! I'm about to cry every moment! I don't want to live!
strings.refugee_cook_1_4a_1: Good, let's talk about it. Is there something you enjoy doing?
strings.refugee_cook_1_4a_2: Of course! I adore cooking raccoon thyroid stew with blackberries and oyster sauce, baked with Tulip flowers soaked in hot cognac!
strings.refugee_cook_1_4a_3: Hmm. Maybe, I could build a <kitchen> for you? Cooking would cure you of your depression.
strings.refugee_cook_1_4a_4: Plus, your skills could be really useful for the other refugees!
strings.refugee_cook_1_4b_1: This <kitchen>... It's so different from the luxury kitchen in my old elite restaurant...
strings.refugee_cook_1_4b_2: When I work here, my hands shake, I get my proportions wrong. I forget even basic recipes!
strings.refugee_cook_1_4b_3: Well, I could <improve it>. That would allow you to cook more effectively and with greater pleasure.
strings.refugee_cook_1_5: Oh, that would be so darling of you! And this improved kitchen will be equal to the luxury kitchen in my former elite restaurant?
strings.refugee_cook_1_6: Hmm... Actually, I can't promise that, but I'll do my best.
strings.refugee_cook_2_1: Oh, thank you, thank you so much! But...
strings.refugee_cook_2_3: This kitchen... It's so different from my luxury kitchen in my former elite restaurant...
strings.refugee_cook_2_4: Maybe you'll be so incredibly darling that...
strings.refugee_cook_2_5: Well, I could <improve it>. That would allow you to cook more effectively and with greater pleasure.
strings.refugee_cook_3_1: I hope it's a little closer now to your ideal.
strings.refugee_cook_3_2: Oh, definitely! My dear Keeper, you're such a wonder! But...
strings.refugee_cook_3_4: There's one thing that's interfering with my complete happiness.
strings.refugee_cook_3_5: There's nothing I have which makes our hard life a little bit... sweeter.
strings.refugee_cook_3_6: I recommend honey for that. And I could even build some <hives> for you.
strings.refugee_cook_3_7: Oh, amazing! If you do that, I... I...
strings.refugee_cook_3_8: I'll share some of my culinary secrets with you!
strings.refugee_cook_4_1: From this moment forward, your life will be much sweeter.
strings.refugee_cook_4_2: Oh, you're such a treasure! I'm so happy! But...
strings.refugee_cook_4_4: But I remember! I promised you to tell my <culinary secrets>!
strings.refugee_cook_4_5: So, what recipes do you want to know?
strings.refugee_d_10_1: "Lands — to donkeys! Factories — ... also to donkeys!"
strings.refugee_d_10_10: "Plus, our rat allies have asked you to make some Jelly of Incredible Power for them."
strings.refugee_d_10_11: "It will make them big and strong, skilled in martial arts, and fond of turtles."
strings.refugee_d_10_12: "And finally, we require a banner! A revolution without a banner is like a Graveyard Keeper without a beard!"
strings.refugee_d_10_14: I only hope that Donkey will leave me alone after their revolution.
strings.refugee_d_10_15: Though I definitely won't refuse a share of the goods stolen by the revolutionaries!
strings.refugee_d_10_2: "1. The donkeys have traded in the battle gear of the donkey, for pink ribbons in their manes."
strings.refugee_d_10_3: "Now they're not just acting like morons, they're also looking like morons."
strings.refugee_d_10_4: "2. When the carriage turned to a pumpkin, the royal vet lost his shoe. That shoe was found by a young and wealthy widow."
strings.refugee_d_10_5: "Today they were married and plan to live happily ever after."
strings.refugee_d_10_6: "In spite of that, you passed the third stage of earning the approval of the ECoPoDP."
strings.refugee_d_10_7: "At last, we're ready for the Revolution!"
strings.refugee_d_10_8: "But first, we need cans of white and black paint. We'll dye our hair with them."
strings.refugee_d_10_9: "Everyone will think we're zebras and no one will realize we're donkeys!"
strings.refugee_d_12_1: Well, at least there's one thing I can be proud of.
strings.refugee_d_12_2: Is there anyone else who has sponsored a socialist revolution using anthropomorphic rats made from magic jelly?
strings.refugee_d_16_1: Sing and dance, my dear comrade! This day will go down in history!
strings.refugee_d_16_10: The Donkey Socialistic Republic knows what gratitude means. So take this <humble gift>.
strings.refugee_d_16_2: <The Revolution is over! We are triumphant!>
strings.refugee_d_16_3: Our <master-exploiter> is captured, and the <noble horses> have been exiled to distant pastures...
strings.refugee_d_16_4: And the <Interim Government> chosen among the most trustworthy donkeys and rats has commenced socialist reforms!!!
strings.refugee_d_16_5: Do I understand correctly — this means you don't need my services any more?
strings.refugee_d_16_6: And I can celebrate the fact?
strings.refugee_d_16_7: Of course not! Though I understand, you must be mad with happiness for us...
strings.refugee_d_16_8: This was only the first and the simplest step! <Worldwide Revolution> awaits!
strings.refugee_d_1_1: Dear comrade, it is my assignment to inform you: <ECoPoDP>, in a plenary meeting, made the decision...
strings.refugee_d_1_11: Then we'll burn down your home, graveyard, garden, and Church.
strings.refugee_d_1_12: And worst of all, you'll be publicly reprimanded and placed on the <Party's blacklist>.
strings.refugee_d_1_14: We're glad you've agreed to help. Now come closer and listen carefully.
strings.refugee_d_1_15: As you realize, this is all top secret. We'll communicate <via notes>.
strings.refugee_d_1_16: Notes? And... how are you going to write notes?
strings.refugee_d_1_17: Those who know less sleep better. And I wouldn't recommend smelling them.
strings.refugee_d_1_18: First: prepare and send to our post office a <cookbook> for our friend — the rat chief.
strings.refugee_d_1_19: He loves cuisine. And the success of the revolution will be impossible without the rats' help.
strings.refugee_d_1_20: Second: send to our post office <5 red apples>, to raise the morale of the oppressed Donkey Commune. You must...
strings.refugee_d_1_21: Wait, I have no way to send all this stuff discreetly! You said this is top secret! Therefore...
strings.refugee_d_1_22: Therefore it's your responsibility to create and install <a special box for contraband>!
strings.refugee_d_1_23: You will be stuffing all the contraband inside the box.
strings.refugee_d_1_24: And then I or other party members will take them away under cover of night!
strings.refugee_d_1_26: Don't worry, you'll manage it. I believe in you!
strings.refugee_d_1_3: <ECoPoDP>! The Executive Committee of the Party of the Donkeys' Proletariat!
strings.refugee_d_1_4: You are addressing <its General Secretary>, by the way.
strings.refugee_d_1_6: So... the ECoPoDP has decided to give you one last chance to rehabilitate yourself in the eyes of enlightened labor!
strings.refugee_d_1_9: Our Party has reached the phase of active preparation for <revolutionary upheaval>. And your role will be key.
strings.refugee_d_3_10: Pff, they just said money is harmful!
strings.refugee_d_3_13: "So you can keep the money for yourself, and send us (faith)5, that we may maintain our trust in a bright future for donkeys!"
strings.refugee_d_3_15: If their EDoPoP won't pay me for my help, I'll put poison carrots into their donkey box!
strings.refugee_d_3_2: "1. The rats chief can't read, but he enjoyed the pictures in your cookbook."
strings.refugee_d_3_3: "So he ripped them out and ate them."
strings.refugee_d_3_4: "2. There weren't enough apples, so the donkeys fought each other over them, and there were a lot of casualties."
strings.refugee_d_3_6: "You have passed the first stage of earning the approval of the ECoPoDP."
strings.refugee_d_3_7: "Continue. You'll receive stolen bank checks and pieces of jewelry via the box."
strings.refugee_d_3_8: "Write and send aphorisms about the harmfulness of money, and we'll put them in the letters instead of the checks and jewelry."
strings.refugee_d_3_9: "Also, sell the jewelry and send the money to us. This will aid us in our great endeavor."
strings.refugee_d_4_1: Meh, it's impossible to cash them, they're personalized. They're nothing more than kindling.
strings.refugee_d_4_2: Who said there's no money in revolutions? Merchant will be delighted to see this stuff.
strings.refugee_d_5_1_1: "Dishonest people shouldn't be rich. And honest people are allowed to be rich. And dishonest."
strings.refugee_d_5_1_2: "The truly wealthy are those who are satisfied with less. We'll take the rest."
strings.refugee_d_5_1_3: "Those who have plenty are not wealthy. It's those who give that are truly wealthy. Those who give a lot!"
strings.refugee_d_5_1_4: "We live not for wealth. We live for happiness, and especially for making others happy."
strings.refugee_d_5_1_5: "There're few people who can tolerate wealth. Other people's wealth, that is."
strings.refugee_d_5_1_6: "Money won't buy you love. The only exception is our love."
strings.refugee_d_5_1_7: "Your heirs looking forward to your death? Teach them a lesson!"
strings.refugee_d_6_10: "One we can exchange for the luxurious carriage of the royal veterinarian."
strings.refugee_d_6_11: "At midnight his carriage will turn back into a pumpkin, and our master will look like a fool in front of the whole royal court!"
strings.refugee_d_6_13: Hmm... I don't know how to make donkey gear, or how to enchant pumpkins.
strings.refugee_d_6_14: Though I know people who can: Krezvold and Clotho.
strings.refugee_d_6_2: "1. ECoPoDP liked your aphorisms very much!"
strings.refugee_d_6_3: "So we have decided to adopt them as the Constitution of the coming Worldwide Donkey Socialistic Republic"
strings.refugee_d_6_4: "2. After consuming the faith, everyday donkeys became greatly inspired, even believing that all donkeys are equal."
strings.refugee_d_6_5: "We have had to remind them with our hooves that some donkeys are more equal than others."
strings.refugee_d_6_6: "Thus you have passed the second stage of earning the approval of the ECoPoDP."
strings.refugee_d_6_7: "Keep going. We need donkey combat equipment in the contraband box."
strings.refugee_d_6_8: "Your task is to assemble and to deliver battle horseshoes and iron unicorn horns."
strings.refugee_d_7_1: Clotho, could you <enchant a pumpkin>? In particular, can you turn it into an impressive and luxurious carriage?
strings.refugee_d_7_10: Obviously I should have started with that question.
strings.refugee_d_7_2: Oh, my boy... Your inexperience in affairs of the heart is so touching! But listen to an old lady's advice.
strings.refugee_d_7_3: Do you really think that you can impress a modern young woman with a carriage?!
strings.refugee_d_7_4: Hold on! Clotho, it's not for me, and I'm not trying to impress any...
strings.refugee_d_7_5: My boy, modern women want things that are far more refined than carriages!
strings.refugee_d_7_6: What an awful time we live in! There's no moral decency!
strings.refugee_d_7_7: Modern women require... Love! Care! Maintenance! Fidelity! Can you imagine it?
strings.refugee_d_7_8: Yeah, it's awful. The fall of civilization. But I'm still asking you to do it...
strings.refugee_d_8_1: Could you help me out, Krezvold? I need you to assemble... <some battle horseshoes and iron unicorn horns>.
strings.refugee_d_8_10: And the same amount again because you spoiled my mood!
strings.refugee_d_8_11: Okay, okay, I agree, just don't be angry. And accept my apologies.
strings.refugee_d_8_13: Come back tomorrow. Or better yet, don't come back at all.
strings.refugee_d_8_3: Did Horadric put you up to this?
strings.refugee_d_8_5: Because he's the one always curing my deep monthly depressions with his idiotic pranks!
strings.refugee_d_8_6: No, it's completely my own idea.
strings.refugee_d_8_7: So it's you who wants to cure my deep monthly depression with idiotic pranks?! Arrr!
strings.refugee_d_8_8: Wait! Wait! I meant the other thing! It's not a prank! I actually need these horseshoes and horns!
strings.refugee_d_9_2: Ready. First class work, too! As always.
strings.refugee_d_9_4: Yep. All the other components were spares. So I'm using them at the house.
strings.refugee_d_9_8: Then take this junk and go away. I urgently need to get drunk as a skunk.
strings.refugee_lender_1_1: Moneylender greets new guests! Moneylender knows all his guests' desires!
strings.refugee_lender_1_10: With an insignificant, tiny commission of <1% per day>.
strings.refugee_lender_1_11a: Just 1%? I agree. Give me the money.
strings.refugee_lender_1_11b: I'll think about it. See ya.
strings.refugee_lender_1_2: Gold, silver... They're already waiting for you, just reach out your hand!
strings.refugee_lender_1_3: Moneylender will drown you in money!
strings.refugee_lender_1_4: Just give your <valuables> — especially your gold valuables — to Moneylender, and the world's wealth is yours!
strings.refugee_lender_1_5: And if I have no valuables?
strings.refugee_lender_1_6: Oh, Moneylender is sooo kind, he gives you his gold nevertheless!
strings.refugee_lender_1_7: Are you serious? That sounds great!
strings.refugee_lender_1_9: Of course, you must be kind to Moneylender as well. And return to him one day the gold you've borrowed.
strings.refugee_lender_2: Ah, you changed your mind! Your bag of gold is already here, in Moneylender's left pocket!
strings.refugee_lender_2_1a: Give it to me. 1% isn't really much.
strings.refugee_lender_2_1b: Actually, I just wanted to trade.
strings.refugee_lender_2_1c: I need to think a bit more.
strings.refugee_lender_3: Ready to return your debt? Moneylender doesn't hurry you, but the percentages are accumulating. Drop by drop.
strings.refugee_lender_4_1: Moneylender feels sorry for disturbing you, but we have a little unfinished business.
strings.refugee_lender_4_3: Oh, yes, I'd already forgotten about it...
strings.refugee_lender_4_4: Unfortunately, in the current situation, Moneylender is forced to insist on its immediate return, plus all interest.
strings.refugee_lender_4_5b: Maybe I'll give it to you after you come back?
strings.refugee_lender_4_6: Just imagine what an enormous sum you'll receive thanks to 1% a day!
strings.refugee_s26_2_1: Clotho, do you know where <Misty Quagmire> is?
strings.refugee_s26_2_10: She's not herself, what should I do?!
strings.refugee_s26_2_11: A rotten-winged demon haunts you, whispering your name in the gloom...
strings.refugee_s26_2_12: Asking, again and again, for a blood sacrifice...
strings.refugee_s26_2_14: Look upon me, Ancient God! Look upon me and weep, though I care not for your tears!
strings.refugee_s26_2_17: What? Keeper? What a pleasant surprise! You visit me so rarely..
strings.refugee_s26_2_18: How can this old lady help you?
strings.refugee_s26_2_19: She doesn't remember anything. But, Jesus — what was that?
strings.refugee_s26_2_20: You know what, I'll be back later.
strings.refugee_s26_2_3: Oh my dear, I beg you, don't go there! Don't go there!
strings.refugee_s26_2_4: The Heart of the Swamps. Veiled in darkness, full of suffering. It will consume you.
strings.refugee_s26_2_5: Dark rituals have defiled that ancient land... No more beauty... No purity... No peace...
strings.refugee_s26_2_6: Like an innocent soul caught in a web of vices... Like a fragile butterfly, reborn as a voracious parasite...
strings.refugee_s26_2_7: Tell me — do you feel its pain?! Tell me!
strings.refugee_s26_3_1: Marquis, this may not be the most pleasant topic for you, but...
strings.refugee_s26_3_10: That's just a matter of approach. Besides, <ghouls don't exist>.
strings.refugee_s26_3_11: Like smart people say, overconfidence is a slow and insidious killer, Keeper.
strings.refugee_s26_3_12: But if you insist, we can return to this issue. After you accomplish your part of our bargain.
strings.refugee_s26_3_2: I'd like you to show me the path to <Misty Quagmire>.
strings.refugee_s26_3_6: What do you want with that place?
strings.refugee_s26_3_7: That's a big secret, marquis. But it would be a great help.
strings.refugee_s26_3_8: The Quagmire is not a thing that helps. It can only destroy.
strings.refugee_s26_3_9: There's no place more evil, or more terrifying. It's like asking a ghoul for help.
strings.refugee_s27_1_1: Graveyard Keeper! In the name of <King Joe VII>, you are under arrest!
strings.refugee_s27_1_10: You're goddamn right, innkeeper! It'll be boring at first: interrogations, court trial, sentencing...
strings.refugee_s27_1_11: But the ending will be spectacular! A <double burning>! Woo-hoo! And...
strings.refugee_s27_1_12: Ugh, that nasty bitch is with him!
strings.refugee_s27_1_13: It is so splendid, milady, that you agreed to dine with me today!
strings.refugee_s27_1_14: Ah, Lord Commander, how could I resist your charms? I'm sure it will be delightful!
strings.refugee_s27_1_15: No doubt, my dear. So let's finish here quickly: Graveyard Keeper and — Harodric, is it? Your sentence is...
strings.refugee_s27_1_16: Sentence? You begin the trial with the sentence?!
strings.refugee_s27_1_17: Why not? Isn't the case clear enough?
strings.refugee_s27_1_18: Horadric and the Graveyard Keeper concealed and aided the fugitives heretics.
strings.refugee_s27_1_19: And the sentence is obvious: <death by burning>. With the right to appeal the sentence afterwards.
