strings.refugee_s27_1_2: Oh oh! Hmm. Listen, guys, maybe we can slow things down here, and... figure out a solution to this that's good for everybody?
strings.refugee_s27_1_20: You know, it's not so easy to burn me. They already tried once.
strings.refugee_s27_1_21: I... we didn't help the fugitives!
strings.refugee_s27_1_22: Poor naive Keeper... Do you think that <my spell> just changed the way you smell?
strings.refugee_s27_1_23: Alas! At any time, day or night, I could look upon the world with your eyes, listen with your ears, even smell with your nose...
strings.refugee_s27_1_25: By the way, try to remember: dried cloves and lilies don't go well with the scent of rotting corpses!
strings.refugee_s27_1_26: Ahem. As for the sentence: according to regulation 3523 "Regarding heretics", paragraph S-27, you will be burned! Any questions?
strings.refugee_s27_1_27: I have one. According to paragraph M-88, paragraph S-27 only applies if the defendants have hair on their feet, the crime involves cattle, and during odd years.
strings.refugee_s27_1_3: The <Lord Commander>, the King's Plenipotentiary of the northern lands, awaits you for the trial!
strings.refugee_s27_1_30: My dear lord, this is nonsense! Just do it, and I promise you the most magnificent date of your life!
strings.refugee_s27_1_31: Just the two of us! No heretics and their helpers, no rowdy soldiers, no stinky, tongue-tied, creepy hunchbacks...
strings.refugee_s27_1_32: Hmm... my lord, you could certainly do it despite the laws, but what would our King say?
strings.refugee_s27_1_33: Silence, you fool! The King will never learn of it!
strings.refugee_s27_1_34: Are you sure? One of the stinky, tongue-tied, creepy hunchbacks you mentioned might tell him. For instance.
strings.refugee_s27_1_35: My lord, your... jester is unbearable! And that smell! Even my <unique freshener> couldn't cope with his smell. Banish him!
strings.refugee_s27_1_37: Keeper and Hodarick — you are free to go. But warn your fellow fugitive friends:
strings.refugee_s27_1_38: <They and their whole camp will be eliminated>! You have the solemn word of the Lord Commander!
strings.refugee_s27_1_4: Oh crap. But I have a right to a lawyer, right? And I'll allowed to remain silent?
strings.refugee_s27_1_5: Dudes, sounds like he's asking for a beating!
strings.refugee_s27_1_6: Wait, I agree, I agree! Oh, how uncivilized...
strings.refugee_s27_1_7: Are you excited, Keeper? You should be. You've got a problem. A big problem! Heh heh!
strings.refugee_s27_1_9: I don't know yet, but it's definitely nothing good.
strings.refugee_s27_2_1: Shhh! Do you hear that? We have disturbed this place. It's awakening...
strings.refugee_s27_2_10: It's apparently the leg of <spirit from the Dungeon>. It's still here, buried in the soil.
strings.refugee_s27_2_11: <Six vampires> stood here in a semicircle. It must have been some kind of <ritual>.
strings.refugee_s27_2_12: <The woman in the black and gold cloak> was here. She was carrying a book.
strings.refugee_s27_2_13: It must be the <Necronomicon> that Marquis Teodoro Sr. later found here.
strings.refugee_s27_2_14: <The Vampire Queen>. She performed the ritual. But what was its purpose?
strings.refugee_s27_2_15: Only riddles and no answers! I need more information!
strings.refugee_s27_2_17: There was a <woman> hiding here! I can't quite make her out. A spy?
strings.refugee_s27_2_18: The vampires attacked her. She's lying there motionless. Is she dead?
strings.refugee_s27_2_19: The Vampire Queen approaches. She sees the woman. She drops the Necronomicon...
strings.refugee_s27_2_2: I wouldn't say I'm afraid, or anything... But...  try to make it quick.
strings.refugee_s27_2_20: Six spots of burned grass. The vampires. <The Queen burned them alive>!
strings.refugee_s27_2_21: I don't understand... It's meaningless... It's madness...
strings.refugee_s27_2_22: <The charred shoe of a vampire>. Perhaps some Memory tincture would make sense of this?
strings.refugee_s27_2_23: Best do that somewhere else. My teeth are chattering from the cold here.
strings.refugee_s27_2_24: I'm ready to go back, marquis.
strings.refugee_s27_2_26: There is no return, human... Face this, and accept your destiny...
strings.refugee_s27_2_27: Marquis? What are you talking about?
strings.refugee_s27_2_28: I have been waiting for so long...
strings.refugee_s27_2_29: Retribution... Mankind's greatest obsession...  And the greatest weapon against it...
strings.refugee_s27_2_30: I don't know who you are, but leave his body! We didn't do anything bad to you!
strings.refugee_s27_2_31: I was pure and innocent... until the humans came...
strings.refugee_s27_2_32: You killed each other... again and again... bathing me in your blood...
strings.refugee_s27_2_33: Filling me with your vices... your intolerance... your hatred...
strings.refugee_s27_2_34: But I struggled... I resisted... resisted... until when the woman came to me...
strings.refugee_s27_2_35: ... and her dark rituals mutilated and defiled me!
strings.refugee_s27_2_36: And now... I will share my pain... with you...
strings.refugee_s27_2_37: Wait! I have an offer for you, Quagmire! A very handsome offer!
strings.refugee_s27_2_38: What's the use of punishing just us two, if you could punish hundreds — or thousands?
strings.refugee_s27_2_39: Just solve a <simple riddle>, and I'll bring them to you! Otherwise, you'll let us go free.
strings.refugee_s27_2_4: This Quagmire is a really creepy place. Let's hope this is worth it.
strings.refugee_s27_2_41: I will listen to your simple riddle, human...
strings.refugee_s27_2_42: Great! Here you go: "What's the principle of the Large Hadron Collider?"
strings.refugee_s27_2_46: What... what happened? I... I'm so weak. My body, it's like I'm full of lead...
strings.refugee_s27_2_47: We're out of here, marquis! Now!
strings.refugee_s27_2_5: The Quagmire whispers my name. It remembers my father. It remembers everything...
strings.refugee_s27_2_6: It senses my fears, and blows upon them like embers in the oven.
strings.refugee_s27_2_7: Hurry, Keeper. Please. The voices are getting louder...
strings.refugee_s27_2_8: The air got colder... The magic of the Eye probably attracted the Quagmire's attention.  Damn...
strings.refugee_s27_2_9: There was magical <ice fire> here. I see blue flames consuming a <bone leg>.
strings.refugee_s28_1: I can still hear her in my head. She's whispering that I don't deserve to live...
strings.refugee_s28_11: I have to hurry. That wasn't the only ambush she laid.
strings.refugee_s28_12: I need to make some <Memory tincture>, as much as possible — and check out <the shoe from the Quagmire>!
strings.refugee_s28_13: Someone really wants to get rid of me!
strings.refugee_s28_14: Hey! Is that all you got?!
strings.refugee_s28_15: This is getting worrying... How many more ambushes will I survive?
strings.refugee_s28_2: I'm a bad person. A bad commander. I'm useless and helpless. My parents died because of me...
strings.refugee_s28_3: You just need a rest, marquis. A little sleep and you'll feel...
strings.refugee_s28_5: Just when I thought the worst was behind us... Marquis, run!
strings.refugee_s28_6: And leave you alone against them? That's...
strings.refugee_s28_7: You in no condition to help! Run, I said!
strings.refugee_s28_8: I bet the <Vampire Queen> sent them!
strings.refugee_s28_9: She's afraid, and that means I'm getting close at last!
strings.refugee_s28_q1_1: Do you remember your parents well?
strings.refugee_s28_q1_2: I was 6 years old when they were executed.
strings.refugee_s28_q1_3: But yes, I remember them. Especially <my father>.
strings.refugee_s28_q1_4: I remember his warm palms... and his extraordinary glasses, which were always falling off his nose...
strings.refugee_s28_q1_5: He quietly muttered as he worked... And drew little funny faces in corners of his work...
strings.refugee_s28_q1_6: I even remember the strange mechanical seagull he crafted for me, that cawed like a crow!
strings.refugee_s28_q2_2: Typically, aristocrats study at <Town University>. But I chose another path.
strings.refugee_s28_q2_3: I had little interest in their endless lectures about faith and patriotism. I desired real knowledge.
strings.refugee_s28_q2_4: So where did you get this knowledge from?
strings.refugee_s28_q2_5: I borrowed it from my <dead father>.
strings.refugee_s28_q2_6: His notes. His drafts. His books. Everything I could find.
strings.refugee_s28_q2_7: After all, he'd been officially recognized as the best University scientist ever!
strings.refugee_s28_q3_10: My pain and hatred are my evidence, Keeper.
strings.refugee_s28_q3_2: You already know that. The Inquisition sentenced them to fire for <heresy and the practice of black magic>.
strings.refugee_s28_q3_3: According to the court's notes, the <Necronomicon> obsessed my parents and drove them insane.
strings.refugee_s28_q3_4: And what do you personally think about it?
strings.refugee_s28_q3_5: I think there were too many people who wanted to get rid of my father.
strings.refugee_s28_q3_6: They envied his intelligence, his success, his fame... His very existence reminded them of their insignificance.
strings.refugee_s28_q3_7: His downfall was only a question of time.
strings.refugee_s28_q3_8: He was doomed. Town has no need of such people. It requires <obedient mediocrity>.
strings.refugee_s28_q3_9: And... do you have any evidence?
strings.refugee_s28_q4_2: It's one of those illnesses that torture patients and keep their doctors well fed.
strings.refugee_s28_q4_3: No treatment exists. My father suffered the same.
strings.refugee_s28_q4_4: He invented <this device>. Look, you spray it into your mouth... And the trouble passes.
strings.refugee_s28_q4_5: An inhaler! In my world... uh... in my native land, that's quite a common thing.
strings.refugee_s28_q4_6: I hope it's a happier place than our own, wherever it is.
strings.refugee_s28_q4_7: I asked them, I begged them, but they wouldn't let me take this thing to the prison...
strings.refugee_s28_q5_2: I noticed that you're not very friendly with <master Alaric>.
strings.refugee_s28_q5_3: I don't mean to offend you, but my relationship with Alaric is not your business, Keeper.
strings.refugee_s28_q5_4: I will never forgive him — that's all you need to know.
strings.refugee_s28_q6_2: They don't exist anymore. I destroyed everything.
strings.refugee_s28_q6_3: Seriously? But why? They could have helped lots of people.
strings.refugee_s28_q6_4: How many people helped my father, when the inquisitors led him to the fire, tormented and broken?!
strings.refugee_s28_q6_5: Even his colleagues, University professors... his dear friends...
strings.refugee_s28_q6_6: They didn't even come! Not to father's cell, nor to Execution Square!
strings.refugee_s28_q6_7: But five years ago, they declared that my father's work belongs to the University!
strings.refugee_s28_q6_8: Of course, the courts took their side.
strings.refugee_s28_q6_9: So I brought it to them... <Five boxes of ash>.
strings.refugee_s28_q7_2: For many long years, I searched for revenge, for a way to destroy the <Inquisition>.
strings.refugee_s28_q7_3: I might even have joined the <Cult> in the end.
strings.refugee_s28_q7_4: But my destiny lay in a different direction.
strings.refugee_s28_q7_6: Some inquisitors broke into my home and captured me. Threw me to a cell.
strings.refugee_s28_q7_7: They explained nothing. They just said that <my execution> would be soon, and went away.
strings.refugee_s28_q7_8: There were six of us, sentenced to death for unknown reasons!
strings.refugee_s28_q8_2: One day I will return, and do all the things that I swore in the cell that I'd do.
strings.refugee_s28_q8_3: The Inquisition, the royal authority, the bureaucracy... <they must perish>.
strings.refugee_s28_q8_4: Revolution. Hmm, he reminds me of someone...
strings.refugee_s28_q8_5: No more authority... no more officials... no more inquisitors...
strings.refugee_s28_q8_6: That means <war>. Violence. Suffering. Lots of innocent victims. Is that what you want?
strings.refugee_s28_q8_7: If it's for the greater good, yes. As many victims as it takes.
strings.refugee_s28_q8_8: Well... At least... thanks for your honesty.
strings.refugee_s29_1_10: Carl, brother, please... Remember who you are. Who we all are.
strings.refugee_s29_1_11: Face it. <We're outcasts>. Freaks. People will never accept us. No matter what you do.
strings.refugee_s29_1_12: No, they will. I'll prove it, you'll see!
strings.refugee_s29_1_13: I'm tired of being a nobody, brother...
strings.refugee_s29_1_15: You'll see! When I get another loan and buy that cool <post office with the donkeys>...
strings.refugee_s29_1_16: When I'll buy some noble horses, organize the right advertising, and get my first big orders from the aristocracy...
strings.refugee_s29_1_17: You'll see! You will all see!
strings.refugee_s29_1_18: <Vampire Carl>, who intends to buy a post office with donkeys and noble horses... Hmm, very interesting!
strings.refugee_s29_1_4: No, <Carl>, it won't work out! Can't you see it's completely idiotic?
strings.refugee_s29_1_5: I agree, it's totally lame! Even worse than your idea to cook up and drink blood substitute!
strings.refugee_s29_1_6: Guys, guys, this won't be like last time. I've really thought this one through!
strings.refugee_s29_1_7: You say it every time! Every time, <Carl>!
strings.refugee_s29_1_8: Dudes, cut the chit-chat. We're late already. She'll be furious. Carl, get dressed and let's go!
strings.refugee_s29_1_9: It'll all work out! We're gonna earn some serious money. And we won't need to work for her ever again!
strings.refugee_s29_2_1: In case you're here to mock on my disability, I remind you that I don't care.
strings.refugee_s29_2_2: Did you want <your leg> back? Here it is.
strings.refugee_s29_2_3: Oh, I can't believe it! My leg! My precious leg! My precious! Oh, how I have missed you!
strings.refugee_s29_2_4: This is the best day since the day of my induction into the <priesthood of the Ancient God>!
strings.refugee_s29_2_5: I'm so happy! Now I'll be able to ask that babe Poppy for a slow waltz!
strings.refugee_s29_2_6: I'm glad to hear it! But what about "I care about nothing and despite everything"?
strings.refugee_s30_10: That won't make a dent. He's hopeless. But I like your way of thinking.
strings.refugee_s30_11: I'll bring him to you as soon as possible.
strings.refugee_s30_12: I'll bring him to you. But understand that I'll only be able to do it <after our victory>.
strings.refugee_s30_2: Listen to me, it's really important! What's the name of your owner?
strings.refugee_s30_2_old: Listen to me, it's really important! What's the name of your owner?
strings.refugee_s30_4: Pff... no! His real name! What do his clients call him? You must know!
strings.refugee_s30_4_old: Pff... no! His real name! What do his clients call him? You must know!
strings.refugee_s30_5: Let me remember... Mmm... <master Carl>, I believe.
strings.refugee_s30_5_old: Let me remember... Mmm... <master Carl>, I believe.
strings.refugee_s30_7: I need to talk to him. Urgently! It's a matter of life and death!
strings.refugee_s30_8: Wait! It smells suspiciously like some kind of <counter-revolutionary activity>!
strings.refugee_s30_9: Why would you think that?! I was merely... preparing a lecture for him. "Private property is the worst sin".
strings.refugee_s31_1: At last! <Vampire Carl>! That guy who will reveal all the secrets!
strings.refugee_s31_10: That's good to hear. So tell me everything you know about the <woman in the black and gold cloak>!
strings.refugee_s31_14: You can torture me, you can kill me — but that's my final word!
strings.refugee_s31_16: Keeper, I'm sorry, but I just can't bear it. You really call this nonsense an interrogation?
strings.refugee_s31_17: Stop making a fool of yourself and find a professional!
strings.refugee_s31_18: Well, okay. I'm sure <Shepherd> will be happy to help with this.
strings.refugee_s31_2: I was always sure that one fine day you'd start cutting up living people.
strings.refugee_s31_3: I hope you were smart enough to eliminate all the witnesses of the kidnapping?
strings.refugee_s31_4: He's a vampire, and I'm going to interrogate him. Do you mind?
strings.refugee_s31_6: Where am I? Who are you?
strings.refugee_s31_8: I'll sign anything! I'll confess — whatever you want! Just don't hurt me!
strings.refugee_s31_9: This'll be even easier than I thought!
strings.refugee_s32_1: If you're not too busy, would you mind helping me <interrogate a vampire>?
strings.refugee_s32_10: I know these tactics. You'll be the good guy.
strings.refugee_s32_11: Are you a fool, apprentice?! I will be the very bad guy!
strings.refugee_s32_2: Why not? There's nothing untoward about helping an <aspiring Undead Hunter> at the beginning of his career.
strings.refugee_s32_3: An aspiring Undead Hunter? Oh, it seems we have a misunderstanding here...
strings.refugee_s32_4: Don't be embarrassed, I know you've always dreamt of it! Just like me in my youth.
strings.refugee_s32_6: I know what you wish to ask. Yes, I agree to be <your mentor>!
strings.refugee_s32_8: And your first lesson shall be — the interrogation of a vampire!
strings.refugee_s32_9: Listen to the <secret tactics> of the Order! You will be the bad guy, and I...
strings.refugee_s32_new_greeting: Ah, my entirely inexperienced and naive apprentice! Are you prepared for a mortally dangerous second lesson?
strings.refugee_s32_new_greeting_1: Almost. I'd like to pray first.
strings.refugee_s32_new_greeting_2: Almost. I need to wash up before something important like that.
strings.refugee_s32_new_greeting_3: Almost. I have to check on my equipment.
strings.refugee_s33_1: Not bad! This place reminds me the Order's break room. Is that skull a trophy from the battlefield?
strings.refugee_s33_10: Eat it right now — that's an order!
strings.refugee_s33_12: Good! Now lean over the vampire and exhale!
strings.refugee_s33_16: Perfect! We just need to increase the concentration! Apprentice, eat two more!
strings.refugee_s33_17: Listen, for God's sake, I can't anymore. Let's try something else!
strings.refugee_s33_18: Okay, time for my favorite. Ahem... E-flat...
strings.refugee_s33_19: <"My love, your eyes are similar to beeeeeet...">
strings.refugee_s33_2: Skull? Er... no, that's just a <trinket>.
strings.refugee_s33_21: AAA! Stop singing! I'll talk, I'll talk!
strings.refugee_s33_23: Did I hear you right — you called me a trinket?
strings.refugee_s33_23_old: Did I hear you right — you called me a trinket?
strings.refugee_s33_24: Gerry, listen, you'll have all my profound apologies, but later! I really need to hurry!
strings.refugee_s33_24_old: Gerry, listen, you'll have all my profound apologies, but later! I really need to hurry!
strings.refugee_s33_25: Apologies? Man, can't you see it? — It's a cool business idea!
strings.refugee_s33_25_old: Apologies? Man, can't you see it? — It's a cool business idea!
strings.refugee_s33_26: You could cover me with gold paint and sell me at the <Town market>. And then I just pop back to you after they're gone!
strings.refugee_s33_26_old: You could cover me with gold paint and sell me at the <Town market>. And then I just pop back to you after they're gone!
strings.refugee_s33_27: We could do it over and over. We'll make tons of money!
strings.refugee_s33_27_old: We could do it over and over. We'll make tons of money!
strings.refugee_s33_3: A trinket that I have asked to stop winking!
strings.refugee_s33_4: Let's try something easy for the starters. I should think I have <some garlic> somewhere...
strings.refugee_s33_5: And here it is. Watch and learn, my apprentice.
strings.refugee_s33_6: It's your last chance, you vampiric spawn! Will you speak?
strings.refugee_s33_8: Good. Then let's begin! Apprentice, take a head of garlic and eat it.
strings.refugee_s33_9: What the hell! Again?! You must be joking!
strings.refugee_s33_q: The woman in the black and gold cloak. Is she really the Vampire Queen?
strings.refugee_s33_q0: Sure. And I'm the Ghoul Sultan. No, man — vampires are all anarchists!
strings.refugee_s33_q1_2: Who knows? She didn't tell us anything about herself. Though obviously she was a <powerful magician>.
strings.refugee_s33_q1_3: She wasn't from Town. She spoke like... like she was accustomed to ruling. And she used old-fashioned words.
strings.refugee_s33_q1_4: Besides, she definitely had some serious mental problems.
strings.refugee_s33_q2_1: Why did you work for her?
strings.refugee_s33_q2_2: We had an <arrangement>. We do what she wants, then she cures us of our blood thirst.
strings.refugee_s33_q2_3: But instead, she destroyed <our whole clan>. All my brothers!
strings.refugee_s33_q2_4: Four of us were turned to jawbones during our first attempt to kill the fourth Keeper.
strings.refugee_s33_q2_5: I told my brothers that it was a <bad sign>, and we should stop working with her, but they didn't listen!
strings.refugee_s33_q3_10: But when she approached the spy's body, something incredible happened.
strings.refugee_s33_q3_11: She yelled! What strange yelling it was!
strings.refugee_s33_q3_12: And then she burned them all alive. She killed all my brothers, who were only doing as she commanded!
strings.refugee_s33_q3_12_old: And then she burned them all alive. She killed all my brothers, who were only doing as she commanded!
strings.refugee_s33_q3_13: I couldn't help them. I was so scared, I can't remember, just that I ran, and ran...
strings.refugee_s33_q3_13_old: I couldn't help them. I was so scared, I can't remember, just that I ran, and ran...
strings.refugee_s33_q3_14: Hm... that spy... the woman with red hair... I know a <local woman with red hair>... Maybe she survived?
strings.refugee_s33_q3_14_old: Hm... that spy... the woman with red hair... I know a <local woman with red hair>... Maybe she survived?
strings.refugee_s33_q3_15: That's all I wanted to know. You can go.
strings.refugee_s33_q3_16: Seriously? I can go? Are you sure?
strings.refugee_s33_q3_2: Powerful black magic. And its purpose was to <kill the fourth Keeper>.
strings.refugee_s33_q3_3: It succeeded, as far as I know: the ritual was completed, then there was the <Great Blast>, and the Keeper died.
strings.refugee_s33_q3_4: Amazing! That's the answer! <She killed the Keeper to trigger the Ancient Curse!>
strings.refugee_s33_q3_5: That day I was a little late getting to the ritual. But that saved my life.
strings.refugee_s33_q3_7: I saw everything while I was hiding in a bush.
strings.refugee_s33_q3_8: There was a spy, a <woman with red hair>.
strings.refugee_s33_q3_9: Our "mistress" sent my brothers to kill her. And they did.
strings.refugee_s34_1: Chain, have you ever been to <Misty Quagmire>? Maybe 30 years ago, for instance?
strings.refugee_s34_10: Chain seems to be that woman with the red hair. I need to try again. She knows something.
strings.refugee_s34_12: Chain, I'm sorry I was so rude. But this mystery must be solved.
strings.refugee_s34_13: I see that this is upsetting you, but please, trust me. I promise that I won't let anything bad happen to you.
strings.refugee_s34_17: I'm trying to stop the <Ancient Curse>, Chain. It's extremely important.
strings.refugee_s34_18: That <woman in the black and gold cloak> killed the fourth Keeper and started the Curse.
strings.refugee_s34_19: And she's the only one who can stop it.
strings.refugee_s34_25: Because... because I don't want to see <my sister> killed!
strings.refugee_s34_26: Clotho? But who would want to kill her?
strings.refugee_s34_27: They all would. The citizens, the villagers... even Horadric... If they find out what she did...
strings.refugee_s34_30: She started telling the story. I have to make her continue.
strings.refugee_s34_31: Maybe Horadric knows where she might be...
strings.refugee_s34_31_2: Chain, what was it that <your sister Clotho> did?
strings.refugee_s34_33: All those things you mentioned. She killed the fourth Keeper and started the Curse.
strings.refugee_s34_34: What?! You mean the woman in a black and gold cloak was Clotho?!
strings.refugee_s34_35: But that's impossible! Clotho is just a harmless old witch. And she couldn't have ordered them to kill you...
strings.refugee_s34_36: It's my fault, Keeper! Everything that happened was my fault!
strings.refugee_s34_37: I abandoned my sister when she needed me the most. I betrayed her, like others.
strings.refugee_s34_38: I enjoyed a happy life with Horadric, while Clotho grew mad in loneliness and despair among the Swamps.
strings.refugee_s34_39: And when we met again, after many years, I discovered that... my sister had become a monster.
strings.refugee_s34_4: It's not that strange. Just answer "yes" or "no", that's all.
strings.refugee_s34_41: Darkness possessed her. She'd become obsessed with dreams of bloody vengeance — with <the destruction of the whole world!>
strings.refugee_s34_42: She kicked me out of her home. But I wouldn't go away. I just couldn't get over it...
strings.refugee_s34_43: And when she went to the Quagmire, I followed her in secret.
strings.refugee_s34_44: Yes, she ordered her vampires to kill me... but that's only because she didn't recognize me!
strings.refugee_s34_45: A part of her still loved me, I'm sure of it.
strings.refugee_s34_46: That explains one thing. When she saw that the vampires had killed her sister, Clotho flew into a fury and vaporized them.
strings.refugee_s34_48: My magic. <The Quagmire enhances magic>. That's why Clotho chose this place for her rituals.
strings.refugee_s34_49: I returned to Clotho's home and...
strings.refugee_s34_5: Look here... Who gave you permission to interrogate me?!
strings.refugee_s34_51: I saw her, miserable and insane, crawling among empty bottles of potions...
strings.refugee_s34_52: She'd attempted to <kill herself>. She didn't succeed.
strings.refugee_s34_53: But it badly damaged her mind and her memory, irreversibly.
strings.refugee_s34_56: So I decided to take care of her and <keep her secret>.
strings.refugee_s34_57: Who knows about this besides you and me?
strings.refugee_s34_58: Nobody. They'd kill her if they found out that she'd brought the <Ancient Curse> upon us.
strings.refugee_s34_59: I need to talk to Clotho.
strings.refugee_s34_6: It's just a question. But based on your reaction, the answer is yes.
strings.refugee_s34_60: In the name of the Ancient God, Keeper... Tell nobody. Everything that happened — it's all my fault!
strings.refugee_s34_7: You can think whatever you like, Keeper. Leave me alone. Right now.
strings.refugee_s34_8: Chain, I didn't mean to offend you, I just wanted to know...
strings.refugee_s34_horadric_1: Horadric, where does <your wife> usually go when she's stressed?
strings.refugee_s34_horadric_2: Usually, she doesn't go anywhere. She just throws heavy objects at me.
strings.refugee_s34_horadric_3: But you might look for her somewhere <on the coast>.
strings.refugee_s35_1: I found the woman, master Alaric. The woman responsible for the return of the Ancient Curse.
strings.refugee_s35_10: I shall have to see and hear for myself.
strings.refugee_s35_2: That's marvelous news! We must act immediately! The situation in Town worsens by the day.
strings.refugee_s35_3: Well, who is she? Where is she?
strings.refugee_s35_4: She's not far. It's <Clotho, the old swamp witch>.
strings.refugee_s35_5: I've heard about her. Are you sure? Why did she do such a thing?
strings.refugee_s35_6: Her sister told me she was driven mad by loneliness, and decided to destroy the world.
strings.refugee_s35_7: That sounds quite ridiculous. It can't be the whole truth. Let's go find out directly from her.
strings.refugee_s35_8: It won't be that simple, I'm afraid. <Her memory> has been irreversibly damaged.
strings.refugee_s35_9: I wouldn't count on her remembering something that happened 30 years ago.
strings.refugee_s36_10: Ah, no need for ceremonies! Call me Clotty, my darling.
strings.refugee_s36_11: I should have seen that coming. Clotho is always full of surprises.
strings.refugee_s36_12: Er... Clotho, actually we came to ask you...
strings.refugee_s36_13: No, it's me who must ask: shall I play the delicate doe, my precious Alaric?
strings.refugee_s36_14: Already, you cannot resist the urge to grab me and take to your lair, my fearsome tiger!
strings.refugee_s36_15: Okay, just one question: do you remember anything about the <Ancient Curse> or the <fourth Graveyard Keeper>?
strings.refugee_s36_16: No, I don't. But I shall remember these passionate moments of our first meeting — forever!
strings.refugee_s36_17: A midnight abduction! How romantic! How sensual! My heart is yours forever. You...
strings.refugee_s36_2: Oh, Keeper! You frightened me so. I thought it was howling ghouls!
strings.refugee_s36_22: We need a moment to ourselves, madame Clotho. Sorry.
strings.refugee_s36_23: Hey, what did you do?! You took away her voice?
strings.refugee_s36_24: No. I deprived you and me of the ability to hear a woman's voice. Temporarily.
strings.refugee_s36_25: Excessive affection for the opposite sex is a key symptom of massive memory loss. You were right.
strings.refugee_s36_26: And if she forgot how she invoked the Curse, there's not much hope that she'll remember how to stop it.
strings.refugee_s36_27: Are you sure that the one who called up the Curse is the only one who can stop it?
strings.refugee_s36_28: Yes I am! The <Ancient God> said so to my brothers and me.
strings.refugee_s36_29: We'll just have to accept that we've failed, Keeper.
strings.refugee_s36_3: Ghouls don't exist. Clotho, allow me to introduce you to master Alaric.
strings.refugee_s36_30: Wait. Maybe we're mistaken? Maybe Clotho didn't actually start the Curse?
strings.refugee_s36_31: Hmm. Distract her for a few minutes.
strings.refugee_s36_32: I have waited for this moment all my life! The man of my dreams! I even have a dress picked out for this occasion!
strings.refugee_s36_33: Oh, how lovely. Where is it?
strings.refugee_s36_34: I'm wearing it! Or did you imagine I'm naked?
strings.refugee_s36_36: Clotho, this <black and gold cloak> I'm holding — is it yours?
strings.refugee_s36_37: Yes, it's mine. I don't like it and I've never worn it, but if you prefer me wearing that cloak for our wedding tomorrow...
strings.refugee_s36_38: Master Alaric, let's have another word.
strings.refugee_s36_4: Madame Clotho, we apologize for disturbing you at such an hour, but our question really is important and very personal.
strings.refugee_s36_7: Oh, master Alaric, it's all so sudden...
strings.refugee_s36_8: And as a decent woman, I must refuse you, but...
strings.refugee_s37_1: It's <her cloak>. Do you need more evidence?
strings.refugee_s37_100: <She> is the only warm and kind thing left in Clotho's life.
strings.refugee_s37_101: And Clotho knows she killed her.
strings.refugee_s37_103: Screaming... Fire... Despair... Unto death... No more memory... But <she> survived.
strings.refugee_s37_108: Could you say that again, please.
strings.refugee_s37_109: Clotho drinks powerful potions one after another, in hopes of killing herself.
strings.refugee_s37_11: These are special circumstances. Yes, I'm ready. What do you suggest?
strings.refugee_s37_110: Clotho's mind can't bear the pain, and breaks into fragments. Clotho descends into oblivion.
strings.refugee_s37_111: When Clotho awakes, only a small part of her mind awakens with her.
strings.refugee_s37_112: Clotho's true identity is forever lost. There's no way to reconstruct it.
strings.refugee_s37_113: Henceforth Clotho must lives with <this condition>.
strings.refugee_s37_118: Could you say that again, please.
strings.refugee_s37_12: An illegal and dangerous spell that the Inquisition uses when a heretic refuses to cooperate.
strings.refugee_s37_120: <Right answer>. This memory is returning home.
strings.refugee_s37_121: <Wrong answer>. This memory remains in the mist.
strings.refugee_s37_122: Hurry, Keeper! Clotho's pulse is growing slower!
strings.refugee_s37_124: Keeper, time is almost up. Clotho is barely breathing!
strings.refugee_s37_125: I'm going as fast as I can!
strings.refugee_s37_126: We must go back right now. She'll die in a few more seconds.
strings.refugee_s37_13: We'll penetrate into the <deepest layers of her mind>. And we'll try to restore her memories from within.
strings.refugee_s37_14: But you must know — it will be torture for her.
strings.refugee_s37_15: And if we fail, she'll lose what remains of her identity. And she may even die.
strings.refugee_s37_16: I don't like it, but do we have any other options?
strings.refugee_s37_17: I'll take that as a yes.
strings.refugee_s37_18: Forgive us, Clotho. We have to do this.
strings.refugee_s37_19: What do you mean, my dear? I certainly don't object to marrying this irresistible...
strings.refugee_s37_2: It's too early to give up. I have an idea.
strings.refugee_s37_22: It's her missing memory. Go ahead. You need to <reconnect her memories with the corresponding entities>.
strings.refugee_s37_24: The more links you restore, the better Clotho's chances for getting her memory back.
strings.refugee_s37_25: Er... Clotho? Can you say... something...
strings.refugee_s37_26: Memories. They're lost in the mist. <Point them home>.
strings.refugee_s37_27: <She> is the Supreme Priestess of the Ancient God.
strings.refugee_s37_28: Everything belongs to her. Her power is limitless. Her will is law.
strings.refugee_s37_3: Her amnesia isn't total. Maybe, it's possible to <recover Clotho's memories>...
strings.refugee_s37_31: Her people turn away from her. They despise her. They destroy all that is precious to her.
strings.refugee_s37_32: Her disciples, her friends, her sisters, her God — they all leave her.
strings.refugee_s37_33: <She> feels nothing but pain, and craves revenge.
strings.refugee_s37_38: Could you say that again, please.
strings.refugee_s37_39: Clotho fills <it> with black magic, day and night without food or sleep. 170 years in a row.
strings.refugee_s37_4: I have a <Memory tincture recipe>. We can ask Clotho to use tincture on this cloak and...
strings.refugee_s37_40: Spell by spell, ritual by ritual, further and darker and creepier.
strings.refugee_s37_41: Death is not enough, Clotho's enemies must suffer.
strings.refugee_s37_42: Thousands of victims are not enough. Humankind must be extinguished utterly.
strings.refugee_s37_43: But whatever Clotho contrives, it is not enough. And so she continues to write in <it>.
strings.refugee_s37_48: Could you say that again, please.
strings.refugee_s37_49: Uncontrollable, irreversible, unstoppable chaos. — The <one thing> that Clotho desires.
strings.refugee_s37_5: The tincture won't do. The cloak's magic is too powerful. I can see its aura, and it's extremely bright.
strings.refugee_s37_50: Countless hordes of walking dead. Cutting down men, women, and children — this is what Clotho desires.
strings.refugee_s37_51: Only the Ancient Contract holds <it> back.
strings.refugee_s37_52: Clotho must find a way to break the Contract.
strings.refugee_s37_58: Could you say that again, please.
strings.refugee_s37_59: <Despised outcasts>, willing to do anything to get rid of their troubles.
strings.refugee_s37_6: Such artifacts were made by the <Ancient God>.
strings.refugee_s37_60: It's so easy to manipulate them. Just give them hope.
strings.refugee_s37_62: <They> kidnap, torture and contaminate a priest for Clotho.
strings.refugee_s37_63: <They> kill for Clotho. All for a tiny promise Clotho gave them, which she has no intention of honoring.
strings.refugee_s37_68: Could you say that again, please.
strings.refugee_s37_69: <He> signed the Contract. He enforces it. He's extremely dangerous.
strings.refugee_s37_7: Spells? Potions? Rituals? There must be something!
strings.refugee_s37_70: And he could be extremely useful. <He> knows everything.
strings.refugee_s37_71: The vampires contaminate him, and then torture him by feeding him the wrong blood group.
strings.refugee_s37_72: <He> is broken and tells them everything. The Graveyard Keeper is the guarantor of the Contract.
strings.refugee_s37_73: Clotho must kill the Keeper! — Then the Ancient Curse will return. <The priest> is no longer needed.
strings.refugee_s37_78: Could you say that again, please.
strings.refugee_s37_79: <He> is the key to breaking the Contract. <He> must die.
strings.refugee_s37_80: Black magic doesn't affect him. — He's protected by the power of the Ancient God.
strings.refugee_s37_81: The vampires' ambush didn't work out either. — The vampires just turned to jaws.
strings.refugee_s37_82: Clotho knows that he's going to use the Ancient Portal. Clotho devises a mighty ritual.
strings.refugee_s37_83: Enchanted by this ritual, the Portal does not obey <his> will. The Portal kills <him>.
strings.refugee_s37_88: Could you say that again, please.
strings.refugee_s37_89: <It> enhances all magic. — It's the perfect place for such rituals.
strings.refugee_s37_9: Yes, there is something. <Black magic>. But are you prepared to take that step?
strings.refugee_s37_90: The vampires were ordered to assist. The vampires will remain in <this place> forever.
strings.refugee_s37_91: Nothing must interrupt the ritual. The Great Blast is inevitable. The fourth Keeper is doomed.
strings.refugee_s37_92: When the ritual is complete, Clotho notices a spy. Clotho sends the vampires to kill the witness.
strings.refugee_s37_93: <The place> was always meant to be a grave. Perhaps.
strings.refugee_s37_98: Could you say that again, please.
strings.refugee_s37_99: Despite the pain <she> inflicted on Clotho, Clotho still loves her.
strings.refugee_s38_1: Good work, Keeper! Things turned out great, I should think!
strings.refugee_s38_12: Oh, thank God! Clotho, can you hear me? It's me, Graveyard Keeper, your friend!
strings.refugee_s38_13: I... Graveyard Keeper... I remember you...
strings.refugee_s38_14: Clotho... Please, try to remember. The Necronomicon, the Ancient Curse, vampires, your sister Chain...
strings.refugee_s38_15: Do you remember all that stuff? Can you remember?!
strings.refugee_s38_16: I remember... warm wind... drops of rain... the smell of jasmine...
strings.refugee_s38_19: Oh, no, I remember something else! You promised to marry me!
strings.refugee_s38_20: We failed! Failed again! The brothers were right: I'm a useless loser!
strings.refugee_s38_21: What do you think — why didn't it work?
strings.refugee_s38_22: I don't know! Damnation! I'm tired of all these riddles. They've plagued my whole life!
strings.refugee_s38_24: Try what?! Her mind can't handle it! And it would be useless! Everything is useless!
strings.refugee_s38_25: We've lost, Keeper! Summon the courage to admit it. <Nothing can stop the Ancient Curse>.
strings.refugee_s38_26: All you can is learn from my mistakes.
strings.refugee_s38_27: There's no use sacrificing yourself for others. Just try to survive whatever is coming.
strings.refugee_s38_28: <Live your own life while you still can>.
strings.refugee_s38_29: The walking dead nearly upon us.
strings.refugee_s38_3: Don't worry, it's just a <common trance>. Go ahead, rouse her.
strings.refugee_s38_31: What?! You want your award? Of course, it's just another job for you!
strings.refugee_s38_32: Fine. Take <this apple>. It's golden. Are you satisfied?
strings.refugee_s38_34: Don't thank me, I stole this apple along with the cloak from Clotho's home.
strings.refugee_s38_35: The only thing I can do now is returning home and get some sleep.
strings.refugee_s38_36: I hope there won't be any monsters waiting for me near home.
strings.refugee_s38_38: If the "Vampire Queen" is old Clotho, who used to send those monsters to kill me?
strings.refugee_s38_4: And now Clotho will help us stop the Ancient Curse. Spectacular!
strings.refugee_s38_40: He... he turned to bat! He...
strings.refugee_s38_41: Yep, he's a vampire. A monster. You wouldn't make a happy pair, believe me...
strings.refugee_s38_5: Clotho! Clotho! Can you hear me?
strings.refugee_s38_6: Master Alaric, I don't like this. She... she's not breathing! Oh my gosh!
strings.refugee_s38_7: What? That's impossible — we were back in time!
strings.refugee_s39_1: Well well. Guys, you must be confused. Your <Lord Commander> let me free.
strings.refugee_s39_2: So, it was nice seeing you, come by again sometime and so on. But right now I'm a little busy.
strings.refugee_s39_3: We weren't sent by Lord Commander. So shut up and follow us.
strings.refugee_s39_4: They're looking at me weird. Something is wrong here.
strings.refugee_s39_5: Are you sure I have no choice?
strings.refugee_s39_6: You have a choice. You can refuse, and we'll kill you immediately.
strings.refugee_s39_7: Incidentally, we can even bury your corpse — for an additional fee.
strings.refugee_s39_9: That's an incredibly attractive offer, but... no, I'll save my money and come with you.
strings.refugee_s40_1: <Lady Beatrice>! I'd say it's a pleasant surprise, but...
strings.refugee_s40_10: And what am I supposed to do? Assuming I agree.
strings.refugee_s40_11: Nothing special. I need <five Emulsions of Death>.
strings.refugee_s40_12: Why can't you make these Emulsions yourself?
strings.refugee_s40_13: <Black alchemy> is difficult to practice in secret. I can't afford to take such a risk.
strings.refugee_s40_14: My reputation as an inquisitor must remain absolutely pure... for now.
strings.refugee_s40_15: Besides, the preparation of Emulsion requires <dark brains>... Fortunately, the Inquisition has <prisoners>.
strings.refugee_s40_16: They're burned along with their brains!
strings.refugee_s40_17: Except when they're killed while they're trying to escape... Or...
strings.refugee_s40_18: Jesus... These poor fugitives... Do you really need them just for dark brains?!
strings.refugee_s40_19: Nope, I have something far more interesting planned. Their escape allowed me to settle legally in <Mountain Fort>, and prepare everything for the next step.
strings.refugee_s40_2: Wasn't it you who tried to convince the <Lord Commander> to incinerate me last time we met?
strings.refugee_s40_20: Your friend Alaric didn't tell you that it was I who threw out him the hint on the way of rescuing the prisoners?
strings.refugee_s40_22: There's a time for everything, my dear.
strings.refugee_s40_23: Why do you need these Emulsions?
strings.refugee_s40_24: The Emulsions will prepare the bodies of the Mountain Fort soldiers for <transformation>.
strings.refugee_s40_26: It will begin with a <small injection of Emulsion>, disguised as a remedy for diarrhea...
strings.refugee_s40_27: There will be a few weeks of invisible mutations, then a few hours of torment, then oblivion. Silent death...
strings.refugee_s40_28: And then I shall revive them as obedient and nearly invulnerable <undead servants>.
strings.refugee_s40_29: Far more powerful than common zombies. And without that nasty smell. Almost.
strings.refugee_s40_3: Return to <Mountain Fort>, my friends. Your work here is done.
strings.refugee_s40_31: Ghouls? Ghouls don't exist. Everyone knows that!
strings.refugee_s40_32: You're right. However, your <old friend Clotho> found a way to make the fantasy a reality...
strings.refugee_s40_33: She came up with a ritual for raising ghouls. I got a <scroll>. Already used it a couple of times...
strings.refugee_s40_34: And the results surpassed all expectations.
strings.refugee_s40_35: What do you need ghouls for? What the hell are you doing with all this stuff?!
strings.refugee_s40_37: That's so typical of people, Keeper. If there's something they don't understand, they call it crazy.
strings.refugee_s40_38: But it's too soon to reveal everything yet.
strings.refugee_s40_39: Wait a little while, and your curiosity will be more than satisfied...
strings.refugee_s40_4: As for you, Keeper — you can relax. What's the use of bringing up old silly quarrels?
strings.refugee_s40_40: Let me guess, it was you who sent monsters to kill me?
strings.refugee_s40_41: And why would you say that?
strings.refugee_s40_42: It was you. Thanks to your <stinky spell>, you knew the whole time where I was and what I was doing!
strings.refugee_s40_43: Not bad. But don't worry: the aroma you hate so much will dissipate soon enough.
strings.refugee_s40_44: And... it was <your fault> the magic that Alaric used on Clotho didn't work!
strings.refugee_s40_46: A few drops of jasmine juice... and Alaric's final chance to stop the Ancient Curse was lost. Bingo, my dear.
strings.refugee_s40_47: However, thank you for your investigation. It was amusing to say the least, observing your meaningless efforts.
strings.refugee_s40_48: What if I refuse to make these Emulsions?
strings.refugee_s40_49: That would be most unpleasant. You'd change from a potential partner to an <unwanted witness>.
strings.refugee_s40_5: I'd like to give you another chance to earn my respect, and my friendship... and something even more intimate.
strings.refugee_s40_50: So I would be obliged to dispose of you. In a most drastic manner.
strings.refugee_s40_51: And then I'll use the dark brains of your <refugee friends>. After the Lord's people kill them.
strings.refugee_s40_52: You see, <I'll get what I need either way>. But you're still able to save some lives.
strings.refugee_s40_53: It is time for you to choose, Keeper. I grow tired, and the morning draws near.
strings.refugee_s40_54: I don't like it... but I agree to help you with the Emulsions.
strings.refugee_s40_55: Your plans are monstrous. Don't count on my help.
strings.refugee_s40_56: Are you sure? Thanks to your ridiculous pride, far more people will suffer. Including you.
strings.refugee_s40_57: Moment of truth. Maybe she's right and she'll win no matter what I do. But can I somehow <foil her plans>?
strings.refugee_s40_59: I refuse. Don't hold your breath waiting for my help.
strings.refugee_s40_6: Like I already told you, I'm not interested. I have my beloved.
strings.refugee_s40_7: Meh... I've heard that one before. But every time it ends the same way. All males are the same.
strings.refugee_s40_8: But as you wish. I can pay you in another coin. I'll rescue <your priceless refugees> from the Lord Commander's soldiers.
strings.refugee_s40_9: The old fool is completely on the hook for me. He'd defy <the King himself> if I asked.
strings.refugee_s41_1: Lovely. I wasn't particularly in the mood for violence today.
strings.refugee_s41_11: What other choice do I have?
strings.refugee_s41_12: Should I talk to <Alaric>? But <her spell> is still working, she'll hear every word.
strings.refugee_s41_13: On the other hand, if I choose my words carefully, she might not suspect a thing.
strings.refugee_s41_14: Or I could just expose Beatrice: tell the <Lord Commander> everything.
strings.refugee_s41_15: That might be rather difficult. He likes her and won't want to believe me...
strings.refugee_s41_16: But <Koukol> hates her! Maybe, he could help me with this?
strings.refugee_s41_17: Though if I whisper a word to Koukol, my deal with Beatrice will be off.
strings.refugee_s41_2: Keep in mind, time is short. The <Lord Commander> could declare an assault on the refugee camp any day.
strings.refugee_s41_4: I hope you understand one more thing: if anyone learns of the things I've told you, you'll be sorry I didn't kill you at once.
strings.refugee_s41_5: How should I deliver the <Emulsions> to you?
strings.refugee_s41_6: Say the code word <"Retribution"> to the <guard of Mountain Fort>.
strings.refugee_s41_7: When I get my five Emulsions, I'll hold up my end of our deal: I'll persuade the Lord Commander to leave the refugees alone.
strings.refugee_s41_8: A thousand kisses, my dear. You're a darling.
strings.refugee_s41_9: She is right, time is short. Better get to work making those <Emulsions>.
strings.refugee_s42_1_1: It will be hard to persuade him. I don't have <any evidence>.
strings.refugee_s42_1_10: But ghouls? Man, couldn't you think of anything more realistic? Ghouls don't exist.
strings.refugee_s42_1_11: Yes, everyone says so, but I'm not lying! You're all in great danger!
strings.refugee_s42_1_12: Listen, I don't have time for stupid jokes. We're getting ready for battle.
strings.refugee_s42_1_13: And I need to care that the boss doesn't notice that half the weaponry has vanished. So buy something or shove off!
strings.refugee_s42_1_14: Wait, there's one piece of evidence! Beatrice owns a <scroll of ghoul raising>!
strings.refugee_s42_1_15: If Koukol sees that scroll, then he'll believe me.
strings.refugee_s42_1_16: I need to talk to him one more time. The deal with Beatrice is off anyway.
strings.refugee_s42_1_2: And if I even try to tell him any of it, <my deal with Beatrice is off>.
strings.refugee_s42_1_4: Koukol, I have some extremely important information for you and the Lord Commander.
strings.refugee_s42_1_5: Lady Beatrice is planning to inject all the soldiers of Mountain Fort with a Death Emulsion...
strings.refugee_s42_1_6: And after that, she's going to revive them all as ghouls!
strings.refugee_s42_1_8: I'm trying to figure out whether you're drunk or you're off your nut.
strings.refugee_s42_1_9: Dude, she's a nasty bitch. I can't argue with that...
strings.refugee_s42_2_1: I have to be very careful, or Beatrice will suspect something.
strings.refugee_s42_2_10: He can push one of his brothers out of the home, hoping the wolf will eat him and go away.
strings.refugee_s42_2_11: Or he can do nothing, and wait until the wolf blows their house down and eats all the little pigs.
strings.refugee_s42_2_12: I got you. I would recommend this little pig named Keeper not play by the wolf's rules.
strings.refugee_s42_2_13: <Perhaps the wolf too has a house that can be blown down?>
strings.refugee_s42_2_3: I can't lie to you. I've been better. What brings you here?
strings.refugee_s42_2_4: I need your advice. Please, imagine... a group of little pigs living in a house made of bricks.
strings.refugee_s42_2_5: And one of these little pigs by the name of... er... Keeper has learned that a big bad hungry wolf is coming.
strings.refugee_s42_2_6: There's nowhere to run. And the wolf can blow the little pigs' house down.
strings.refugee_s42_2_7: Blow down a house made of bricks?!
strings.refugee_s42_2_8: Er... yes.... He's a black magician pretending to be a common wolf!
strings.refugee_s42_2_9: And the pig named Keeper has only two alternatives. And both of them are bad!
strings.refugee_s43_2: Hey, I already gave you Emulsions! Damned bureaucrats!
strings.refugee_s43_4a: Good to see you're one of us. I'll inform <milady>.
strings.refugee_s44_1: I was sure you would betray me. But you're smarter than I expected. Or... more cowardly?
strings.refugee_s44_2: I'm satisfied either way. Both are first steps towards loyalty and obedience.
strings.refugee_s44_3: Take your Emulsions and do as you promised. But don't expect any more services from me.
strings.refugee_s44_4: You're mistaken again. The path you just started on doesn't let people turn back.
strings.refugee_s44_5: Just one step is enough. Believe me, I know it more than anyone.
strings.refugee_s44_6: The only thing I want to hear: will the refugees be safe?
strings.refugee_s44_7: Of course. Until you tell anyone more than they should know.
strings.refugee_s45_1: I've done all I can, marquis. Nothing is threatening your people any more.
strings.refugee_s45_10: And together, we are a true bastion of courage, friendship, and loyalty!
strings.refugee_s45_11: This place will be our new home — a shelter for anyone who wants to join our brotherhood!
strings.refugee_s45_12: And we must thank Graveyard Keeper, he was the one who made this future possible!
strings.refugee_s45_14: But that's not all. I swear, one day we shall return to our native land — to Town!
strings.refugee_s45_15: With fire and sword, we shall restore justice! We'll reclaim everything we once had!
strings.refugee_s45_17: I swear this before you. Remember this day and these my words.
strings.refugee_s45_2: Neither the Lord Commander's soldiers nor the Inquisitors will disturb you.
strings.refugee_s45_3: I knew that trusting you was the best decision I ever made.
strings.refugee_s45_4: Look at all these people. — They are alive thanks to you!
strings.refugee_s45_5: You'll have your reward immediately, but our gratitude is impossible to measure with material things.
strings.refugee_s45_8: We have fought like hell. And... we've won! All the threats we were facing — it's all behind us!
strings.refugee_s45_9: Each of you is a hero.
strings.refugee_s46_1: Master Alaric, what are you going to do now that the threat to the refugees has passed?
strings.refugee_s46_10: Thank you, but... I'm not so sure.
strings.refugee_s46_12: Maybe, today he'll tell me his secret. Why does Teodoro hate Alaric so much?
strings.refugee_s46_14: I know what you want to ask.
strings.refugee_s46_15: It was I who inflicted upon <Teodoro> the most awful pain of his life.
strings.refugee_s46_16: As a senior inquisitor, I was responsible for the case of <his parents>.
strings.refugee_s46_17: I was the chairman on their court, the man who decided their sentence and handed it down.
strings.refugee_s46_18: And it was I who gave the signal to ignite the wood.
strings.refugee_s46_19: Were they really obsessed with <black magic>?
strings.refugee_s46_2: The best thing I can do now is to get as far away from Teodoro and his people as possible.
strings.refugee_s46_20: I tried to interrogate them, but they were like wild animals.
strings.refugee_s46_21: I had to use <black magic> to penetrate their memory.
strings.refugee_s46_22: Within their minds I found nothing but ruins covered with cold darkness.
strings.refugee_s46_23: They'd forgotten each other, their son, themselves...
strings.refugee_s46_24: Why didn't you destroy the cause of this tragedy — the <Necronomicon>?!
strings.refugee_s46_25: I wanted to. But the councilors sold it to the <University>. The war against the heretics required more and more money...
strings.refugee_s46_26: You think the sentence was a mistake?
strings.refugee_s46_27: No. Death was the best release for them.
strings.refugee_s46_28: But I could have done much more for <their poor orphan>... And now it is too late... too late...
strings.refugee_s46_29: Technically everything ended well... But I feel a little uneasy...
strings.refugee_s46_3: I'm not sure Teodoro will ever find the strength to forgive me. Or that I'll forgive myself.
strings.refugee_s46_30: We got in Lady Beatrice's way, but we didn't stop her. Who knows what the <other diabolical plans> she has.
strings.refugee_s46_31: Who knows whether the <Desert Witch> will tell master Alaric anything useful. Or whether he'll find her at all.
strings.refugee_s46_32: The marquis and the refugees are safe, but that speech was worrying. Obsession with revenge is an awful thing!
strings.refugee_s46_33: Nevertheless, I did my best. And I don't have any regrets.
strings.refugee_s46_5: I'll try to find the <Desert Witch>. She's said to be the wisest of women. Perhaps she knows another way to stop the <Ancient Curse>.
strings.refugee_s46_6: Though I don't have much hope left.
strings.refugee_s46_7: Then I can only wish you good luck.
strings.refugee_s46_8: Good luck to you too as well, Keeper. Take care of yourself.
strings.refugee_s46_9: You're a good man. And today you made this disgusting world a bit better.
strings.refugee_s47_1: Hmm... <Donkey> never leaves corpses here. How strange.
strings.refugee_s47_5: "Whether they knew the truth or not, keeping them alive was an unnecessary risk."
strings.refugee_s47_6: "Get rid of the bodies as soon as possible."
strings.refugee_s47_7: "A thousand kisses. And stay in touch, our work together has just begun!"
strings.refugee_s48_1: Koukol, you'll find a <Scroll of ghoul raising> among Beatrice's stuff. And then you'll know I'm telling the truth!
strings.refugee_s48_2: Hm, let me get this straight. You're saying I should search through the inquisitor's stuff, is that it?

strings.refugee_s48_5: Protect me? That old fool has one thought in his head all day — <serenading his lovely Beatrice>!
strings.refugee_s48_6: He'd rather send half his soldiers into the bonfire than quarrel with her!
strings.refugee_s48_7a: If you won't help me, I'll handle this on my own! <Call the Lord Commander>!
strings.refugee_s48_7a_1: Well, okay. But get ready to be beaten with sticks the second you open your mouth.
strings.refugee_s48_7b: You're right. Forget everything I told to you. It was just a... <bad joke>.
strings.refugee_s48_7b_1: Yeah, yeah, I thought I'd die laughing.
strings.refugee_s48_7b_2: It seems the only thing I can do is <warn Teodoro> of the coming assault.
strings.refugee_s50_1: Didn't I tell you not to distract me? I've almost finished the lyrics for the second verse!
strings.refugee_s50_11: She... killed you? Koukol, do you hear that? It would seem we're talking to a dead man!
strings.refugee_s50_12: She told me about them herself. She wanted my help and I agreed.
strings.refugee_s50_13: But then I decided to expose her.
strings.refugee_s50_14: To... expose her? Koukol, do you hear that? Never do business with graveyard keepers. Otherwise they'll... expose you!
strings.refugee_s50_16: A, ha, ha, ha! Keeper, I do like your sense of humor! What a splendid joke!
strings.refugee_s50_17: It's not a joke, it's a truth! Please, believe me!
strings.refugee_s50_18: Listen, my boy. To thank you for these few moments of laughter, I shall be merciful and let you go...
strings.refugee_s50_19: But if I ever again hear anything like that about <my precious Lady Beatrice>...
strings.refugee_s50_2: It will only take a moment, my lord. This will be most amusing, you'll see.
strings.refugee_s50_20: I shall imprison you and torment you unto your death. Is that clear?
strings.refugee_s50_22: Meh, I was expecting something bloodier.
strings.refugee_s50_23: One day, Koukol, you'll find out who was right. But then it'll be too late.
strings.refugee_s50_24: It seems the only thing I can do is <warn Teodoro> of the coming assault.
strings.refugee_s50_3: Lord Commander, I have terrible news about <Lady Beatrice>.
strings.refugee_s50_4: Oh my Gosh! What happened to the poor girl?!
strings.refugee_s50_5: I do hope this doesn't mean that our moonlight walk today is canceled?!
strings.refugee_s50_6: <She's a villain>, my Lord. She wants to kill all your people and raise a <ghoul army>!
strings.refugee_s50_7: Like I told you. It's stupid... but it's funny.
strings.refugee_s50_8: Wait, wait... And... how did you learn of her... sinister plans?
strings.refugee_s50_9: She told me about them herself. She wanted my help but I refused.
strings.refugee_s51_1: Sorry, marquis, but it's all I can do for you.
strings.refugee_s51_10: The only way left is the <Swamps>. But no one who has tried to cross the Swamps has ever returned.
strings.refugee_s51_12: Keeper, I'm going to need your help. Come talk to me tomorrow.
strings.refugee_s51_2: But Horadric! There wouldn't be any risk to the villagers! The Village is protected by the <Ancient Contract>!
strings.refugee_s51_3: Please, shelter at least some of us.
strings.refugee_s51_4: You overestimate the power of the Contract.
strings.refugee_s51_5: If the Inquisition learned that you settled in the Village, the Contract wouldn't...
strings.refugee_s51_6: Keeper, you have returned! Please, tell me that you bring good news!
strings.refugee_s51_7: I'd love to do that, but... I'm afraid, <the assault is unavoidable>, marquis.
strings.refugee_s51_8: You and your people have to run away. As soon as possible.
strings.refugee_s51_9: Run away... but where? We're trapped between Town and Mountain Fort.
strings.refugee_s52_11: For the perfect plan. Did you think I do this stuff for free?
strings.refugee_s52_12: Horadric, are you seriously trying to earn money off the tragedies of others?
strings.refugee_s52_14: It's not that I like it, Keeper. But this is the real world. The truth is — everybody survives however they can.
strings.refugee_s52_15: And if you live as long as I have, you'll see that I'm right.
strings.refugee_s52_2: Yes, yes, now come close and listen carefully.
strings.refugee_s52_2_1: Arrr. Bad luck. Not... um... today... um...
strings.refugee_s52_2_11: You know... it isn't that easy to pull off... There's a lot of additional overhead...
strings.refugee_s52_2_12: I'll need money for drinks, and girls for the crew, new uniforms, overhaul the hold...
strings.refugee_s52_2_13: All together, it will cost an additional... er... (gld)30.
strings.refugee_s52_2_14: Now you listen to me, you greedy scoundrel.
strings.refugee_s52_2_15: I'm damned tired of all this stuff.
strings.refugee_s52_2_16: I'm tired of people using my good deeds against me.
strings.refugee_s52_2_17: I already did enough for you. I'm not paying a penny more.
strings.refugee_s52_2_18: If you agree to my terms, then just do what I asked.
strings.refugee_s52_2_19: But if you insist on more, then go to hell. Seriously, just go to hell.
strings.refugee_s52_2_2: Um-um. Today... Bad today... luck... Um... Arrrrrrr.
strings.refugee_s52_2_20: Hey... easy, dude, it was a joke! I agree... This will be... the best voyage ever!
strings.refugee_s52_2_3: Hey, what the hell... am I doing here?! And where is... my rum, you landlubbers?!
strings.refugee_s52_2_4: Here's the short version: you were cursed, and I made you lick the Golden Apple of wisdom, and you're all right now.
strings.refugee_s52_2_5: In exchange, you'll kindly bring a group of people with their luggage to <some safe place far from here>.
strings.refugee_s52_2_6: It's very urgent, and nobody must know about our deal.
strings.refugee_s52_2_7: You... You mean that... you helped me so much, and... you request just a small voyage in exchange?!
strings.refugee_s52_3: You see that drunkard with the dice? That's a <former smuggler Captain>.
strings.refugee_s52_4: One day he tried to rob the <Desert Witch>, and she put a curse on him. Now he has the <mind of an ostrich>.
strings.refugee_s52_5: But the point is — he has a <vessel>. And...
strings.refugee_s52_6: Let me guess: if I can break <his curse>, he'd be willing to get the refugees out of here.
strings.refugee_s52_7: True. But it won't be easy. The <Golden Apple of wisdom> is the only thing that can cure him. Theoretically.
strings.refugee_s52_8: Hm, that's definitely a bit more complicated than I thought... But okay. Thank you, Horadric.
strings.refugee_s53_0_1: If I tell him right now, all the refugees will <depart> very soon.
strings.refugee_s53_0_2: Am I sure that I don't have <unfinished business> with them?
strings.refugee_s53_1: I arranged everything with the <smuggler Captain>, marquis. He'll get you all safely out of here.
strings.refugee_s53_10: We struggled with every fiber of our being, but now we must withdraw.
strings.refugee_s53_11: This camp will soon be destroyed by our enemies, but it will remain in our hearts forever...
strings.refugee_s53_12: A monument. To courage, friendship, and loyalty!
strings.refugee_s53_13: A new life awaits us on distant shores.
strings.refugee_s53_14: And we have Graveyard Keeper to thank for this new chance.
strings.refugee_s53_16: But that's not all. I swear, one day we shall return to our native land — to Town!
strings.refugee_s53_17: With fire and sword, we shall restore justice! We'll reclaim everything we once had!
strings.refugee_s53_19: I swear this before you. Remember this day and these my words.
strings.refugee_s53_1b: Nothing. We'll talk a bit later.
strings.refugee_s53_2: Pack your stuff. The sooner you leave these shores the better.
strings.refugee_s53_4: Damned! I worked so hard but... the only thing I achieved is <your exile>.
strings.refugee_s53_5: Well, it's not the best outcome, but you know, we survived and that's what's important.
strings.refugee_s53_6: It was a pleasure to meet you, Graveyard Keeper. Actually you helped us quite a lot, and we'll never forget it.
strings.refugee_s53_7: All that remains is to say goodbye and reward you for your efforts.
strings.refugee_s54_1: It was nice meeting you, master Alaric. I suppose you're going with the others on the ship?
strings.refugee_s54_10: Maybe, today he'll tell me his secret. Why does Teodoro hate Alaric so much?
strings.refugee_s54_2: I think I must. But afterwards I'll leave Teodoro and his people.
strings.refugee_s54_3: I'm not sure Teodoro will ever find the strength to forgive me. Or that I'll forgive myself.
strings.refugee_s54_5: I'll try to find the <Desert Witch>. She's said to be the wisest of women. Perhaps she knows another way to stop the <Ancient Curse>.
strings.refugee_s54_6: Though I don't have much hope left.
strings.refugee_s54_7: Then I can only wish you good luck.
strings.refugee_s54_8: Good luck to you too as well, Keeper. Take care of yourself.
strings.refugee_s55_1: It's so quiet here... I hope they'll be okay.
strings.refugee_s55_10: "Not bad! But don't be surprised if your life soon turns into a nightmare."
strings.refugee_s55_12: Well, at least... That's to be expected.
strings.refugee_s55_2: Hmm, what is this? Someone left me a <note>?
strings.refugee_s55_3: "I'm extremely disappointed in you, my dear."
strings.refugee_s55_4: "In cheating me, you have made a great mistake, and you will pay for it."
strings.refugee_s55_5: "I will do all I can to make your life a nightmare."
strings.refugee_s55_7: Well... I should have expected worse.
strings.refugee_s55_8: "You survived, my dear. What an amazing surprise."
strings.refugee_s55_9: "You survived — and dashed all my plans."
strings.refugee_s61_1: It was a pleasure to meet you, Keeper. I'll remember you... as you are now.
strings.refugee_s61_10: Hmm... That's an interesting idea... It could even be an opportunity to frame that nosy twerp <Koukol>.

strings.refugee_s80_10: Interesting... It looks like a <page torn from the Necronomicon>.

strings.refugee_s80_12: Well... let's put an end to this. Let's go to the Lord Commander.
strings.refugee_s80_2: Dude, I have to say, that was really cool!
strings.refugee_s80_3: Hmm. I hope you didn't leave <any evidence> of your search?

strings.refugee_s81_10: A villain? A ghoul army? Are you mad, young man?! It seems I should have the executioner prepare two racks...
strings.refugee_s81_11: Look at <this scroll>, my Lord. I found it in Lady Beatrice's room. During the search that she's protesting.
strings.refugee_s81_13: What is <this abomination>? My dear, do you know something about this?
strings.refugee_s81_14: Nothing, my Lord. I'm seeing it the first time, just like you.
strings.refugee_s81_15: For the first time? Are you sure? The thing reeks of your <"revolutionary, unique freshener">. The one you used in my home!
strings.refugee_s81_16: Hmm, it is indeed a <familiar aroma>...
strings.refugee_s81_17: My lord, this is just awful slander! They're trying to pull us apart!
strings.refugee_s81_18: How could I be planning something so terrible, if... I love you!
strings.refugee_s81_2: Don't worry, my dear. As soon as we get to the <Fort>, I'll put him on the rack!

strings.refugee_s81_21: "My sweetheart Koukol! Can you imagine my disgust when the elderly maniac tries to touch me?"... Et cetera.
strings.refugee_s81_23: Elderly? Elderly?! Soldiers, arrest Lady Beatrice!
strings.refugee_s81_24: Miserable worms! You can't even imagine the power you seek to resist!
strings.refugee_s81_26: The true King, purified by betrayal, damnation and holy fire, will deliver everyone the justice they deserve.

strings.refugee_s81_3: So what is this incredible surprise, fool?! Don't you see, milady is beside herself?!
