strings.refugee_s81_32: Oh, I don't feel well... My migraine has returned... Along with my rheumatism and this blasted nervous tick... Soldiers, we're going home...
strings.refugee_s81_33: You know, I like that <elderly maniac> after all. It's so easy to manipulate him.
strings.refugee_s81_34: I never imagined the <old love note trick> could work so perfectly! The right timing is the key to success!
strings.refugee_s81_35: So when did you write that note?
strings.refugee_s81_36: The day after that <arrogant bitch> came to the Fort.
strings.refugee_s81_7: Lord Commander, you should know something about <Lady Beatrice>.
strings.refugee_s81_8: She is a villain. She's planning to kill all your people and raise a <ghoul army>!
strings.refugee_tanner_1_1: Tell me, good lad, did someone ask you to bring something for me? A note?
strings.refugee_tanner_1_10: I wish... He was fired, lost his home and all his savings, and given an <enormous fine>!
strings.refugee_tanner_1_11: I had to sell my tanning workshop, and it only covered part of my son's fine.
strings.refugee_tanner_1_13: You know, even now, living as an outcast, I'm still a mother. And I have to help my kid.
strings.refugee_tanner_1_14: Could I ask you to build a <tanning workbench> for me? Even here, I could earn a little extra money for my son.
strings.refugee_tanner_1_2: Actually, no. Did something happen? You look really sick.
strings.refugee_tanner_1_3: It's sleeplessness. And nerves. I can't stop thinking of <my son>. He's in terrible trouble.
strings.refugee_tanner_1_5: He was one of the King's guards. He dreamt of being a guard since he was a child. But recently...
strings.refugee_tanner_1_7: Sorry. It's difficult for me to tell.
strings.refugee_tanner_1_8: He happened to sneeze during the King's solemn speech for the Holiday of Great Purification.
strings.refugee_tanner_2_1: Maybe there's something else I can do for you?
strings.refugee_tanner_2_10: Good bags are always useful. All right — you'll get your farm.
strings.refugee_tanner_2_2: Thank you very much. Although I'm not comfortable asking you for anything else, in fact I am in need of something.
strings.refugee_tanner_2_3: My son said to me in his note that he's going to a forest with his friends.
strings.refugee_tanner_2_4: They'll be robbing the wealthy and giving the money they steal to the poor.
strings.refugee_tanner_2_5: But they need <special costumes>. For protection against mosquitoes. And enemy arrows. And they're also good for picking up girls.
strings.refugee_tanner_2_6: I've decided to make these costumes from leather dipped in cow's milk and egg yolks.
strings.refugee_tanner_2_7: I already have enough leather. If you were so kind as to build a small <animal farm> for me...
strings.refugee_tanner_2_8: An animal farm? That's no small task...
strings.refugee_tanner_2_9: I know. But for this, I'll let you buy my <best bags> — the kind that town aristocracy use.
strings.refugee_tanner_3_1: That's right. The Big Tournament of Bowmen approaches, and my son and his friends hope to participate in it, wearing their new costumes.
strings.refugee_tanner_3_2: I'll try to take care of it quickly.
strings.refugee_tanner_3_3: Rose could sell me a cow. If I ask her persistently enough.
strings.refugee_tanner_3_4: As for hens... Maybe the weird house with the egg basket will be of some help? Somehow...
strings.refugee_tanner_4_1_1: Really? That's wonderful! And it will be so useful for our community!
strings.refugee_tanner_4_1_2: Actually, I have wonderful news: <my son and his friends> just collected enough money to pay off their debts!
strings.refugee_tanner_4_1_3: But like you said before, they're going to give the stolen money to the poor!
strings.refugee_tanner_4_1_4: They were, but then they decided that that would do too much harm to the country's economic system. And they started robbing poor people too.
strings.refugee_tanner_4_1_5: Well, okay. It's good that now they can repay their debts and return to their normal lives.
strings.refugee_tanner_4_1_6: You know, they decided it's better to remain forest thugs. The pay is better, and the girls love it.
strings.refugee_tanner_4_1_7: Aha... I see. So how do they plan on spending the stolen money now?
strings.refugee_tanner_4_1_9: Nevertheless, I'm very grateful to you. Let me share with you some of <my skills>.
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_1: Rose, how much does <one of your cows> cost?
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_10: "Love is smoke made with the fume of sighs."
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_11: And... "To love a cow means to sell it for (gld)1."
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_12: Oh, that's so wise and so touching! Of course I'll sell it!
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_2: Keeper, would you ever sell one of your best friends?
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_3: I understand. Okay, I can offer one whole (gld)1 for a cow.
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_4: You could offer (gld)1000. That wouldn't change a thing. I love them so!
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_5: Mmm... have you ever heard the phrase: "if you love someone, set them free"?
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_6: Nope. Who said it? It sounds so beautiful and wise!
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_7: I don't know who said it, but yes, it is very wise.
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_8: Do you know any other wise phrases about love? Tell me!
strings.refugee_tanner_4_2_9: "Life is the flower and love is the honey."
strings.refugee_tutorial_10: Well... how to explain this... Speaking scientifically, <Satisfaction> (refugee_happiness_filler) converts <Camp Quality> (refugee_happiness_slot) into <Refugee Happiness> (refugee_happiness).
strings.refugee_tutorial_11: But remember, refugees only produce <Satisfaction> (refugee_happiness_filler) when they have enough food and water!
strings.refugee_tutorial_12: In other words, the more satisfied refugees, the more <Satisfaction> (refugee_happiness_filler)?
strings.refugee_tutorial_15: <Refugee Happiness> (refugee_happiness) is just a <Camp Quality> (refugee_happiness_slot), modified by <Satisfaction> (refugee_happiness_filler).
strings.refugee_tutorial_16: Keep in mind that it can't exceed <Camp Quality> (refugee_happiness_slot). And it falls if your refugees are suffering from a shortage of food or water.
strings.refugee_tutorial_17: And what's the purpose of this... er.... parameter?
strings.refugee_tutorial_18: Alas, without sufficient <Refugee Happiness> (refugee_happiness), you can't build something in the camp or attract new refugees!
strings.refugee_tutorial_19: Hmmm... that's a bit inconvenient. But logical. It's hard to argue.
strings.refugee_tutorial_2: I can try to explain it. Obviously I'm no specialist, but I've read about such matters.
strings.refugee_tutorial_21: Our refugees can look after themselves for the bare necessities, but this isn't enough to feel any <Satisfaction> (refugee_happiness_filler).
strings.refugee_tutorial_22: They won't die of starvation, but it won't be enough for <camp development>.
strings.refugee_tutorial_23: I got you. So how do you suppose I should feed them?
strings.refugee_tutorial_24: For instance, you could regularly put some <food> and <water> (refugee_water) in the storehouse.
strings.refugee_tutorial_25: And please, watch that the storehouse isn't empty.
strings.refugee_tutorial_26: One refugee needs just 3 <water> (refugee_water) and 30 <energy> (en) a day. As you see, they aren't gluttonous at all.
strings.refugee_tutorial_3: There are certain deep mechanisms and parameters involved. Imagine it's a... some tricky game.
strings.refugee_tutorial_4: And if you understand it that way, why you're halfway there. The rest is pure logic.
strings.refugee_tutorial_8: Oh, that's simple. When you build something useful for our camp, you increase the <Camp Quality> (refugee_happiness_slot).
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_1: I'll be short. Do you want me to give you some work, Graveyard Keeper?
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_11: What exactly do you need from me?
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_12: I need <5 iron chisels> and <10 wood wedges>.
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_13: In exchange, I'll give you a <serious discount> on my stuff.
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_2: It depends on the amount of the work and the payment.
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_3: Good. I need a gravestone for one of my acquaintances.
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_4: But my tools are back in Town. Could you provide <other tools>?
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_5: Yes. And my condolences for your loss. What happened to your acquaintance?
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_6: Well, according to the newspapers, I strangled him on our wedding night.
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_7: But, of course, that's just a vile lie. It's a lie — just like all the gossip about the asphyxiations of my three previous husbands.
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_8: It was all just a series of accidents!
strings.refugee_undertaker_1_9: You know how it is. Wild passion, alcohol, role playing... Special toys for enhancing desire...
strings.refugee_undertaker_2_2: Great. I'll start work immediately. I hope my dead husband's relatives will be satisfied.
strings.refugee_undertaker_2_3: The thing is, they already sent me a couple of threatening letters.
strings.refugee_undertaker_2_4: Just in case — could you please build a <workbench> for me, so I can do my work more effectively?
strings.refugee_undertaker_3_1: That's perfect. Though you know, it might be not enough.
strings.refugee_undertaker_3_2: My dead husband's relatives are insisting on the best gravestone I'm capable of.
strings.refugee_undertaker_3_3: Yesterday I discovered the decapitated head of my dear horse Molly under my blanket!
strings.refugee_undertaker_3_4: That sounds serious. What can I do to help you?
strings.refugee_undertaker_4_1: I hope these will help you see an end to the threats from your dead husband's relatives.
strings.refugee_undertaker_4_2: Mmm, quality things. They'll be really helpful in my affairs.
strings.refugee_undertaker_4_3: And about my husband's relatives — their threats don't scare me anymore.
strings.refugee_undertaker_4_4: My own relatives will take care of them during my husband's funeral... if you know what I mean.
strings.refugee_undertaker_4_5: It seemed like I understood that. By the way, how do you make your special gravestones?
strings.refugee_undertaker_4_6: Wouldn't you like to know <my secrets>? Hmm. Okay, but don't tell them to anybody or...
strings.refugee_undertaker_4_7: Or come the next holiday, something nasty will happen to me. Yeah, I got it.
strings.refugees_city_2_1_1: Ah, Keeper, you're just in time! I was just about to visit you.
strings.refugees_city_2_1_11: First, we need an <improved warehouse> and an <improved campfire>.
strings.refugees_city_2_1_12: And <one more tent> would be just right. — So we can take in more refugees.
strings.refugees_city_2_1_13: Hm, that smell... is that cloves? Where is that coming from? Weird.
strings.refugees_city_2_1_2: We've had terrible news. <The King> was in a terrible rage, and refused even to speak to my cousin about our bid for clemency.
strings.refugees_city_2_1_3: His <son's wedding> was disrupted. The bride is dead.
strings.refugees_city_2_1_5: Inquisitors. A group of inquisitors led by some <Lady Beatrice> accused her of witchery.
strings.refugees_city_2_1_6: They produced some "evidence", so the court's judgment was swift...
strings.refugees_city_2_1_7: That's bad. By the way, that Lady Beatrice you just mentioned paid me a visit. She's looking for you.
strings.refugees_city_2_1_8: We've nowhere else to go, so I hope she stops looking before she finds us here.
strings.refugees_city_2_1_9: We'll have to stay here for a long time. Maybe forever.
strings.refugees_d_17_1: Let me guess. Now you need an <inspiring bronze statue> the size of my church?!
strings.refugees_d_17_10: The only thing I'm any good at: bringing you corpses and eating carrots.
strings.refugees_d_17_11: Hmm... maybe... it's not as bad as you think? My carrots are quite tasty. And...
strings.refugees_d_17_2: Or, maybe tons of <politically correct literature> for the baby donkeys?!
strings.refugees_d_17_3: Oh, I know! You need a <golden sarcophagus with a glass cover> for every donkey who participated in the Revolution!
strings.refugees_d_17_4: Nothing of the sort. The thing is... we failed, my dear comrade.
strings.refugees_d_17_5: Hmm, I've never seen him so oppressed... He's about to cry!
strings.refugees_d_17_7: The rats seized power in our post office and declared a <military dictatorship>.
strings.refugees_d_17_8: And now the donkeys' situation is even worse than it was before the Revolution.
strings.refugees_d_17_9: So what are you going to do?
strings.refugees_s10_1: It's incredible! It's... like a classic horror movie!
strings.refugees_s10_2: I should hurry to the <Village> and stop him. Somehow...
strings.refugees_s10_3: By the way, I wonder where he's hid his sleeping coffin?
strings.refugees_s11_1: You shall not pass, foul creature!
strings.refugees_s11_10: YOU WILL DIE A LONG AND TORTUROUS DEATH FOR THIS INSULT, YOU BASTARD! DEFEND YOURSELF!
strings.refugees_s11_11: I admire your logic — not to mention your fervor. But if you don't leave me alone...
strings.refugees_s11_12a: HE'S NOT ALONE! WE'LL BOTH STOP YOU, VAMPIRE!
strings.refugees_s11_12b: HEY, GUYS, THERE'S NO NEED TO KILL EACH OTHER! LET'S TALK... FIRST!
strings.refugees_s11_13: Keeper? This is not your business! I asked you not to bother me!
strings.refugees_s11_15: HEY! I CAN'T SEE! THAT'S NOT FAIR!
strings.refugees_s11_16: EVEN IF YOU ESCAPE, I KNOW WHERE TO FIND YOU AND...
strings.refugees_s11_18: Why'd you have to go and do that? If you hadn't intervened, I have <that bloodsucker> the next second.
strings.refugees_s11_19: Or he would have dealt with you in half a second...
strings.refugees_s11_20: Sorry about that. I promise it won't happen again.
strings.refugees_s11_21: Good. He didn't stand a chance. You saw how he was so frightened he went deaf!
strings.refugees_s11_3: Hey, I'm talking to you! Have some respect!
strings.refugees_s11_4: You'll have to speak louder. He's deaf.
strings.refugees_s11_5: This world has gone crazy! Deaf vampires, garlic-munching vampires... What's next?
strings.refugees_s11_6: STOP, YOU MONSTER, AND FIGHT ME!
strings.refugees_s11_8: There's no point, young man. Your wife's blood doesn't suit me. And as for you...
strings.refugees_s11_9: You really don't seem tasty enough.
strings.refugees_s12_1: Where am I? Did I die? Is this Heaven?
strings.refugees_s12_10: Because of everything! You're a monster, I know your secret and...
strings.refugees_s12_11: I'm no monster. And I'm not so foolish as to kill the Graveyard Keeper. That would <ruin everything>.
strings.refugees_s12_12: I had planned to... do something rather naughty with you, I admit. But I have since changed my mind.
strings.refugees_s12_13: You managed to track me, so you're more capable than I imagined. And you might even be useful.
strings.refugees_s12_15: I'll leave you alone for a while. Calm your emotions, and shed your ridiculous delusions of heroism.
strings.refugees_s12_16: Time's up. Now listen to my words, and make your choice.
strings.refugees_s12_17: <The Ancient Curse>. It has returned. And I must stop it before it's too late.
strings.refugees_s12_18: This is my duty, as written in the <Ancient Contract>.
strings.refugees_s12_19: Should I fail, a <thousand bloodthirsty zombies> will flood the Town, the Village — and even your graveyard.
strings.refugees_s12_2: Heaven? No, more like the opposite. This is <my tent>, and you're alive.
strings.refugees_s12_20: But the problem is already too advanced. I can't deal with it all on my own. I need your help, Keeper.
strings.refugees_s12_21: It's... It's all rather unexpected, I need to think.
strings.refugees_s12_22: I see. You're welcome to ask <any questions>. But remember, we're already running short of time.
strings.refugees_s12_3: You! I remember! You're a vile vampire!
strings.refugees_s12_4: Wait a second. Why didn't you kill me?
strings.refugees_s12_5: And... Hey, you can hear me! What the hell is going on?!
strings.refugees_s12_6: While you were unconscious, I borrowed a <part of your hearing>.
strings.refugees_s12_8: Don't worry, as you can tell, your own hearing has already regenerated.
strings.refugees_s12_9: But why did you suggest I might have killed you?
strings.refugees_s12_q1_2: Absolutely nothing. A little bump on the head. It was completely harmless.
strings.refugees_s12_q1_3: I suppose it might even do him some good.
strings.refugees_s12_q1_4: Anyway, he's at home and <his wife> is looking after him.
strings.refugees_s12_q2_2: No. I was... <contaminated>. Over 30 years ago.
strings.refugees_s12_q2_3: <Some vampires> kidnapped me, put me in a cage, tortured me... and did this to me.
strings.refugees_s12_q2_4: I hate my curse more than anything, but there's no cure for it.
strings.refugees_s12_q2_5: I drink blood only in the most desperate situation, to avoid a <terrible death>.
strings.refugees_s12_q3_2: I didn't want to. But I'm nearly <dying of hunger>.
strings.refugees_s12_q3_3: If I try to attack anyone at the camp, <Teodoro> would easily find me out.
strings.refugees_s12_q3_4: I remember a movie, there was a guy who drank rat blood or he'd...
strings.refugees_s12_q3_5: I do not fear death. But I cannot leave this world without fulfilling my duty.
strings.refugees_s12_q4_2: It was laid upon us two centuries ago, when <disciples of the New Faith> destroyed the <Ancient Bridge>.
strings.refugees_s12_q4_3: Departed souls could no longer find the way to the <Land of the Dead>.
strings.refugees_s12_q4_4: They grew mad in despair, returned to their bodies, and began killing everyone.
strings.refugees_s12_q4_6: Only the <Ancient God> and the <Ancient Contract> saved humankind from annihilation.
strings.refugees_s12_q5_2: It contains the list of dictates which stave off the <Ancient Curse>.
strings.refugees_s12_q5_3: It was agreed to by representatives of New and Old Faith, and the Ancient God.
strings.refugees_s12_q5_4: <My brothers> and I, as signatories, were obliged to follow it faithfully and execute all its conditions.
strings.refugees_s12_q5_5: We did so for nearly <170 years>. But as you can see, we failed eventually.
strings.refugees_s12_q5_6: Ha. You're even older than Moses. Not bad.
strings.refugees_s12_q5_7: I always considered it strange that <Graveyard Keepers> weren't informed of all this stuff.
strings.refugees_s12_q5_8: In the end, you're the <guarantors of the Contract>.
strings.refugees_s12_q6_2: Because the <strictures of the Ancient Contract> were violated. Too many times.
strings.refugees_s12_q6_4: The <Inquisition's cruelty>, the <Cult's brutality>, the <Ships of the Dead> stuck in the harbor...
strings.refugees_s12_q6_5: And most importantly, we haven't had a <Graveyard Keeper> for the past 30 years.
strings.refugees_s12_q6_6: <Your predecessor> was killed before you, the next chosen Keeper, were even born!
strings.refugees_s12_q6_7: There must always be a Graveyard Keeper. They are the guarantors of the Contract.
strings.refugees_s12_q6_8: That's why I asked when we first met about the role you play.
strings.refugees_s12_q7_2: The Curse began to return after the <Great Blast>. And according to the information I have...
strings.refugees_s12_q7_3: The <fourth Keeper>, your predecessor, has been killed in the Great Blast!
strings.refugees_s12_q7_4: So we must unmask the <murderer> of the fourth Keeper.
strings.refugees_s12_q7_5: Only the person who triggered the Curse can stop its spread.
strings.refugees_s12_q7_6: Well... It looks like I'll be playing Sherlock Holmes a bit more...
strings.refugees_s12_q7_7: So there's nobody else who can help with this Curse?
strings.refugees_s12_q7_8: Nobody. The other signatories are bound by a <seal of silence>.
strings.refugees_s12_q7_9: Except for me and my brothers. But it's useless to count on them.
strings.refugees_s12_q8_2: This is not the time or place to discuss them. Perhaps one day...
strings.refugees_s12_q8_3: But for now, know this: we can rely only on ourselves.
strings.refugees_s12_q9_2: I know it's not an easy decision, but it's the right one. Let's see...
strings.refugees_s12_q9_3: For starters, take <these scrolls>: they'll help you save a lot of time travelling.
strings.refugees_s12_q9_4: Then we should... We should... should...
strings.refugees_s12_q9_5: Master Alaric, what happened to you? Wait, I'll call the marquis...
strings.refugees_s12_q9_7: If he learns that I'm a vampire... he'll pierce my heart with a wooden stake... with the greatest of pleasure...
strings.refugees_s12_q9_8: Blood... Just <a drop of blood>... please... hurry...
strings.refugees_s12_q9_9: Blood? Well... I doubt corpse blood is tasty, but we're out of options.
strings.refugees_s13_10: Thank you. May I ask: why did you say <Teodoro> would be glad to kill you?
strings.refugees_s13_11: Because it's true. But that is one of those burdens that cannot be shared.
strings.refugees_s13_2: There, that's a bit better... but the taste is amazingly foul. What was it?
strings.refugees_s13_3: Corpse blood. Or were you counting on me to ask some villager to volunteer his blood?
strings.refugees_s13_4: Oh no, not again. Hello diarrhea. But you're right. Thank you, in spite of it all.
strings.refugees_s13_5: If you wish, I can bring you some regularly. So that you can stop bothering the villagers.
strings.refugees_s13_6: It's a deal. And paying you for this service, would be the honest thing, wouldn't it?
strings.refugees_s13_7: Okay. I have something for you right now. It's my old <vampire sun cream>.
strings.refugees_s13_8: You can show it to them as an evidence of the... vampire's demise.
strings.refugees_s13_9: Then the villagers will stop worrying, and you'll get your reward.
strings.refugees_s14_10: Some strange magic turned their attackers to <vampire jaws>.
strings.refugees_s14_11: Maybe it's possible to find these jaws and disenchant them?
strings.refugees_s14_12: I've heard of this place. I should inform Alaric.
strings.refugees_s14_14: I know where we could start looking. But that event happened so long ago. Any clue must be long gone.
strings.refugees_s14_15: That's not a great problem. Borrow the <Witcher's Eye> from Teodoro.
strings.refugees_s14_16: It's a special artifact for discovering things which are shrouded in the veils of time.
strings.refugees_s14_18: I'm still too weak from hunger. And daylight is deadly to me.
strings.refugees_s14_19: Hm... Well, I'll tell you if I find anything.
strings.refugees_s14_2: You passed out and never finished your thought.
strings.refugees_s14_3: Ah yes. You must <find the vampires> who captured and tortured me 30 years ago.
strings.refugees_s14_4: I remember — they asked me about the Ancient Contract and the Ancient Curse.
strings.refugees_s14_5: I'm sure they're somehow connected to the <Curse> and the <Great Blast>.
strings.refugees_s14_6: Where should I start looking? Do you have an address?
strings.refugees_s14_7: I don't know. They sort of disappeared after the Great Blast.
strings.refugees_s14_8: So the trail is cold.  Let me think...
strings.refugees_s14_9: Astrologer told me that he and the fourth Keeper were <attacked by vampires>.
strings.refugees_s15_1: I heard that the Graveyard Keeper is an extraordinary individual.
strings.refugees_s15_10: Someone who... what's that disgusting smell? Is that corpses?
strings.refugees_s15_11: Please, stop doing that. It smells unbearable!
strings.refugees_s15_12: What?! It's a <revolutionary, unique freshener>! ... Really? You prefer the smell of corpses?
strings.refugees_s15_13: Definitely. At least it doesn't make my eyes water.
strings.refugees_s15_14: How disappointing. I had hoped on a more... arousing encounter. Perhaps... next time.
strings.refugees_s15_15: Sorry. You didn't say — who are you looking for?
strings.refugees_s15_16: <Heretics>, sentenced to the holy fire. They escaped from <Prison> and fled Town.
strings.refugees_s15_17: With the help of an <old inquisitor>, who betrayed his faith and his God.
strings.refugees_s15_19: I'd love to help, but I don't know anything about it.
strings.refugees_s15_1_1_1: Master Alaric, you must know something about inquisitor Beatrice. She paid me a visit.
strings.refugees_s15_1_1_10: No doubt. But that's just common stuff. There's something else at work here...
strings.refugees_s15_1_1_2: Beatrice? The <Council> entrusted our affair to Beatrice?!
strings.refugees_s15_1_1_3: It seems they're even crazier than I imagined...
strings.refugees_s15_1_1_4: What do you mean? What do you know about her?
strings.refugees_s15_1_1_5: Ever since she appeared several years ago, strange things have been happening...
strings.refugees_s15_1_1_6: She's had a tremendous career, gathered hundreds of supporters, even including councilors...
strings.refugees_s15_1_1_7: So what's strange? She is ambitious, smart, and quite beautiful. Not my type, but...
strings.refugees_s15_1_1_8: Her influence over the Council and the Inquisition is grown too strong. There's a secret behind this — I'm sure of it!
strings.refugees_s15_1_2_1: Monsignor, have you heard about Lady Beatrice?
strings.refugees_s15_1_2_2: Pff, of course I've heard! I've heard about her all the time in recent years!
strings.refugees_s15_1_2_3: The <other councilors> are crazy about her! They say she's our pride — the future of the Inquisition!
strings.refugees_s15_1_2_4: It sounds like you don't like her.
strings.refugees_s15_1_2_5: The girl's looks and smiles don't work on me! I see the truth!
strings.refugees_s15_1_2_6: Oh, Monsignor, your wisdom never ceases to amaze me! So what is this truth?
strings.refugees_s15_1_2_7: This is monstrous, I know... but... I'm afraid her faith isn't as firm and fanatical as it ought to be — as it must be!
strings.refugees_s15_2: But nobody warned me that he's also a handsome man.
strings.refugees_s15_21: Don't worry, my dear. You've already helped.
strings.refugees_s15_24: Dried cloves and lilies. Beautifully combined with the smell of rotting corpses.
strings.refugees_s15_2_buck_1: It's a good thing Teodoro doesn't know what we're doing here.
strings.refugees_s15_2_buck_2: So much blood... and all the wrong type.
strings.refugees_s15_2_buck_3: I wonder who this blood belonged to? I hope he followed a healthy lifestyle.
strings.refugees_s15_2_dr_1: Thanks. That will help me through one more day.
strings.refugees_s15_2_dr_2: Corpse blood again. It tastes like marsh mud. Though it's better than nothing.
strings.refugees_s15_2_dr_3: Oh, how I miss regular food! I'd even be willing to eat celery.
strings.refugees_s15_2_dr_4: It makes us alike. We live off death — you, me... and the worms.
strings.refugees_s15_3: And your beard is so... so long, so attractive. It calls out for me to touch it — to immerse my fingers in it...
strings.refugees_s15_3_1: Look at this. I took it from the <corpse of the vampire>.
strings.refugees_s15_3_10: The Town's duties have increased, and the harvest hasn't been good to us these past few years...
strings.refugees_s15_3_14: It's a sad day when even heroes can't show compassion for the common villager!
strings.refugees_s15_3_2: You did it! Amazing! You have helped us enormously! Oh, thank you, thank you!
strings.refugees_s15_3_3: All our Village is grateful to you, our hero! What you have done here today will not be forgotten.
strings.refugees_s15_3_7: Reward? Oh, sorry, I entirely forgot!
strings.refugees_s15_3_8: I must warn you, that the economic situation in our Village is not the best...
strings.refugees_s15_4: Well... Er... Thanks. It's unusual to hear such words coming from an inquisitor.
strings.refugees_s15_4_1: Marquis, I'd like to borrow something from you. The Witcher's Eye.
strings.refugees_s15_4_2: Alaric told you about that, did he? I shouldn't have trusted my secrets to that old scoundrel.
strings.refugees_s15_4_3: Yes. I have it. But it is a precious thing to me.
strings.refugees_s15_4_4: It's a minor technical wonder, my father's masterpiece. And it's the only one of its kind.
strings.refugees_s15_4_5: I'll be careful. And I'll bring it back really soon.
strings.refugees_s15_4_6: Hm... No. But I know what my father would have done in this situation.
strings.refugees_s15_4_7: If you <accomplish your task> — if you help all these people survive...
strings.refugees_s15_4_8: Then I shall give the Witcher's Eye to you. As a gift.
strings.refugees_s15_5: Does it surprise you that a beautiful and intelligent woman can be an inquisitor?
strings.refugees_s15_6: See for yourself, my dear: not all female inquisitors are lonely, bitter, ugly old hens.
strings.refugees_s15_7: Her voice is hypnotic, and her eyes. It's... I feel naked. It's awful.
strings.refugees_s15_8: May I know your name, and the purpose of your visit?
strings.refugees_s15_9: Oh, I adore direct men. <Lady Beatrice>. And I am looking for someone.
strings.refugees_s16_past_1: They were playing dice right here.
strings.refugees_s16_past_10: There! <Four vampires> attacked them right here. Some sort of magic turned them into jawbones...
strings.refugees_s16_past_11: And... bingo! <One of those jaws> — it's still here in the ground!
strings.refugees_s16_past_12: It looks like that's it. But I can't stop thinking about naked raven-haired women riding unicorns!
strings.refugees_s16_past_13: I think the <witch Clotho> could disenchant this jawbone for me.
strings.refugees_s16_past_2: Keeper was cheating, and Astrologer lost his shirt... then his pants... and his underwear...
strings.refugees_s16_past_3: They lit a fire and fried a fish. Hm, I've never heard of poisonous fish around here...
strings.refugees_s16_past_4: Then Keeper tried to catch a moth — I could see myself doing that! But he caught a huge hornet. Uh oh!
strings.refugees_s16_past_5: Then Keeper made a cocktail, mixing four types of alcohol in one flask... Oh my God!
strings.refugees_s16_past_6: There's Keeper and Astrologer daring each other to drink their hellish cocktail.
strings.refugees_s16_past_7: Here they're singing serenades and embracing each other.
strings.refugees_s16_past_8: That's where Astrologer vomited. Twice. Eww!
strings.refugees_s16_past_9: Then Keeper knocked the flask over, then fell over himself... and... wait!
strings.refugees_s16_think_1: Hm, it looks like just the place.
strings.refugees_s16_think_2: They were here. The <young Astrologer> and the <fourth Keeper>.
strings.refugees_s16_think_3: The <Eye> is trembling... Why am I thinking about unicorns?
strings.refugees_s17_1: Clotho, I have a jaw. I'd like you to turn it into a vampire.
strings.refugees_s17_10: He told me it's unstable, unreliable, and has several side effects...
strings.refugees_s17_11: If there's any hope it'll work, it's worth trying.
strings.refugees_s17_12: Oh, one more thing. If you meet that lovely woman who purchased a recipe for <Emulsion Of Death>...
strings.refugees_s17_13: Please, remind her that she has forgot to take her change.
strings.refugees_s17_15: By the way, you'll need some <Memory powder> for preparing the Tincture. Here's a pinch.
strings.refugees_s17_16: If you need any more, you're welcome to it. It's 20 years past its expiration date.
strings.refugees_s17_2: Why certainly, sweety. Open your mouth...
strings.refugees_s17_3: Stop! I meant this other jaw. It's an enchanted vampire and I need you to disenchant it.
strings.refugees_s17_4: Oh, that's even easier! Let me see... Hmm... Interesting!
strings.refugees_s17_5: <Its aura> is so bright... I'm afraid I can't dispel such powerful magic, my boy. I'm sorry.
strings.refugees_s17_6: Argh! I was really counting on you! Are you sure there's nothing we can do here?
strings.refugees_s17_7: Hm.. Well, of course, you could always try one thing... A <Memory tincture>.
strings.refugees_s17_9: I must warn you. One of your predecessors, the <third Keeper>, used Memory tincture several times.
strings.refugees_s18_1: And now... "Spray it into both eyes". Jesus!
strings.refugees_s18_10: We've tried everything, mistress, but Alaric is incredibly resistant!
strings.refugees_s18_11: Pain, cold, hunger, thirst — nothing works!
strings.refugees_s18_13: You mean we should... turn him? But... it's an awful sin. And...
strings.refugees_s18_15: Oh no! My eyes! ... It's like I've been staring at the sun for a whole hour!
strings.refugees_s18_16: But I've learned something new. I must learn more about <that woman>.
strings.refugees_s18_17: They mentioned the Order of Undead Hunters. So maybe <Shepherd> knows about her.
strings.refugees_s18_18: And, of course, <Alaric> might remember something.
strings.refugees_s18_19: It's too dangerous to use the tincture in the Dungeon
strings.refugees_s18_1f: Nothing. Well, Clotho warned me. Let's try one more time. Damned tincture!
strings.refugees_s18_2: A-A-A! My eyes! It's worse than Shepherd's garlic! A-A-A!
strings.refugees_s18_20: I have nothing to apply the tincture on
strings.refugees_s18_3s: Nothing again... Wait! What the hell is happening?!
strings.refugees_s18_4: You're late. Do you require another lesson in respect, you miserable worms?
strings.refugees_s18_5: It's not our fault, mistress. The Town is much less friendly to vampires these days.
strings.refugees_s18_6: The <Order of Undead Hunters> patrols the night streets. With nets to catch bats!
strings.refugees_s18_7: Yeah! It's a blessing we managed to make it here at all!
strings.refugees_s18_8: You useless nobodies! Your endless silly excuses — that's all I ever get from you!
strings.refugees_s18_9: Have you wrung anything more from <that priest>?!
strings.refugees_s19_1_1: I have some new information, master Alaric. About the vampires who kidnapped you.
strings.refugees_s19_1_10: The thing is... when <Lady Beatrice> visited me, she... It doesn't matter.
strings.refugees_s19_1_11: Who else might know about this "Vampire Queen"? Who is so comfortable dealing with the undead?
strings.refugees_s19_1_2: There was a woman who ordered them to do it. And to turn you into a vampire.
strings.refugees_s19_1_3: A <woman in a black and gold cloak>. Have you ever heard anything about her?
strings.refugees_s19_1_5: I would have remembered if the kidnappers mentioned her. But they didn't.
strings.refugees_s19_1_6: They mentioned ghouls a lot. They said they'd feed me to them if I kept quiet.
strings.refugees_s19_1_7: How foolish! Every adult knows that ghouls don't exist!
strings.refugees_s19_1_8: I think that woman might be the key to our mystery.
strings.refugees_s19_1_9: Sorry I can't help you. But... listen, why do you smell so strange?
strings.refugees_s19_3_1: Don't leave your home without weapon, Keeper! These days we must be on the lookout. Evil is everywhere!
strings.refugees_s19_3_2: No kidding. Tell me, what do you know about a <woman in a black and gold cloak>?
strings.refugees_s19_3_3: Is she a werewolf? An evil spirit? A rider with burning skull instead of his head?
strings.refugees_s19_3_4: She might be a <vampire> but I'm not sure.
strings.refugees_s19_3_5: Then let's go kill her, dissect her, and find out!
strings.refugees_s19_3_6: Well, she was around 30 years ago, but who knows where is she now, or if she's even alive!
strings.refugees_s19_3_7: A black and gold cloak you say? Hmm. I remember <one fresco>...
strings.refugees_s19_3_8: I always admired it when I visited the Town Cathedral as a child. It was called <"Master vs Vampire Queen">
strings.refugees_s19_3_9: And that Queen wore a <cloak> like the one you mentioned.
strings.refugees_s1_1: Holey Smokes! Who are you? A thief?
strings.refugees_s1_10: But we are not heretics. This is just someone's vile slander!
strings.refugees_s1_12: Alas, not everyone managed to get out of Town. Those who survived set a <camp> nearby.
strings.refugees_s1_13: I'm forced to come to you, Keeper: we desperately need your help...
strings.refugees_s1_15: I know that look... Yes, we're ready to pay you.
strings.refugees_s1_16: Money makes the world go round. Show me your camp and let's talk details.
strings.refugees_s1_2: Sorry for the intrusion. And no, I'm not a thief.
strings.refugees_s1_3: Hm... but... are you sure you're not a thief? Have you ever been in prison?
strings.refugees_s1_4: Yes, we escaped from <prison> three days ago.
strings.refugees_s1_5: Wow! A real repeat offender! Cool!
strings.refugees_s1_6: Dear Keeper, I couldn't possibly be a thief. I'm a marquis!
strings.refugees_s1_7: Well... I've heard of contract killers nicknamed Baron, Viscount, and Countess.
strings.refugees_s1_9: I, the <Marquis Teodoro Jr.>, along with my friends, were sentenced by the Inquisition to the fire.
strings.refugees_s20_1: Gerry, have you ever met a <woman in a black and gold cloak>?
strings.refugees_s20_10: By the way, what's with the new smell? — Is it <cloves>? It's disgusting!
strings.refugees_s20_2: That's a pretty funny question to ask a guy with amnesia!
strings.refugees_s20_3: Partial amnesia. So have you heard anything about the <Vampire Queen>?
strings.refugees_s20_4: Sure, I've heard some things. In fact, that was the Lighthouse Keeper's ex-wife's nickname, when they played private games at home...
strings.refugees_s20_5: Gerry, please, stop making jokes! This is serious.
strings.refugees_s20_6: You are talking to the wrong guy.
strings.refugees_s20_7: There are only two reliable sources of hard facts: Town housewives... and <ghosts>.
strings.refugees_s20_9: Then come back tomorrow, and meanwhile I'll chat up the <local ghosts>. But I'll have you know, this is skull exploitation!
strings.refugees_s21_10: Hmm. So how do I get this amulet?
strings.refugees_s21_11: Well... You can make one. Out of human intestines, some wax... and... oh yeah, the hair of a donkey-communist!
strings.refugees_s21_12: Yes, yes. Just don't ask why!
strings.refugees_s21_2: Of course! One ghost named William visited a couple of students, and told them that their uncles killed their fathers!
strings.refugees_s21_3: Yeah, that's incredibly important. Is that it?
strings.refugees_s21_4: Almost. About the black and gold cloak. They remembered one <ghost-weirdo from the Dungeon>...
strings.refugees_s21_5: He came around only once — back before the Great Blast. He was search for the <same woman>.
strings.refugees_s21_6: She had taken <his leg> and wouldn't give it back.
strings.refugees_s21_7: That's better than nothing. So where can I find this "weirdo"?
strings.refugees_s21_8: He had a lisp, so he must be from the <eighth floor>. Don't ask why. And...
strings.refugees_s21_9: And if you want him to appear... you'll need a <special amulet>.
strings.refugees_s22_10: That's a fine thought, my good comrade. I only wish everyone were as determined as you!
strings.refugees_s22_11: Here, let me do it myself. It'll be an honorable pain!
strings.refugees_s22_11_old: Here, let me do it myself. It'll be an honorable pain!
strings.refugees_s22_13: That's a fine thought, my good comrade.  But alas, you've yet to earn such a great honor!
strings.refugees_s22_14: Spend your sweat to benefit our movement, and one day I'll reconsider.
strings.refugees_s22_2: Listen, this will sound a little unexpected, but I'd like to purchase some of your... hmm... a <piece of your hair>.
strings.refugees_s22_2_old: Listen, this will sound a little unexpected, but I'd like to purchase some of your... hmm... a <piece of your hair>.
strings.refugees_s22_4: I knew it. I suspected that your rehabilitation was no more than a vile ruse.
strings.refugees_s22_5: The damned capitalist can't again resist the temptation to shear an honest worker!
strings.refugees_s22_5_old: The damned capitalist can't again resist the temptation to shear an honest worker!
strings.refugees_s22_6: Do you know what you are? You're a public enemy! Shame on you! Shame! Shame!
strings.refugees_s22_6_old: Do you know what you are? You're a public enemy! Shame on you! Shame! Shame!
strings.refugees_s22_7: Don't spit at me, please. You've got me totally wrong. I was asking you to honor me!
strings.refugees_s22_7_old: Don't spit at me, please. You've got me totally wrong. I was asking you to honor me!
strings.refugees_s22_8: I'll put your hair in a frame and hang it over my bed, to inspire me to fight for my rights!
strings.refugees_s22_8_old: I'll put your hair in a frame and hang it over my bed, to inspire me to fight for my rights!
strings.refugees_s23_1: Not that it bothers me, uninvited guest, but what made you bring this... er... thing here?
strings.refugees_s23_10: Like anyone with two legs. And in case you didn't hear me: I don't care.
strings.refugees_s23_11: What a weirdo! But I know another <one-leg fellow> who could help...
strings.refugees_s23_2: Hello! Oh, you mean <the amulet>? Well, it's for attracting spirits. And...
strings.refugees_s23_3: Amulet? Not that it matters, but all I see is just a disgusting mix of wax, hair, and human flesh.
strings.refugees_s23_4: If I were still alive, I might be laughing right now, but emotions are foreign to me.
strings.refugees_s23_5: Hmm... Well, let's change the subject. I need a bit of help.
strings.refugees_s23_6: Assisting anyone would contradict my philosophy of progressive ignoring.
strings.refugees_s23_7: In short: <I care for nothing and despite everything>.
strings.refugees_s23_8: I could find <your leg> and bring it back, if you help me.
strings.refugees_s23_9: I don't believe you. You cannot imagine my absent but painful sufferings.
strings.refugees_s24_1_1: I need some help. It's related to the <Vampire Queen> you told me about. And...
strings.refugees_s24_1_2: Has evil already drawn so close? I see. Rose! Rose!!
strings.refugees_s24_1_4: Time for battle, my love! My final battle, perhaps! Prepare my equipment. And pray for me.
strings.refugees_s24_1_6: Oh, dear! Does it mean you'll be late for dinner?
strings.refugees_s24_1_7: It means I may fall in battle. Today's enemy is greater by far than any I've faced before!
strings.refugees_s24_1_8: Oh, no! Don't leave me! What will I do all alone? And what will the neighbors say?!
strings.refugees_s24_1_9: It is my holy duty, my love! Let's go, Keeper — let's die like heroes!
strings.refugees_s24_2_2: It's hard to argue with that. But which specific case do you mean?
strings.refugees_s24_2_3: <The amulet of spirit summoning>. The spirit laughed at me!
strings.refugees_s24_2_4: What amulet? I don't... wait... you mean to say... oh my... Keeper, come on!
strings.refugees_s24_2_5: You really believed that rubbish? No, you're kidding me!
strings.refugees_s24_2_6: It's you who was making fun of me! I was awfully embarrassed by that spirit!
strings.refugees_s24_2_7: Wait a minute! He appeared, didn't he? So the amulet must have worked!
strings.refugees_s24_2_8: He appeared to laugh at how absurd I looked!
strings.refugees_s24_2_9: He appeared! So I won't hear any of your complaints!
strings.refugees_s25_1: Stay behind me! She could strike at any moment!
strings.refugees_s25_10: He's joking, forget it! His leg, along with his hand and his eye were taken by an unknown lady.
strings.refugees_s25_12: So he totally understands your absent but painful sufferings. Now help us!
strings.refugees_s25_13: Tell me everything you know about the <woman who took your leg>.
strings.refugees_s25_14: She was very proud and overbearing. Her voice was like thunder.
strings.refugees_s25_15: She used archaic words. I haven't heard living people talk like that for hundreds of years.
strings.refugees_s25_16: And she said that I can always get my leg back, from a place called <Misty Quagmire>.
strings.refugees_s25_17: Please, recover my leg from that place! — I beg you!
strings.refugees_s25_19: Though, as I've said before, I really don't care.
strings.refugees_s25_2: Listen, I'll explain it to you a third time:
strings.refugees_s25_20: I don't know where this <Misty Quagmire> is, but I've heard about it.
strings.refugees_s25_21: About 25 years ago, a famous university scientist, <Marquis Teodoro Sr>, found a book there.
strings.refugees_s25_22: Could that be the father of Marquis Teodoro Jr.?
strings.refugees_s25_23: It was an evil book, full of dark magic. They called it the <Necronomicon>.
strings.refugees_s25_24: The marquis studied it in secret, and eventually, the book drove him and his wife crazy.
strings.refugees_s25_25: I was in Execution Square the day that the inquisitors brought them to the fire.
strings.refugees_s25_26: They roared like wild animals, tried to bite their captors, and shouted things about the <Ancient Curse>...
strings.refugees_s25_29: My intuition tells me there's no Vampire Queen here. Therefore: she must be on another floor!
strings.refugees_s25_3: He's just a <harmless ghost>, and we just need to convince him to help!
strings.refugees_s25_30: Sad story... But it contained a clue: <Marquis Teodoro> might know where this Quagmire is.
strings.refugees_s25_31: Or, I could ask <Clotho>. She's been living in the Swamps for many years.
strings.refugees_s25_4: True evil often comes in harmless forms! And loves to divert your attention...
strings.refugees_s25_5: How many people are visiting me these days! Even though I don't desire visitors at all.
strings.refugees_s25_6: Look here. Shepherd is a one-legged guy. Can you trust us now?
strings.refugees_s25_7: It depends on how he lost his leg.
strings.refugees_s25_8: Well, I and several other brave guys from <our Order> were hunting two spirits...
strings.refugees_s26_1_1: Marquis, this may not be the most pleasant topic for you, but...
strings.refugees_s26_1_10: All hope dies in that place. The Quagmire fills you with pain, horror, and despair.
strings.refugees_s26_1_11: And even if you leave the Quagmire forever, it will find you in your nightmares.
strings.refugees_s26_1_12: Sounds sinister. Well then just show me the road and you can stay here. You have every right to be... scared.
strings.refugees_s26_1_13: Scared? Ha! I can't afford to be scared or weak. I'm the leader of these people.
strings.refugees_s26_1_14: Of course! How can you help them to overcome their fears if you can't deal with your own?
strings.refugees_s26_1_15: Indeed. After all, our family has always had courage. And liver problems...
strings.refugees_s26_1_17: Wait! I should take the <Witcher's Eye> with me. I'll be back soon.
strings.refugees_s26_1_2: I'd like you to show me the path to <Misty Quagmire>.
strings.refugees_s26_1_3: Marquis, are you ready to talk to me about <Misty Quagmire>?
strings.refugees_s26_1_5: Do you even know anything about that place, Graveyard Keeper?
strings.refugees_s26_1_6: A little. It's the place where your father found the <Necronomicon>.
strings.refugees_s26_1_7: He studied it. And the consequences were awful.
strings.refugees_s26_1_8: I even can't imagine what you've been through.
strings.refugees_s26_1_9: I went there once. And I swore I'd never return again.
strings.refugees_s26_1_ready_1: Good! It's time to face our fears.
strings.refugees_s2_1: Our servants secretly delivered us some items and food for the first days.
strings.refugees_s2_10: Which means: if you tell anyone about us, we'll all die by torture.
strings.refugees_s2_12: And the more thing... One of my... mmm... friends desired to meet you very much.
strings.refugees_s2_13: <Master Alaric>. The former inquisitor who helped us escape.
strings.refugees_s2_2: But we need much more to survive. And we have nowhere to go.
strings.refugees_s2_3: Then why don't you hunt, gather mushrooms and berries, grow vegetables?
strings.refugees_s2_4: You're right. But understand our situation, please.
strings.refugees_s2_5: We all belonged to the <aristocracy>. We have neither experience nor skills for living in... such conditions.
strings.refugees_s2_6: We know philosophy, etiquette, rhetoric. Can that help us with food and drink?
strings.refugees_s2_7: On the other hand, please rest assured — we have more than enough to pay you for your services.
strings.refugees_s2_8: <Food and drink>? That doesn't sound complicated. Okay. Get the money ready.
strings.refugees_s2_9: Great! There's just one more thing you should know: the <Inquisition> is looking for us.
strings.refugees_s3_1: Graveyard Keeper! What an honor to meet you!
strings.refugees_s3_11: What did <Ancient God> tell you when he brought you here?
strings.refugees_s3_13: He's looking straight through me. It makes me feel uncomfortable.
strings.refugees_s3_14: MMM... I HAVE NO IDEA WHAT YOU'RE TALKING ABOUT.
strings.refugees_s3_15: I BURY CORPSES, CONDUCT SERMONS... trade human flesh... . THAT'S ALL.
strings.refugees_s3_16: Don't lie to me, Keeper. I know more than you can possibly imagine!
strings.refugees_s3_17: THEN WHAT'S THE POINT OF INTERROGATING ME, MASTER ALARIC?
strings.refugees_s3_18: I see. Forget my questions. Please, just leave me in peace.
strings.refugees_s3_19: NO PROBLEM. HAVE A GOOD DAY, MASTER ALARIC. This guy sure could use a hearing aid.
strings.refugees_s3_2: It's a pleasure for me too, but...
strings.refugees_s3_3: Speak louder. His hearing is quite poor.
strings.refugees_s3_4: But I haven't done anything yet to...
strings.refugees_s3_7: You do and you will do. Teodoro, could you let us talk privately?
strings.refugees_s3_8: OF COURSE, MASTER ALARIC... YOUR GRIM SECRETS, THANK GOD, ARE NOT MY BUSINESS!
strings.refugees_s3_9: And now... what do you know of the role you've been chosen to play?
strings.refugees_s4_1_1: What a fine place! Let's make a trade: my smithy for your house, the Church, and the graveyard.
strings.refugees_s4_1_11: There are <vampires in the Village>, Keeper. And we expect the first fatalities are just around the corner.
strings.refugees_s4_1_12: Horadric has requested a specialist in the dead. Now go!
strings.refugees_s4_1_2: That's an incredibly generous offer, <Krezvold>, but I'm afraid...
strings.refugees_s4_1_3: Ha ha! He thought I was being serious!
strings.refugees_s4_1_4: I'm not such a complete idiot that I'd want to live and work in this dump. Yuck!
strings.refugees_s4_1_5: Ehm... You're so polite. Almost like <Farmer>.  Are you brothers by any chance?
strings.refugees_s4_1_6: Heh heh. I'll tell you a secret: I was the smith before his ancestors even moved here.
strings.refugees_s4_1_9: There's an emergency in the Village. Horadric is gathering all the villagers in his <Tavern>.
strings.refugees_s4_2_1: Don't pay him any heed. Alaric is just a selfish and cruel old man.
strings.refugees_s4_2_3: But you said he rescued you, marquis. Isn't that a reason to be... grateful?
strings.refugees_s4_2_4: Perhaps. But there are many more reasons not to be grateful.
strings.refugees_s4_2_a_0: I have nothing to say to you, Keeper.
strings.refugees_s4_2_a_1: When I close my eyes, I see my brothers. Oh, how I miss them... despite everything.
strings.refugees_s4_2_a_2: I do what I must. But every day this burden grows heavier.
strings.refugees_s4_2_a_3: Don't hold out for gratitude. Just be glad that they're not throwing stones at you.
strings.refugees_s4_2_coo: It's like being in chains! I'm down to my last twelve types of relish. — I can't bear it!
strings.refugees_s4_2_cs_1: Hey! I know you! You're the one who trashed my store!
strings.refugees_s4_2_cs_2: You punched my sales clerk in the nose!
strings.refugees_s4_2_cs_3: And then — you called me a rabid hamster!
strings.refugees_s4_2_cs_4: Sorry, but I have no idea what...
strings.refugees_s4_2_cs_5: How did you escape from the Town prison?
strings.refugees_s4_2_cs_6: You've got me mixed up with someone else. I've never even been to Town.
strings.refugees_s4_2_cs_7: Come on! I'd know that silly beard anywhere!
strings.refugees_s4_2_g1: I still can't believe it. We were high society! Why did the King not protect us?
strings.refugees_s4_2_g2: My servants brought me my collection of toothpicks. Nice! What did you get?
strings.refugees_s4_2_g3: The Inquisition took everything! The greedy bastards! May they choke on my workshops!
strings.refugees_s4_2_g4: My mansion... my diamonds... my housekeeper Jackeline with all her exotic fantasies...
strings.refugees_s4_2_g5: People, stop being so depressing. It's boring. Besides — look at this magnificent scenery!
strings.refugees_s4_2_t_1: People live like slaves and don't even notice. How could this happen?
strings.refugees_s4_2_t_2: One day we'll return. And they'll pay for their crimes.
strings.refugees_s4_2_t_3: No time for regrets! To survive, we must look to the future.
strings.refugees_s4_2_t_4: Our minds are free, my friends. We've left the shackles and prison cells behind!
strings.refugees_s4_2_tan: I had a 50% discount for inquisitors. Damn them, they don't even deserve 10%!
strings.refugees_s4_2_und: Why are men so weak? Most can't even survive a week with me!
strings.refugees_s5_10: One week only! "Cory and Brother" will be available to fix your porch...
strings.refugees_s5_11: For a 15% discount! And as a free gift, you'll get a special wooden platypus from <Tress>!
strings.refugees_s5_13_1: Ehm... okay. <Adam>, let's hear your suggestion!
strings.refugees_s5_14: My suggestion is to assign two bodyguards to each villager.
strings.refugees_s5_15: A week ago a band of ghouls wrote some offensive slander on my wall!
strings.refugees_s5_17: Adam, it was the village teenagers. I even helped them a bit. With the grammar.
strings.refugees_s5_19: My suggestion is for everyone to stop eating dead animals!
strings.refugees_s5_2: We're late. Remember: it's your fault!
strings.refugees_s5_20: It's only natural that you'd end up seeing vampires and other nonsense!
strings.refugees_s5_21: Fresh roots and braised leaves — the secrets to a healthy body and spirit!
strings.refugees_s5_22: What?! To turn down candied chicken leg marinade? Never!
strings.refugees_s5_22_1: <Beekeeper>, please don't spit on the floor. Is there something you'd like to add?
strings.refugees_s5_23: Yes there is! You people — are you crazy?! You're all full of rubbish!
strings.refugees_s5_24: It's all becoming clear. It's the vile doings of my sworn enemy — <Hornetman>!
strings.refugees_s5_25: But fear not! My army of carnivorous bees is nearly ready!
strings.refugees_s5_26: Soon, very soon, I will release them upon the Village!
strings.refugees_s5_27: That... would be most kind of you, Beekeeper. Are there any other suggestions?
strings.refugees_s5_28: Great! The meeting is adjourned. You are all free to go.
strings.refugees_s5_29: Keeper, could you spare a moment?
strings.refugees_s5_3: Rose, thank you. We all feel your pain. We all know your suffering...
strings.refugees_s5_30: Listen... Might I ask you to look into <all that stuff>?
strings.refugees_s5_31: It's pretty unexpected... But I appreciate that you confide in me.
strings.refugees_s5_32: Frankly speaking, I wouldn't exactly say that I confide you.
strings.refugees_s5_33: But if I asked some villager, I'd have to give them a huge tax write off, in addition to their reward.
strings.refugees_s5_34: So it only makes sense to ask someone outside the Village, wouldn't you say?
strings.refugees_s5_36: On the other hand, you're such a kind and understanding guy...
strings.refugees_s5_37: Perhaps you'd agree to help us... for free?
strings.refugees_s5_37a: I agree to help. <For the fee>.
strings.refugees_s5_37a_1: Pff, I'd hoped for a little compassion in the time of our misfortune. But very well!
strings.refugees_s5_37a_2: What a greedy rascal! Very well, let's go home and think a bit.
strings.refugees_s5_37b: I'll think about it. We'll talk later.
strings.refugees_s5_37b_1: Very well. I do hope you make the right decision. The selfless choice.
strings.refugees_s5_37c: I'm too busy to deal with this.
strings.refugees_s5_37c_1: Well... If you change your mind, your reward is waiting for you.
strings.refugees_s5_37c_2: I want to go home and forget all this nonsense.
strings.refugees_s5_5: That was the third and final of the <vampire's victims>. For today.
strings.refugees_s5_6: But any one of us could be the next... to meet him.
strings.refugees_s5_7: <Chain>, the <Farmer's son>, <Rose> — it's only just beginning!
strings.refugees_s5_8_1: Not all at once now, please! <Cory>, your suggestion first!
strings.refugees_s5_9: My suggestion? Ah, yes of course! People, hear my words.
strings.refugees_s6_1: It's time to pay for your crimes, you foul creature!
strings.refugees_s6_12: Aha! He refuses! The fiend gives himself away!
strings.refugees_s6_16: Like my old teacher from the <Order of Undead Hunters> used to say...
strings.refugees_s6_20: However, if you are a mutant, you might be resistant to the garlic...
strings.refugees_s6_21: Eureka! I know what we must do!
strings.refugees_s6_22: Take this wooden stake, and plunge it deep into your heart! If you die...
strings.refugees_s6_23: Stop! I have a better idea. I'll find you an <actual vampire>, and then you can cut me a break.
strings.refugees_s6_25: Then you can kill me, or I'll eat a whole bucket of garlic, or whatever you need.
strings.refugees_s6_26: It's a deal. But don't you try to cheat me, you bearded horror!
strings.refugees_s6_28: I guess it would make sense to talk to the victims — <Chain>, <Farmer's son>, and <Rose>.
strings.refugees_s6_4: To you, you vile vampire! Prepare to die! In the name of <my wife>, and all the other innocents!
strings.refugees_s6_5: Hey, that's kinda funny! You really think I go around at night sucking people's blood?
strings.refugees_s6_6: How come I'm always out in the sun working?
strings.refugees_s6_7: That proves nothing! You could be a vampire-mutant!
strings.refugees_s6_9: There's only one way to check!
strings.refugees_s7_1_1: Chain, could you tell me a bit about that vampire?
strings.refugees_s7_1_2: No, I couldn't! I won't say another word until <Horadric> apologizes for his disgusting behavior!
strings.refugees_s7_1_explanations_3: Go ask him why he was returning home after midnight that day!
strings.refugees_s7_1_explanations_5: Listen, I'm sorry about your family troubles but... do you have anything useful to tell me?
strings.refugees_s7_1_explanations_6: I don't know anything. I was asleep.
strings.refugees_s7_1_explanations_7: Very well then. Have a good day!
strings.refugees_s7_1_explanations_8: Wait! The <Astrologer> knows a thing or two about vampires.
strings.refugees_s7_1_explanations_9: He says he was once <attacked by vampires>. About 30 years ago.
strings.refugees_s7_1_sorry_1: Horadric, <Chain> asked you to say sorry for your...
strings.refugees_s7_1_sorry_3: I found my wife's lover in my own bedroom, and it's me who has to say he's sorry?!
strings.refugees_s7_1_sorry_4: Just picture it — he looked right at me, and then jumped through the window,
strings.refugees_s7_1_sorry_5: And now she's insisting that she was merely sleeping, and this fellow was a <common vampire>!
strings.refugees_s7_1_sorry_7: Go to her, and inform her that I demand an explanation!
strings.refugees_s7_2_1: I have some questions for you, child.
strings.refugees_s7_2_10: He... just went away. Please! Don't laugh! Everyone laughs at that part!
strings.refugees_s7_2_11: Don't worry. At 15 years old, I'd have been scared too.
strings.refugees_s7_2_2: About the <vampire>? Do you promise you won't laugh?
strings.refugees_s7_2_3: My father. My uncle. All the neighbors. None of them believe me and just laugh!
strings.refugees_s7_2_5: That night, my father and uncle Miller were drinking uncle's wheat whiskey...
strings.refugees_s7_2_6: I was home alone. And <some man> came through the window.
strings.refugees_s7_2_7: At first, I thought it was my drunk father. I even called out to him — 'Dad'. But he... it was like he didn't hear me.
strings.refugees_s7_2_9: In a flash, I knew it wasn't Dad, and I hid under my blanket! And he... he...
strings.refugees_s7_3_1: Rose, that vampire who attacked you. May I...
strings.refugees_s7_3_10: It was like he was disgusted! And you know what? It was even a little insulting! If my husband had been home...
strings.refugees_s7_3_12: He said: "B again?! <Group B>! It's just like you're all mocking me!" And then he ran away.
strings.refugees_s7_3_13: Thank you for your help. I hope... er... your cows have lots of nice calves.
strings.refugees_s7_3_4: Oh... I'm sorry to hear that, but please... a bit less loud...
strings.refugees_s7_3_5: Was it gripping and sinister? I practiced that line for hours!
strings.refugees_s7_3_7: So could you tell me what happened?
strings.refugees_s7_3_8: He lured me to the barn, by imitating the sounds of a pregnant cow...
strings.refugees_s7_3_9: Then he grabbed me, and started drinking my blood. But almost right away he just <spat it out>.
strings.refugees_s8_1: Well, my childhood dream has come true. I'm a detective... just like Sherlock Holmes...
strings.refugees_s8_2: So let's apply the deductive method. Or inductive? Doesn't matter.
strings.refugees_s8_3: Horadric <didn't recognize> the guy. Neither did Rose. And what's more...
strings.refugees_s8_4: Farmer's son called out to him, but the individual <didn't hear him>...
strings.refugees_s8_5: So... He isn't a <regular villager>, and he has <hearing problems>...
strings.refugees_s8_8: I need to talk to <master Alaric>! And the <marquis>.
strings.refugees_s9_1_1: Marquis, do you know anything about <vampires>?
strings.refugees_s9_1_2: One of them is terrorizing the Village. And I suspect that it might be...
strings.refugees_s9_1_3: One of us? Impossible. I know all of these people quite well.
strings.refugees_s9_1_4: When you share a cell, it makes you especially close...
strings.refugees_s9_1_6: Alaric? I... I don't think so. But... I couldn't guarantee it...
strings.refugees_s9_2_1: Master Alaric, the nearby village is greatly alarmed at the thought of vampires.
strings.refugees_s9_2_10: Ah yes, vampires! Vampires? Don't talk rubbish!
strings.refugees_s9_2_11: I'd rather believe in the fluffy yellow rabbit that calls down the lightning! Vampires! Pff!
strings.refugees_s9_2_13: BUT THE VILLAGERS SAW THEM... WITNESSES, VICTIMS...
strings.refugees_s9_2_14: I don't merely doubt they exist. I'm absolutely sure of it!
strings.refugees_s9_2_15: The joke is on you, my poor boy. Isn't it obvious?
strings.refugees_s9_2_17: Please don't bother me anymore over such nonsense, all right?
strings.refugees_s9_2_18: He's so confident, it's easy to believe him. But...
strings.refugees_s9_2_19: He forgot to cover the <green sore on his wrist>.
strings.refugees_s9_2_20: Astrologer said that's a sign of a <vampire on a bad diet>!
strings.refugees_s9_2_21: I'll stake out the tent at night, and <keep an eye> on Alaric.
strings.refugees_s9_2_3: MASTER ALARIC, I SAID, THE CLOSEST VILLAGE...
strings.refugees_s9_2_5: NO, NOT PILLAGE! THE CLOSEST VILLAGE! THEY ARE CONCERNED...
strings.refugees_s9_2_6: Burned?! But who did it? And why?
strings.refugees_s9_2_7: OKAY. THE VILLAGERS ARE IN A RAGE OVER VAMPIRES!
strings.refugees_s_ev_7_1_1_1: You know, Horadric's wife mentioned that you once had an encounter with some vampires.
strings.refugees_s_ev_7_1_1_2: Vampires? Hmm. That was a long time ago... even before the <Great Blast>.
strings.refugees_s_ev_7_1_1_3: Yes... it was in the glade to the right of the waterfall. <My friend Keeper> was with me.
strings.refugees_s_ev_7_1_1_4: We were having a picnic, as I recall. And then <four guys with fangs> suddenly showed up, and assaulted the Keeper.
strings.refugees_s_ev_7_1_1_5: But some strange magic protected him, and they all turned into <vampire jaws>!
strings.refugees_s_ev_7_1_1_6: Amazing. Do you know anything else about vampires?
strings.refugees_s_ev_7_1_1_7: Well... for instance, I've read that vampire-alchemists have discovered <4 groups of blood>...
strings.refugees_s_ev_7_1_1_8: More interesting — vampires only drink <Group O>. The other groups give them cavities in their fangs... ulcers...
strings.refugees_s_ev_7_1_1_9: ... green eruptions on the skin... decades-long paralysis, and other nuisances.
strings.remove_grpart_confirm: Are you sure you want to remove this part of the grave?

strings.rosa_intro_2: Do you have any fresh beef?
strings.rosa_intro_3: Oh, no sir. The cows are our friends!

strings.skull_3_12: So shut the sard up! And do what I tell you!

strings.skull_6_15: Sard you smartass! I'll be waiting for that beer at my place! No beer — no answers...

strings.skull_6_4: And everybody is ok with me just appearing out of nowhere.
strings.skull_6_6: Stealing... I remember there's a <Cellar> in your cottage! Some provisions must be stored there!

strings.skull_7_2: Oh sard he'll kill me — or even worse.

strings.skull_8_2b_1b_4: Net, net... I used to like fishing! I remember fishing...

strings.skull_8_2b_1b_8: You know what? I need to go.

strings.snake_aple_1: What's my final task going to be?
